LaPorta caught three of four targets for 44 yards against the Jets in Week 3, which was his quietest game of the year. Detroit's ability to score and defensive problems keep the passing game alive even when running back Jahmyr Gibbs is tearing it up on the ground, so there don't look to be any issues with LaPorta's usage moving forward. He'll face a Carolina defense that ceded a 7-51-2 stat line to Harold Fannin in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Sam LaPorta will look to build on a season-best showing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. LaPorta impressed even in a Week 4 loss to Carolina, reeling in eight of 13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown. The fourth-year tight end has now registered a 22-228-2  receiving line this season, and he remains a consistent option for Jared Goff, especially in important situations. LaPorta will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Sam LaPorta will aim to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. LaPorta recorded another statement performance in Week 5 over the Cardinals heading into Detroit's bye, bringing in all five of his targets for 88 yards and a touchdown. The featured tight end has now surpassed 50 yards in three of his last four games, and he's found the end zone in each of those outings as well. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: LaPorta has settled in as one of the league's top tight ends, but the 2023 second-round pick simply hasn't been able to match the fantasy success he enjoyed as a rookie. Since posting an 86-889-10 receiving line in 17 games that first season, LaPorta has totaled a 100-1,215-10 line in 25 games over the past two seasons. LaPorta's 2025 campaign was cut short by a back injury, otherwise he was well on his way to his third straight top-10 fantasy campaign (he finished seventh in PPG). The 25-year-old joins Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs as the clear "Core Four" targets in a good, pass-friendly Detroit offense, and is thus a solid fantasy TE1.

outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard is expected to continue leading the Panthers' backfield in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Hubbard out-touched Jonathon Brooks 13 to five in the Week 1 loss, which is a good sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Hubbard also found the end zone twice and looked very efficient, averaging 6.7 yards per touch. He's in for a tougher Week 2 matchup, however, as Atlanta allowed just 16.4 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Hubbard appears to have returned to his 2024 form over Carolina's first two games this season, rushing for 102 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 49 yards and a score. Additionally, with Jonathon Brooks (groin) exiting the Week 2 win in the fourth quarter, Hubbard's role could continue growing. He faces a difficult matchup, however, as the Browns' defense has given up just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Without Jonathon Brooks (groin) in the Week 3 loss, Hubbard accounted for 82.1 percent of the Panthers' running back touches (23 to AJ Dillon's five). Despite Carolina throwing the ball over 40 times per game this season, Hubbard has remained one of fantasy's most productive backs, averaging 16.7 opportunities and 17.7 PPR points per game. He's likely to remain the bell-cow in Carolina's Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 19.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Hubbard is coming off one of the best games of his career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, totaling 129 yards and two touchdowns on 21 touches. He's been a true work-horse running back for the Panthers since Jonathon Brooks' (groin) injury, playing 84% of Carolina's snaps in Weeks 3 and 4. Expect Hubbard to continue producing in the Week 6 matchup against an Eagles defense that's given up 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Hubbard has been extremely productive for Carolina over its last three games, averaging 120 yards and a touchdown per game on 73 total touches. While Jonathon Brooks (groin) remains on the injured reserve list, Hubbard is expected to continue taking the vast majority of work in the Panthers' backfield. Despite this, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle. The veteran was limited to 734 yards on 164 touches (he cleared 275 touches and 1,100 yards in 2023 and 2024), and he ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Still in his prime at age 27, a bounce-back season is possible, especially with Dowdle gone and unproven Jonathon Brooks as his competition for touches. Hubbard should be considered a flex/bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Worthy captured three of his six Week 1 targets for only 18 yards. The workload was low, but Kansas City QB Patrick Mahomes completed only five passes to wideouts in the Monday night opener. The third-year pro has the speed to stretch the field, but he's generally used more underneath, along with occasionally carrying the ball. Worthy is a Week 2 flex option when the Chiefs host the Colts. Indianapolis was one of five defenses to allow over 300 yards passing in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Worthy scored his first touchdown of the season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, snagging a one-yard toss from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter. Worthy has notched steady target volume early in the season, with 13 total looks, but that has resulted in just an 8-43-1 line, and he has yet to get a carry. With Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Worthy will need some big plays to make a real fantasy contribution. The third-year speedster will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Worthy has struggled to break free for a big gain for Kansas City this season. The third-year speedster has managed just a 10-63-1 line on 15 targets, and surprisingly, he has yet to get a carry, perhaps to keep him healthy. Patrick Mahomes has also spread the ball around effectively, as Worthy, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets, so a big volume increase isn't likely. Worthy faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Xavier Worthy comes out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye still looking to establish himself as a consistent part of the passing attack. With both Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton getting hurt during a Week 4 win over the Raiders, Worthy caught four of seven targets for a season-high 70 yards. Rice appears to be on track to return quickly, but Thornton is likely to miss the rest of the year, which could open up some downfield routes for Worthy. The third-year speedster will face a Chargers secondary in Week 6 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Xavier Worthy is coming off his most productive game of the season, catching all seven of his targets for 73 yards in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers. With Rashee Rice sidelined, Worthy's volume has ticked up, but he hasn't been targeted more than seven times in a game this season. The third-year speedster also hasn't been able to break many big gains, with only one of his 21 catches going for 20-plus yards after nine of his 42 receptions in 2025 went for 20-plus. Worthy isn't likely to produce a ceiling game in Week 7 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing as a rookie with 101 touches and 12 touchdowns in 20 games (including the playoffs), Worthy had the look of an emerging star. Things didn't go as planned in Year 2, though, as the 2024 first-round pick was injured on his third snap of the season and wasn't productive or utilized as much as expected upon his return. Worthy was limited to one touchdown (Week 6) and reached 12 fantasy points once in 14 games (Week 4). The speedy Worthy is still only 23 years old, so a Year 3 breakout is certainly possible, especially with Rashee Rice and 36-year-old Travis Kelce as his only legit target competition. He's worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes proved he was fully recovered from last year's ACL injury in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, scoring a 15-yard rushing TD in addition to completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. The offense flowed through new lead back Kenneth Walker and benefited from some short fields, but Mahomes still took advantage of his opportunities. The star QB could be headed for better individual numbers in Week 2 against a Colts defense that looked awful in its opener and which ranked 31st in passing yards allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City's offense humming, and through two games, he's produced 566 passing yards and a 5:1 TD:INT while adding a touchdown on the ground. The superstar QB has spread the ball around effectively, as five different targets have been on the end of those TDs, and a revitalized running game with Kenneth Walker has prevented defenses from laying back and clogging the passing lanes. Mahomes could be headed for big numbers in Week 3 against a Dolphins defense that has yet to record a sack in 2026 and which sits 32nd in completion rate against at a stunning 78.8%.
outlooksByWeek.4: Patrick Mahomes continued his strong start to the season in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, producing multiple touchdowns for a third straight game. The two-time MVP has a 7:2 TD-to-INT ratio in those three contests while adding another score on the ground, and his 8.3 yards per attempt would be his highest mark since 2019. He's done it without the benefit of a single dominant receiver, as Travis Kelce, Kenneth Walker, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy have all logged between 15 and 18 targets. Mahomes will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Patrick Mahomes comes out of Kansas City's bye with a strong 9:2 TD:INT and 8.1 yards per attempt through four games. The presence of Kenneth Walker in the backfield has opened things up for the team's passing game, but Mahomes did lose Week 4 breakout Tyquan Thornton to a dislocated ankle that could potentially sideline the speedy wideout for the rest of the season. Rashee Rice also picked up a minor hamstring strain prior to the bye, which could leave Mahomes working with a very inexperienced group of WRs, although he still has Travis Kelce to fall back on. Mahomes will be facing a Chargers defense in Week 6 that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Patrick Mahomes didn't have much to do in Kansas City's Week 6 easy win over the Chargers. With Kenneth Walker and the defense doing most of the work in a 22-6 victory, Mahomes failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time this season, although he did rack up 272 passing yards and 9.1 yards per attempt. His 8.3 mark on the year is his best since 2019, and through five games he's produced 10 TDs-nine passing and one rushing-against three turnovers. Mahomes faces a much tougher test in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Love should continue to lead a high-volume passing attack as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Love finished Week 1 with the second-highest passing yard total of his career (387), completing 21 of 42 passes with two touchdowns and one interception. Most of his success came in the first half, with then two turnovers and virtually no offensive prowess in the fourth quarter. With that being said, Green Bay should continue to rely on the passing offense, especially given that there's no return timeline for RB1 Josh Jacobs (personal). Given that Love was able to find success against one of the best defenses in the game, he should have no problem piecing up a New York unit that allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game (22.1) to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Love will look to make a statement as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Love snuck out a win for Green Bay in Week 2, but a 55.2 percent completion rate for 145 yards, even with a 2:0 TD:INT, was uninspiring against the Jets. The sixth-year gunslinger luckily still sits at 532 passing yards on the year with four touchdowns and one interception, and his high volume only looks to continue with Josh Jacobs' return date uncertain. He'll face an Atlanta defense that gave up 287 passing yards and three touchdowns to Bryce Young this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Love will look to get the Packers back in the win column against Tampa Bay in Week 4. Love posted friendly fantasy numbers in Week 3 even amidst a disappointing loss, completing 52.8 percent of passes for 312 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. The sixth-year quarterback has now thrown two touchdowns in every game so far this season, and he's eclipsed 300 passing yards twice. Love remains a solid, high-volume option moving forward, especially given the struggles of Green Bay's run game. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a top-10 18.3 fantasy points per game to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Love will look to deliver a big win for the Packers in Week 5 against the Bears. Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT in a close win over Tampa Bay in Week 4. The veteran quarterback has now completed a career-low 56 percent of passes for 1,041 yards with eight touchdowns and three interceptions this season, with 300 or more passing yards in two of four outings. Love will take on a Chicago defense that's ranked 12th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jordan Love will look to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Love was on fire in a blowout win over the Bears in Week 5, completing 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. After a shaky but still touchdown-heavy start to the season, he's now completed 73 percent or more of his passes in back-to-back weeks and totaled 564 passing yards with a 4:1 TD:INT ratio in that stretch. Love will have the perfect opportunity to replicate his greatness again, as Dallas has ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks (23.8) so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Love will look to keep an electric stretch going as the Packers travel to Detroit in Week 7. Love was solid in another Packers win in Week 6, completing 23 of 41 passes for 276 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, and he also made some noise on the ground with two rushes for 14 yards and a touchdown. The fourth-year starter has now thrown for more than 275 yards in four of six games this season, and he's thrown two touchdowns in all but one outing. He'll enter another favorable matchup as the Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks on the year.

player.seasonOutlook: Love is back for his fourth season as the Packers' starting quarterback. The 2020 first-round pick has emerged as one of the league's best passers (he has finished ninth, fifth and third in QBR during his three seasons as a starter), but that hasn't converted to much fantasy production as of late. After finishing sixth in fantasy points per game in 2023, Love has finished 17th and 21st the past two seasons. A dramatic dip in both passing (19th in pass attempts both years) and rushing (282 yards and one TD total during the two seasons) has been the culprit. Love, who produced just five weekly finishes better than 16th last season, has a limited ceiling in Matt LaFleur's scheme. He's best valued as a back-end QB2.

No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hunter Henry will look for more opportunities in Week 2 when New England hosts Pittsburgh. Henry caught all three of his targets to open 2026, and with the Patriots losing A.J. Brown (ankle) for the foreseeable future, additional targets could come Henry's way. Pittsburgh didn't allow a catch to tight ends last week, but that was a product of poor opponent quarterback play. Henry can be considered a back-end option at the position with the potential for far more against a defense he posted two touchdowns and 90 yards against a season ago.
outlooksByWeek.3: Hunter Henry will look to keep expanding his role for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Jaguars. In their first full game without A.J. Brown in Week 2, Henry logged a 92% snap share but drew only five targets, turning them into three catches for 40 yards. Drake Maye has struggled to open the season, posting a 1:4 TD:INT ratio, and while someone has to catch the limited passes, Henry faces a challenging matchup against a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing tight end to top 32 yards against them so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Hunter Henry is laboring for opportunity in a sputtering Patriots passing offense ahead of a Week 4 game against the Bills. Henry caught just one of two targets in Week 3, finishing with five yards, and has yet to score or top 40 yards. There are likely better Week 4 options with Henry facing a defense that's allowed one opposing tight end to top 35 yards.
outlooksByWeek.5: Hunter Henry could have an expanded role in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders with Eli Raridon (ankle) uncertain. Henry was already playing at least 70% of the snaps, and he posted a season-high five catches for 62 yards in Week 4, collecting five targets for the second time this season. Las Vegas has allowed five touchdown catches to opposing tight ends, but also just 6.1 yards per target through four games, suggesting Henry may need to find the end zone for the first time in 2026 to be a fantasy asset.
outlooksByWeek.6: Hunter Henry has been steady in the Patriots passing game ahead of a potentially difficult Week 6 matchup with the Jets. He has three catches in four of the Patriots' first five games, three times recording at least 40 yards, and he posted 45 and 49 yards in two matchups last season against this divisional opponent. However, the Jets have been stingy against tight ends, allowing just 191 yards (6.0 yards per target) and zero touchdowns through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Hunter Henry brings a two-game scoring streak into the Patriots' Week 7 matchup with the Bears. With Drake Maye clicking on all cylinders over the last three weeks (10 touchdown passes), Henry has posted at least three catches and 44 yards during that stretch. Chicago has defended tight ends well for most of the season, but over the last two weeks, an opposing tight end has gone for 60 or more yards, and they've surrendered their first two touchdowns of the year to the position. Henry's volume is steady, giving him a bit more of a reliable floor than high potential.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference matchup in Week 2. The rookie third-round pick is doubtful to suit up with a fractured wrist sustained in the opener. Head coach Jesse Minter advised that Lane is seeking second and third medical opinions before establishing a timeline for his return. His health is something to monitor, but for now, his absence could make way for Devontez Walker (groin) and Elijah Sarratt (coach's decision).
outlooksByWeek.7: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens return home to face off against the division-rival Bengals in Week 7. He impressed in his first game back from a four-week stint on injured reserve with a wrist injury suffered in Week 1, catching four of five targets for 40 yards during Baltimore's Week 6 defeat. Lane tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing third in yardage, setting career highs across the board. With Rashod Bateman (shoulder) exiting the loss in the first half, Lane could see a boost in opportunities if the former is unable to suit up in Week 7. However, he'll be facing Cincinnati's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (29.3) to WRs, so it's best to proceed with caution.

player.seasonOutlook: Lane was selected by the Ravens in the third round of April's draft. Lane is a tall, perimeter receiver with the biggest hands in this rookie class. He produced solid 43-525-12 and 49-745-4 receiving lines during his final two seasons at USC. Lane was rarely used in the intermediate area and struggled to produce after the catch (career 3.7 RAC is second worst in this class), but he has the frame and skill set to allow him plenty of pro potential. He'll battle the likes of Devontez Walker and fellow rookie Elijah Surratt for work behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman in Baltimore's low-volume pass offense. Lane's primary value is as dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Puka Nacua managed to put up decent numbers despite the Rams' dismal offensive performance in their season opener, and he'll look to ramp up his production further in Week 2 against the Giants. Nacua recorded 74 of Matthew Stafford's 155 passing yards in Week 1 versus San Francisco, though he caught just five of nine targets. No other Rams pass catcher had more than three catches or 26 yards, so there's little doubt that Nacua unsurprisingly remains Stafford's favorite target. The Giants' defense looked good in a win over Dallas in Week 1, with top wideout CeeDee Lamb posting a modest 5-44-1 receiving line.
outlooksByWeek.3: Puka Nacua (hip) is uncertain to play in the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Nacua missed Monday's Week 2 game versus the Giants, though he wasn't ruled out until game day. That lends some hope that Nacua could return soon, though his availability for practice during the week should provide more insight about his potential to return versus the Broncos. Should Nacua suit up, he'll draw a tough Denver secondary that have given up just 203 receiving yards to wideouts so far, tied for third-fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Puka Nacua (hip) could return to action when the Rams face Philadelphia in Week 4. Nacua has missed Los Angeles' past two games due to a hip injury, but there is some hope that he can return against the Eagles. While Nacua has been out, Davante Adams has thrived statistically as the Rams' top wideout. The team's receiving corps as a whole could find success against an Eagles squad that ranks 24th in the NFL through three weeks by giving up an average of 24.0 fantasy points per game to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.5: Puka Nacua appears to be past his early-season injury woes as the Rams prepare to host Buffalo in Week 5. The star wideout missed Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hip/groin issue, but he returned this past Sunday against the Eagles and put up a 9-125-0 receiving line on 12 targets while adding a two-yard rushing touchdown. Nacua logged a 90% percent offensive snap share in the contest, so it doesn't appear that he is going to be inhibited by the injury, at least in terms of playing time, moving forward. The Bills present a good matchup on paper, as they've given up the fourth-most fantasy points (27.8) to wideouts so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Puka Nacua is coming off a massive performance on Monday Night Football with the Rams' Week 6 clash against the Cardinals on tap. Nacua recorded career-best marks with 17 catches and 24 targets in Week 5 against Buffalo, turning that enormous volume into 138 yards and a touchdown while adding nine yards on two carries. The TD was Nacua's first over three games this season, but he's otherwise been massively productive in averaging 10.3 receptions and 112.3 receiving yards per game. The Cardinals don't figure to offer much resistance, as they've yielded the second-most fantasy points per game (28.0) to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Puka Nacua should handle an even bigger role on offense following the news that Davante Adams will miss between six and 10 weeks due to a hamstring injury, so fantasy managers who have rostered Nacua could expect a sizable uptick in both volume and production. Nacua has already compiled 37 receptions for 417 yards and a touchdown through four appearances in 2026, and he's had over 75 receiving yards in every game, so the floor is clearly there. The Week 7 matchup against the Raiders looks like an ideal opportunity to deliver one of his best performances of the season, as Las Vegas has allowed the 10th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Nacua has defied the odds, emerging from fifth-round flier in 2023 to one of the most relied upon and productive offensive players in the league. Nacua has finished each of his three pro seasons sixth or better among receivers in fantasy PPG and peaked with a first-place finish last season. Matthew Stafford's top target led the league with 129 receptions and finished no lower than third among receivers in targets, yardage and touchdowns, while also adding 105 yards and one score as a rusher. More goal-line work would be nice (he has 11 end zone targets over the past two seasons), but Nacua's heavy usage in an elite offense locks in the 25-year-old as arguably the top receiver in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Olave definitely benefitted from Tyler Shough's 56 pass attempts during the Week 1 overtime loss. However, New Orleans averaged 34.8 pass attempts per game in 2025, so Olave will likely continue to see loads of volume. Additionally, he saw a 25 percent target share, which should remain steady until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns later this season. Olave is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to WRs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top receivers in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Olave ranks second in the NFL in both receptions (18) and receiving yards (268) through the first two weeks, cementing himself as New Orleans' top wideout. Currently, he's received a 25.6 percent target share, which should continue proving valuable with the Saints high-volume of pass attempts (90 through two weeks, second-most in the NFL). Olave could struggle against the Raiders, however, whose defense has allowed just 21.9 PPR fantasy points to wideouts per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Olave has surpasses 100 receiving yards in two of three games this season, catching 27 of 36 targets for 373 yards and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from New Orleans' pass-happy offense that has averaged 44 pass attempts per game through three weeks. Additionally, Olave is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a struggling Falcons secondary that's allowed 38.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Olave is expected to lead New Orleans' receiving corps again in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Olave has been spectacular through the Saints' first four games this season, catching 35 of 48 targets for 491 yards (second in the NFL) and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense, which has led to ample opportunities for Olave this season. Despite this, Olave could struggle in Week 5 against a tough Vikings secondary that's given up just 30.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Olave will look to return to form in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Olave struggled along with the rest of New Orleans' offense in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for 46 yards. On the season, Olave ranks second in the NFL with 537 receiving yards and will likely continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's aggressive style of offense (averaging 41 pass attempts per game). Expect Olave to bounce back against a solid Giants defense that's allowed 30.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Olave didn't receive his usual volume in Week 6 but remained productive, catching four of seven targets for 43 yards and a score. He's expected to continue benefitting from Kellen Moore's aggressive offense that's averaged 39.2 pass attempts per game through six weeks. However, Olave is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, as Pittsburgh's defense has given up just 29.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Olave is fresh off a career year in which he reached new highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yardage (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He finished eighth among receivers in fantasy PPG, which beat out his previous career best of 19th in 2023. Olave finished no lower than seventh among receivers in nearly every counting stat, including end zone targets (12) and air yards (1,816). The big season was a sigh of relief after a 2024 campaign riddled with concussions, and it positions the 26-year-old right back in the fringe-WR1 discussion. Especially with No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson expected to miss a month or two with a hamstring injury, Olave will remain Tyler Shough's top target, and that sets him up for another highly productive campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyren Williams may again be part of a pretty evenly split backfield when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Williams scored Los Angeles' only touchdown in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he had 13 fewer rushing yards on one more carry than backfield mate Blake Corum. Williams did produce more total yards thanks to logging 24 receiving yards on three catches, but Corum seems to have forced his way into a substantial backfield role after averaging over five yards per carry last year. Both backs will look to break through a Giants defense that gave up just 69 yards and 3.8 YPC against Dallas in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyren Williams is fresh off his most productive performance of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 4 clash against Philadelphia. Williams posted season-best tallies with 15 carries for 88 yards in Week 3 against Denver, and he complemented his output on the ground with a season-high six catches for 70 yards through the air. Whereas fellow running back Blake Corum has frequently eaten into Williams' volume since last season, Corum recorded just six totes and 15 total yards against the Broncos. Corum isn't likely to exit the picture anytime soon, but Williams remains a consistent week-to-week producer. However, he could have his work cut out for him in Week 4 versus an Eagles defense that ranks 12th in the league in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyren Williams enters the Rams' Week 5 matchup against the Bills with plenty of momentum. Williams totaled 147 yards and two touchdowns in a comeback win over Philadelphia in Week 4, pushing him up to four total TDs on the season. The star running back has logged at least 80 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's averaged 68.5 receiving yards across his past two contests. Buffalo has yielded 22.2 fantasy points per game to running backs so far, sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyren Williams will take aim at the end zone again in the Rams' Week 6 matchup versus the Cardinals. Though Williams was held to 49 yards on 16 carries against Buffalo in Week 6, he added 27 yards as a receiver and scored his fifth touchdown of the season. He also continued to put plenty of space between him and No. 2 RB Blake Corum, logging 11 more totes than his backup. Williams could find ample running room against an Arizona defense that ranks 19th in the league by allowing 4.17 yards per carry to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyren Williams remains the Rams' leading running back entering Week 7 against the Raiders, having rushed 80 times for 393 yards and four touchdowns while adding 30 receptions for 217 yards and another score. He's averaging an efficient 4.9 yards per carry, and his Week 6 showing against the Cardinals was right in line with that, as he notched 50 rushing yards in just 10 carries. Williams' receiving involvement provides a dependable fantasy foundation, particularly with Davante Adams sidelined for an extended period, and this looks like a favorable matchup on paper for the star tailback since Las Vegas has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams continues to produce at a high level as the Rams' lead back. The 2022 fifth-round pick has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons (including a career-high 1,533 in 2025), and he's one of 11 backs in NFL history who have scored 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. Williams' carry share actually dropped quite a bit last season, but it was mostly offset by a boost in both rushing and receiving efficiency, and he still averaged a healthy 15.5 fantasy points. Williams doesn't do much as a receiver (he has never cleared 36 catches in a season), but his overall usage and scoring potential in the Rams' elite offense is enough to make the 26-year-old a solid RB2 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will aim to replicate a huge game as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Swift was dominant against the Panthers in Week 1, carrying the ball 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns. The veteran ball carrier topped any of his games in the 2025 season, showcasing that he should also benefit from a higher-scoring Chicago offense this year. He'll play a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but he has established himself more than the Packers' current RB room.
outlooksByWeek.3: D'Andre Swift will be a top option in Chicago's offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Swift cooled down in Week 2 after a monster opener, logging 16 rushes for 45 yards on the ground. The veteran RB did see success in the passing game, logging five catches for 54 yards. With Tyson Bagent expected to start at quarterback for the Bears, Swift could be utilized more heavily on the ground. Philadelphia has also allowed 216 rushing yards to running backs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: D'Andre Swift should remain Chicago's top option in the rushing game against the Jets in Week 4. Swift saw a season-high 20 carries in Week 3 versus Philly , taking them for 84 yards and adding on two catches for four yards. The veteran ball carrier eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign, but he's seen his only end zone appearances come from Week 1. He'll now turn his attention to a Jets defense that ceded 99 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 20 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in their most recent outing.
outlooksByWeek.5: D'Andre Swift will seek to get back on track as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Swift rushed the ball 15 times for 58 yards and caught two targets for 16 yards against the Jets in Week 4, but he also lost a fumble and was stopped at the goal line twice. The veteran was outplayed by his younger counterpart, Kyle Monangai, who posted a 30-146-2 rushing line. Either way, Swift should still get plenty of usage against a Packers defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: D'Andre Swift could be in line for a featured role once again as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Swift should have benefited hugely from Kyle Monangai being out with a toe injury in Week 5, but he rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 30 yards in a blowout loss. The status of Monangai remains up in the air ahead of Chicago's away bout, and Swift's value is very much contingent on his position mate's status. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: D'Andre Swift could see his workload take a hit as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Swift was inefficient on the ground in Week 6 with 16 carries for 44 yards, but he was able to salvage his outing with two rushing touchdowns and four catches for 26 yards. The veteran has benefited from Kyle Monangai being out the last two weeks with turf toe, especially given that three of his six touchdowns this season have come in that stretch. Whether Monangai plays or not, Swift will face a New England front that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Warren salvaged his fantasy day in the Colts' season-opening loss with a nine-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, but he had only four receiving yards across the rest of the game. The 2025 first-round pick has just 213 receiving yards in his last eight games after recording 617 yards in his first 10 outings. Warren did enough in Week 1 to warrant another fantasy start in most formats for a Week 2 road game against the Chiefs, but his lack of yards since the halfway point of his rookie season is becoming a worrying trend.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Warren has started his second NFL season on a two-game TD streak but has a meager 34 receiving yards on 12 targets. The Colts' 2025 first-round pick is poised to keep logging plenty of targets in Week 3 against the Texans, as Indianapolis is running out of NFL-caliber pass catchers in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Warren had six catches in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City, a game Pierce exited early. Given Warren's mix of talent and usage, he remains a top-10 fantasy TE in Week 3 against Houston's talented defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Warren has increased his catch total by three with each subsequent game this season, and he has scored in two of the Colts' three games heading into a Week 4 international game against the Commanders in London. Coming off a nine-catch game, Warren is a set-and-forget starting fantasy TE against a Washington defense that has allowed five TDs to the position through three games. The 2025 first-round pick is a key part of a Colts passing game that's missing top WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on injured reserve.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Warren has emerged with a consistent role as a short outlet for Colts QB Daniel Jones. Warren has caught 23 of 27 targets for 130 yards and two TDs, averaging almost six catches per game but just 5.7 yards per catch. His floor is high enough to be trusted as a weekly fantasy starter at TE, as Warren leads the Colts in catches and is one target shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. Week 5 at Pittsburgh is no exception, even though the Steelers are tied for the fourth-fewest catches allowed to TEs with 13. Two of those 13 receptions have resulted in touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Warren had a season-high 83 receiving yards and a short rushing TD in the Colts' Week 5 loss to Pittsburgh. The versatile TE has been the team's second-best offensive player behind star RB Jonathan Taylor. Warren has accounted for three of the team's five non-Taylor touchdowns and leads the Colts with 30 catches through five games. Warren remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter in Week 6 due to his prominent involvement in the game plan every week, even against a Titans defense that has allowed the third-fewest receiving yards to TEs at 29 per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Warren sat out the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans after being a late addition to the injury report due to a groin injury. If the 2025 first-round pick is cleared to return in Week 7 against the Vikings, he would reclaim his role as a key cog on offense for the Colts and a borderline top-five fantasy TE. Jonathan Taylor has seven of the Colts' 13 offensive TDs this season, and Warren has scored three of the other six while averaging six receptions per game. Minnesota hasn't allowed a TE to score this season while giving up 44 receiving yards per game to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren put together a solid rookie season, but it could've been even better. In 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones, Warren scored five touchdowns and averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG. In five games without Jones, Warren fell to 6.3 PPG and failed to find the end zone. In fact, the 2025 first-round pick was unlucky in the scoring department, ranking fifth among tight ends in end zone targets (seven) and expected TDs (7.5). Warren finished the season third among tight ends in targets and also had three goal-line carries. The 24-year-old was already a featured target and might see even more work with Michael Pittman Jr. shipped to Pittsburgh. Warren is a quality TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in New England to face the Patriots in Week 2. The veteran wideout corralled four of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win against the Falcons. He led the team in targets by four but finished third in receiving yards. Metcalf has a hypothetical advantage over Michael Pittman after playing last year with Aaron Rodgers, and there's a good chance he'll be his favorite target against New England's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional clash. He caught four of a team-high nine targets for just 27 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Metcalf finished fifth in yardage despite tying Germie Bernard and Pat Freiermuth for second in receptions, and he now has an 8-67-0 receiving line on 19 targets through two outings. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers offense have been underwhelming to begin the season, and they'll face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North clash between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught three of five targets for 31 yards and his first TD of the season during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. Metcalf has an 11-98-1 receiving line on 24 targets through three contests, as he and Aaron Rodgers have had a hard time connecting in their second season together. With that being said, it'll be difficult to trust Metcalf until the duo is on the same page, even against a beatable Cleveland secondary allowing 36.7 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 26th.
outlooksByWeek.5: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Colts in a Week 5 clash between 2-2 teams. He caught five of nine targets for 115 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Metcalf turned in his best performance of the season by far while leading his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He'll look to stay hot against a beatable Indianapolis secondary that allows 35.0 fantasy points per game (20th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are on the road to take on the Buccaneers in Week 6. He caught three of four targets for 12 yards and rushed once for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Metcalf and Darnell Washington tied for the fewest receiving yards on the team, while the veteran wideout finished fourth in targets. He'll try to rebound against a Tampa Bay defense that allows 29.5 fantasy points per game (12th) to WRs and just gave up nine receptions for 130 yards and a TD to George Pickens.
outlooksByWeek.7: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 showdown against the Saints. He caught 11 of 15 targets for 93 yards in Pittsburgh's gritty comeback victory in Week 6. Metcalf led the team in yardage and targets while tying with rookie Germie Bernard (11-87-1) for first in receptions. The 11 catches were a product of game flow with the Steelers playing from behind most of the game, and they were Metcalf's most on the season by far, as he had the same number of receptions over his previous three games combined. He'll look to take advantage of a New Orleans defense that just allowed Malik Nabers to record a 12-165-0 line on 15 targets.

player.seasonOutlook: Metcalf returns for Year 2 in Pittsburgh after a solid but unspectacular debut season. The ex-Seahawk missed two games and finished outside the top 20 receivers in targets, catches and yardage (career-low 850), but still did just enough to produce a 21st-place finish in fantasy PPG (his fifth top-25 in his last six seasons). Metcalf soaked up 11 end zone targets and is up to 107 for his career, which leads the NFL since his debut in 2019. The 28-year-old has added target competition this season in the form of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, so while he'll certainly remain busy, a slight dip in usage is probable. Metcalf should be valued as a back-end WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Stefon Diggs had more than double the targets of teammate Terry McLaurin in Week 1 for Washington. Diggs was targeted a team-high nine times, though managed only four catches. However, he gained 55 yards and also found the end zone, though had a costly celebration penalty on the score that cost Washington a chance to go for two and tie the game late. Still, it was an extremely promising start for Diggs, who will have a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus Dallas. The Cowboys allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Stefon Diggs has scored three times in two games as a member of the Commanders. Diggs snagged five passes for 47 yards and two touchdowns in Washington's loss to Dallas last week. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Diggs and the rest of the Washington offense, though the newly acquired wideout does seem to have a knack for finding the end zone thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Stefon Diggs finished second in targets for the Commanders last game. Diggs caught four balls on seven looks, though managed just 33 yards in the surprising win over Seattle. Diggs was also held out of the end zone for the first time this season. Diggs caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Stefon Diggs led the Commanders in targets and receptions last game. With Terry McLaurin sidelined due to a hamstring issue, Diggs managed five catches on nine targets. However, he could only muster 35 yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Diggs, regardless of whether McLaurin also suits up. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Stefon Diggs missed Washington's last game due to a hamstring issue. In his absence, Terry McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams would likely benefit if Diggs cannot suit up in Week 6 versus the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. The 30-year-old was Tampa Bay's second-most productive wideout in the Week 1 loss, hauling in all four of his targets for 40 yards. Godwin likely won't have many big plays after sustaining multiple serious lower-body injuries throughout his career, but he should remain a reliable PPR option and an important part of the Buccaneers' offense moving forward. Additionally, he's in for a great Week 2 matchup, as the Browns defense allowed 13.6 yards per target to WRs in Week 1, the second-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Godwin will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Godwin leads Tampa Bay's receiving corps in offensive snaps played (101) and has caught all seven of his targets through two weeks. However, this hasn't translated to much production, as he's accumulated just 86 receiving yards. Expect Godwin to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in a difficult matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 27 receptions to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Godwin had a quiet Week 3 performance (3-25-0), though he had an 85-yard touchdown reception called back for holding. The veteran wideout has struggled along with the rest of Tampa Bay's offense, and those struggles could be amplified with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined for the Week 4 contest. However, Godwin is in for a favorable matchup against a Packers defense that's allowed 6.7 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top weapons in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Godwin was targeted a season-high seven times in the Week 4 loss to the Packers, catching six of them for just 31 yards. The veteran wideout may actually benefit from Jalon Daniels acting as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback while Baker Mayfield (thumb) is sidelined, as Godwin could act as the rookie's safety blanket. Additionally, Godwin is in for a good Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's allowed five receiving touchdowns to WRs through four contests this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Godwin is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top safety blanket in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Godwin has caught 19 of 22 targets this season, totaling 179 yards. Despite ranking second on the Buccaneers in receptions and third in targets, he's gotten just one red-zone target all season and could struggle finding fantasy relevance without a touchdown. Regardless, Godwin is in for a tough Week 6 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up 220.8 passing yards per game this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Godwin was targeted a season-high eight times during the Week 6 loss to the Steelers, recording four receptions for 37 yards. The veteran wideout ranks second on Tampa Bay in targets (30), receptions (23) and yards (216) through the first six games and could benefit from the potential return of Baker Mayfield (thumb) in Week 7. However, Godwin is in for a tough matchup against a Panthers secondary that's allowed just 5.9 yards per pass attempt this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Godwin is on the comeback trail after injuries have limited him to 16 games during the past two seasons. In 2025, he appeared in nine games and reached 11 fantasy points only twice. It seems like a long time ago, Godwin was second among receivers in fantasy points in 2024 when he suffered a severe ankle injury. He wasn't nearly as effective when he was on the field last season, but he's now more than a full year recovered from the injury and has less target competition with Mike Evans no longer on the roster. Entering his age-30 season, Godwin's days as a fantasy WR1 may be over, but with Emeka Egbuka as his only competition to lead the team in targets, he certainly has a path to flex numbers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Stafford will look to clean things up in the turnover department when the Rams host Buffalo in Week 5. Stafford was picked off twice and didn't throw any touchdowns in Week 4 against Philadelphia, but he also threw for 317 yards and led Los Angeles to a comeback victory. Still, Stafford has recorded a mediocre 6:6 TD:INT through four games, with the pickoff total nearly reaching the eight interceptions he tossed across 17 regular-season contests during his MVP campaign last year. The Bills have given up 10 passing touchdowns and have picked off just two passes this year, so Week 5 may be a good opportunity for Stafford to get back on track.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Stafford will look to help Los Angeles rebound from a crushing loss on Monday Night Football with a Week 6 matchup against Arizona. Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns in Week 5 against Buffalo, but the team was defeated in overtime. Still, it was an impressive showing for the reigning NFL MVP, as he posted his fourth consecutive effort of 300-plus passing yards. Stafford could be in for another big performance versus a Cardinals defense that has given up the second-highest passer rating (117.2) this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Stafford enters the Rams' Week 7 matchup against the Raiders having completed 164 of 249 passes for 1,794 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions through six games. The veteran quarterback is averaging 299 passing yards per contest, but his production has been inconsistent, and Los Angeles has stumbled to a 2-4 record. The absence of Davante Adams, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, creates another obstacle for Stafford. However, Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, making Stafford an appealing bounce-back candidate despite the Rams' recent offensive struggles.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jared Goff will look to build off a season-opener win as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Goff's performance and Detroit's overall in Week 1 weren't pretty, but he got the job done, finishing with 206 passing yards and two touchdowns. The game also showed that the Lions will continue to have a high-volume air attack, as the veteran ended with 39 pass attempts. Goff will now turn his focus to a Bills defense that ceded 274 passing yards and two touchdowns to C.J. Stroud in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Goff will look to keep his high production rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Goff benefited from playing from behind in Week 2 at Buffalo, racking up 327 passing yards and four touchdowns on a 68.4 percent completion rate. The veteran quarterback has now totaled 533 passing yards with a 6:0 TD:INT across his first two games, and Detroit's lacking defense has only helped his output so far. Goff will take on a Jets defense that's allowed a top-10 fantasy points per game (14.2) to quarterbacks in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jared Goff will continue to benefit from a high-powered offense as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Goff kept it rolling in Week 3, throwing for 269 yards with two touchdowns and zero interceptions. The veteran quarterback has completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 802 yards and eight touchdowns with no interceptions across three games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game (23.5) to QBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jared Goff will remain a high-volume option as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. No matter the outcome of each game so far, Goff has delivered consistent output, and Week 4 against the Panthers was no different. The veteran quarterback recorded season-high totals in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, completing 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in what was an eventual loss. He's now thrown for 250 or more yards in his last three games, and he's yet to commit a turnover this year. Goff will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jared Goff will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Goff recorded another monster performance heading into Detroit's bye week, and he's yet to throw an interception this season. The veteran quarterback has now completed 67 percent of passes for 1,485 yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions in five games. He'll face a Green Bay defense that allowed 258 passing yards and a 1:2 TD:INT ratio to Dak Prescott in Week 6.

player.seasonOutlook: Goff is entering his 10th NFL season, including his sixth with the Lions. The 2016 No. 1 draft pick has been extremely successful through the air over the past three seasons (4,500-plus yards and 30-plus touchdowns in all three), which has helped him to fantasy finishes of seventh, sixth and ninth. Of course, there's some survivorship bias here, as Goff's per-game finishes during the span are 15th, seventh and 12th. The reason for the limited fantasy output is a lack of rushing, as Goff has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season and was held to 45 yards in 2025. Playing at his absolute ceiling as a passer and still no more than a fringe QB1, the 31-year-old is just a solid backup/occasional streaming option in fantasy.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rachaad White found the end zone last game for Washington. White caught a six-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota during the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. White also doubled up starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in terms of yards per carry. However, Bill out-touched White by a margin of 20-9 for the game. Nevertheless, both backs should remain involved in Week 4 versus a suspect Colts defense. Indianapolis is allowing the most yards per game in the NFL through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rachaad White missed Washington's last game due to a shoulder issue, leaving his status in question for Week 5 versus the Giants. An argument can be made that White has been more productive than fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt in 2026, though that point may be moot as long as White is sidelined. Austin Ekeler will be the backup to Bill if White remains shelved. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rachaad White returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a shoulder issue. However, White failed to have much of an impact. He rushed seven times for just 18 yards, while also catching a two-yard pass out of the backfield. Meanwhile, starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown. In Week 6, the Commanders face a 49ers defense that has been rather stingy against the run. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per clash, which is 10th in the league. In addition, San Fran has surrendered just three rushing scores to date, which is tied for sixth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are on the road in Week 2 to take on Houston. The Texans have the 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to TEs, and they are last in receiving yards allowed to the position after Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox combined for 137 yards last week. Gesicki led the Bengals in catches (5), targets (7), and receiving yards (78) in Week 1, to go along with one TD. He could be primed for another big performance in what may very well be another high-scoring affair.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 3. After leading Cincinnati in receptions, yards, and targets in the season opener, Gesicki failed to record a single target versus the Texans in Week 2. Some of that could be chalked up to game flow with the Bengals ahead for most of the game, but it's nonetheless worrisome. The Steelers rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) and are first in receptions allowed to TEs through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town in Week 4. He caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Gesicki finished third in receiving yards while catching his second TD of the young season, just one week after failing to earn a target. Jacksonville's defense ranks fifth in fantasy points allowed (7.8) and second in receptions (8) to TEs, so he could be in for another quiet day.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals travel to take on the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He grabbed three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. Gesicki now has two straight outings with a TD and recorded his third overall, and he could be in line for an uptick in opportunities in a favorable matchup versus a Miami defense that allows 18.6 fantasy points to TEs, which is tied for 28th. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor), and Colbie Young (knee) are all questionable, potentially leaving Gesicki as one of Joe Burrow's primary receivers against a Dolphins unit that just gave up 13 receptions and 119 yards to T.J. Hockenson
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Baltimore for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He caught one of two targets for a four-yard touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Fellow tight end Erick All Jr. notched a 3-25-0 line on three targets, finishing second on the team in yardage. Gesicki is hard to trust with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) healthy, especially versus a Baltimore defense tied for seventh in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darius Cooper caught the game-winning touchdown for the Eagles in Week 2. Cooper managed just two catches for 26 yards, though one of them gave the Eagles the lead for good with precious seconds left on the clock. Cooper also tied for third on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.5: Darius Cooper scored twice last game for the Eagles. Cooper finished the contests with seven targets, parlaying those looks into three catches for 33 yards and the pair of scores. If Devonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and/or Saquon Barkley are sidelined in Week 5 versus the Jags, Cooper could see an uptick in usage again.  Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darius Cooper continues to flash his big-play ability for the Eagles. Cooper snagged his fourth touchdown of the season last game versus the Jaguars en route to leading the Eagles in receiving yards. Four of Cooper's seven receptions have gone for touchdowns in 2026. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has also likely boosted the opportunities for Cooper, who has 10 targets in his last two contests alone. This trend could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darius Cooper caught just one pass for nine yards last game for the Eagles. Cooper had just two targets overall, as the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap Cooper's upside as well. However, in Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathan Taylor carried the Colts' offense with 121 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 22 touches in the season opener. His heavy Week 1 workload was encouraging considering the Colts trailed by 18 points at halftime and lost by that same margin to the Ravens. Indianapolis could face another negative game script in Week 2 at Kansas City, but Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1, even with the team around him looking shaky. Taylor led the NFL with 323 carries and 18 rushing TDs last season while compiling 1,963 scrimmage yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathan Taylor has scored multiple rushing TDs in both of the Colts' games heading into a Week 3 home tilt against the Texans. The star RB led the NFL with 20 scrimmage TDs last season and looks poised to finish near the top of the leaderboard again this season. Taylor is a set-and-forget fantasy RB1, even against a stout Texans front seven that allowed the fourth-fewest rushing yards to RBs last season and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jonathan Taylor has four rushing TDs through three games and is averaging 25 touches per game heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London. Washington has allowed the third-fewest rushing yards in the NFL while struggling to defend the pass, but the Colts have proven they intend to feed their star RB a steady diet of carries regardless of opponent. A positive game script is certainly possible against a Commanders team that's starting backup QB Marcus Mariota, so Taylor has a clear path to another heavy workload and remains a must-start fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD performances through four games and is averaging 88 rushing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers rank among the 10 most generous defenses against RBs, allowing 138 scrimmage yards and one TD per game to the position. Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1 while working as the focal point of the Colts' offense, which lacked talent at wide receiver even before injuries further depleted that position. His 26 scrimmage touchdowns since the start of last season are the most in the NFL over that span.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD outings on the ground through five games, and he's likely to be the focal point of the Colts' offense in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who are surrendering 120 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Taylor averages 23 touches per game and should handle a heavy workload, with the Colts expected to play from ahead at home. Start the star RB, who is averaging 101 scrimmage yards per game, with confidence in this clash between AFC South rivals.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jonathan Taylor has topped 90 rushing yards four times this season and has seven TDs, while the rest of the Colts' offense has scored six touchdowns combined. The star RB remains a set-and-forget fantasy RB1 for Week 7, even in a difficult matchup with a stout Vikings defense that's allowing 86.6 rushing yards per game (fifth-fewest) and a league-low 12.8 points per game. Opponents have been stacking the box against Taylor with Daniel Jones struggling to make defenses pay through the air, but Taylor has overcome those difficult situations to rank among the league's most productive players at his position as usual, despite the lack of help from his teammates.
