player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Saquon Barkley averaged 5.5 yards per tote in Week 1 for the Eagles. Barkley rushed 15 times for 83 yards, though was held out of the end zone in the 24-22 win over Washington. Barkley should have even greater success in Week 2 versus a dismal Titans squad. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Saquon Barkley missed portions of Philadelphia's last game due to a stinger, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Saquon had five carries for just 20 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown, while Will Shipley saw nine touches and managed 29 yards overall. Bigsby and Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Saquon Barkley rushed for 82 yards last game for the Eagles. Philadelphia fell behind in the second half, though, which forced the Eagles to all but abandon the run. Barkley has yet to rush for 100 yards in a game this season. In Week 4, Barkley will face a stout defensive line with Aaron Donald when the Eagles clash with the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Saquon Barkley left Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring ailment. While the injury is not considered serious, it remains to be seen whether Barkley will be able to suit up in London in Week 5 versus the Jags. If Barkley can play, he will face a stiff test, as Jacksonville is allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is second in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have given up just two rushing touchdowns through the first four games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Saquon Barkley missed Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina remains up in the air. The Eagles could be on their fourth-string running back in the form of Dameon Pierce, as Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve and Will Shipley started last game but suffered a foot injury of his own and did not return. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense, though. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Saquon Barkley has missed the last two games for the Eagles due to a hamstring ailment, leaving his status for Week 7 versus the Cowboys in jeopardy. Dameon Pierce rushed for 35 yards and a touchdown in Barkley's place, while also catching four balls out of the backfield. If Barkley can somehow suit up, he will be facing a Dallas defense that has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL to date. Per game, the Cowboys are allowing a brutal 149.8 yards on the ground.

player.seasonOutlook: Barkley is looking to rebound in his ninth NFL season (third with the Eagles) following a big step back in 2025. After producing 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in his first season with Philly, Barkley dipped to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. Barkley fell from first among backs in fantasy points per game (22.5) to 15th (14.5). Now 29 years old, it's possible Barkley's best days are behind him, but he's still positioned as a clear feature back in a good offense that will have a healthier line and a new playcaller in Sean Mannion. Barkley is riskier than ever, but he's still worthy of mid- to back-end RB1 consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to operate as Carolina's top pass catcher in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. McMillan caught just five passes for 75 yards and lost a fumble in last week's loss, despite the game ending with the most points ever scored in a Week 1 contest. He was out-shined by third-year wideout Jalen Coker, who paced Carolina's receiving corps in targets (nine), receptions (eight), yards (138) and touchdowns (two). McMillan will look to return to form in Week 2, but he's in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that gave up just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top targets in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. McMillan bounced back in Week 2 after a lackluster Week 1 performance, catching five of 10 targets for 101 yards while leading the team in receiving. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year is tied with Jalen Coker for the most targets on Carolina (18) entering Week 3, which is a positive sign for both players' outlooks going forward. With the Panthers' offensive success through two games, McMillan should be in for a great Week 3 matchup, especially while facing a Browns defense that's given up four receiving touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tetairoa McMillan will look to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year was held to just two catches for 17 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, the second-fewest yards he's ever recorded in an NFL game. Despite this, McMillan has an extremely positive outlook going forward, as both Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) are dealing with injuries, making him the clear number one target. Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top receiving option in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. McMillan is coming off the best performance of his young career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, recording career highs in targets (16), receptions (14) and yards (192) while scoring two touchdowns. He ranks ninth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (96.3) through four appearances this season, leading Carolina in yards, targets and receptions. Expect McMillan to remain productive in Week 6 against an Eagles secondary that's allowed 38.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of Carolina's top wideouts in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. McMillan has been one of the league's most productive wideouts this season, catching 32 of 48 targets for 471 yards and two touchdowns in just five contests. He's averaged 94.2 receiving yards per game, the seventh-best mark in the NFL, and is expected to continue benefitting from the Panthers' aggressive style of offense (40.2 pass attempts per game). Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers secondary that's allowed 32.2 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, McMillan is a candidate to make the leap into the "elite" conversation at wide receiver this season. The 2025 eighth overall pick was very busy as a rookie (top 15 among WRs in snaps, routes, target share, targets, yards, end zone targets and touchdowns) and, while he finished 16th among receivers in fantasy points (22nd PPG), he lacked upside, producing only one top-10 outing (Week 9). Improving on a 56% catch rate will be key in Year 2, though that would require improvement from Bryce Young. McMillan, 23, remains positioned as Carolina's clear top target and, though Young's limitations may cap his ceiling a bit, McMillan's talent/usage combo supplies him with top-10 upside. He's safest as a midrange fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference showdown in Week 2. Jackson was stellar in the opener despite losing a fumble, throwing for 324 yards (17-for-25) with one TD and no picks while rushing seven times for another 40 yards and a TD. Although he still offers elite upside at the QB position, it's important to note that his favorite receiver, Zay Flowers, is dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Jesse Minter considers "day-to-day." The two connected on five of six targets for 150 yards and a score in the victory. The New Orleans defense ranks 12th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.5) to QBs after Jared Goff's 206 yards and two TDs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens look to bounce back after a tough loss when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. Jackson threw for 235 yards (21-for-31) with one TD and one INT while rushing four times for 34 yards in Week 2's 24-17 loss. Baltimore draws a favorable matchup against a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in fantasy points allowed (27.2) and 31st in rushing yards allowed to QBs. Zay Flowers (hamstring) missed Week 2's contest, but the hope is that Jackson's speedy receiver makes it back on the field in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the 0-3 Titans for a Week 4 showdown. In Baltimore's thrilling 34-31 win over Dallas in Week 3, he connected on 15 of 20 throws for 186 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 50 yards, including a 27-yard strike to Zay Flowers that helped set up the game-winning field goal as time expired. Tennessee's defense has been stingy, allowing just 13.9 fantasy points per game to QBs through three games, which ranks first. Jackson should have his full complement of receivers available as the Ravens aim to improve to 3-1 on the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens travel to face the Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 5. Prior to missing the entire second half of Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4, the two-time MVP threw for 222 yards (15-for-20) with two TDs and no INTs while rushing twice for 20 yards. Jackson was well on his way to a stellar outing with his team up 24-7 at halftime, but an ankle injury forced him out early and has him in jeopardy of missing the upcoming road tilt in Atlanta. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that the Ravens are uncertain of Jackson's status for Week 5, and if he's unable to suit up, Tyler Huntley will get the nod at quarterback.
outlooksByWeek.6: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the division-rival Browns in Week 6. The two-time league MVP sat out Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5 with a sprained left ankle. Head coach Jesse Minter relayed Monday that Jackson is "definitely doing better" in his recovery, but there's still no guarantee that he'll be ready for the trip to Cleveland. Tyler Huntley filled in admirably as the starting QB, throwing for 201 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 20 yards and another score in the OT victory. Jackson will need to practice in some form before the Ravens can determine his status against the Browns' 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Bengals for an AFC North showdown in Week 7. He missed a second consecutive game in Week 6, a 13-10 loss to Cleveland, due to an ankle injury sustained in Week 4. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Jackson could potentially get back on the practice field during Week 7 prep, but Baltimore is still considering their star quarterback day-to-day. If he's unable to suit up for the third straight contest, Tyler Huntley will continue to start under center versus Cincinnati's 19th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.5) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jackson, 29, is eyeing a rebound after a disappointing, injury-plagued 2025. Jackson started the season strong (26-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games) but left Week 4 because of an injury and wasn't the same once he returned in Week 9 (13.5 fantasy points per game in his final nine outings). Jackson's overall rushing was down, but that was likely a product of him not being fully healthy, especially considering his scramble rate (8.4%) remained high. Jackson has a new coach (Jesse Minter) and playcaller (Declan Doyle), but his supporting cast is otherwise similar to a 2024 campaign in which he paced all quarterbacks in fantasy points. Assuming he's back to full health, Jackson is a strong bet for a rebound and should be valued as a high-end QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Luther Burden will look to stay highly involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent starting under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Burden will take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Luther Burden will aim to build on an impressive performance as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Burden had his first big time of the season against the Eagles in Week 3, turning 11 targets into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wideout had a solid connection with veteran Case Keenum, who is likely to fill in under center for at least one more week, if not more. This bodes well for the future of Burden, but he will have to face a New York defense that's allowed the eleventh-least fantasy points per game (28.2) and fourth-least receiving yards (337) to wide receivers across three outings.
outlooksByWeek.5: Luther Burden will aim to stay involved as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Burden tied his season high of 63 receiving yards in Week 4 against the Jets, and he's now recorded 60 or more yards in all but one game this season. The second-year wide receiver appears to be a pivotal part of Chicago's offense, and he could be a key piece towards a win in Tundratown. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Luther Burden will continue to be a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 6 at Atlanta. Burden brought in four of six targets for a team-high 47 receiving yards and rushed the ball four times for two yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers. The second-year pass catcher has been unable to get things going in multiple games this season, but this can be attributed to the struggles at the quarterback position. No matter who is throwing him the ball, the Falcons ranking 27th in fantasy point allowed to wide receivers this campaign could be favorable for Burden.
outlooksByWeek.7: Luther Burden will seek to stay busy as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Burden secured all eight of his targets for 95 yards in a Week 6 win over the Falcons, leading Chicago in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The second-year wideout has a 31-361-1 line on 43 targets across six games this season, and a dominant connection looks to be growing with quarterback Caleb Williams. Burden will now turn his sights to a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Pitts will look to rebound for a disappointing Week 1 performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Pitts failed to haul in his lone target during last week's loss, with Bijan Robinson and Drake London combining for a 73.6% of Cooper Rush's targets. Despite this, Pitts could very well rebound against a Panthers defense that just allowed a whopping 59 points in Week 1, as they also gave up 11.5 PPR fantasy points to tight ends. His rebound could depend on Atlanta's quarterback situation, with both Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) looking to return from injury in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Pitts has really struggled along with the majority of Atlanta's offense throughout the first two weeks, catching just one of four targets for 15 yards. However, he could really benefit from the return of Michael Penix as the team's starting quarterback heading into Week 3. While Penix was healthy during the 2025 season, Pitts averaged 4.2 receptions and 41.7 yards per game -- a vast difference from his 2026 production thus far. He's also in for a favorable matchup, as the Packers' defense has allowed 12.0 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a disappointing start in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Despite Michael Penix returning to the field in the Week 3 win over the Packers, Pitts' role remained limited, catching just one of two targets for five yards. He was overshadowed by Drake London (9-194-0) and appears to be operating as the Falcons' No. 3 pass catcher, also behind Bijan Robinson (16 targets to Pitts' six). However, Pitts could rebound in Week 4, as the Saints' defense has allowed 20.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Pitts had his most productive game of the season in the Week 4 win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 47 yards. Despite this, he played just 50% of Atlanta's offensive snaps and has now logged an average of 2.3 targets per game, suggesting he may not be as involved in the team's offensive game plan as he has been in past years. Additionally, Pitts in in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 10.4 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyle Pitts will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Pitts had his best game of the 2026 season during the Week 5 overtime loss to the Ravens, catching five of six targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. Since the return of quarterback Michael Penix (ribs) in Week 3, Pitts has caught nine of 11 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown. Pitts could struggle in Week 6, however, as he's set to face a Chicago defense that's allowed just 7.7 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top offensive weapons in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Pitts is coming off his best performance of the season in a Week 6 loss to the Bears, catching five of seven targets for 60 yards and two scores. It appears as if he's been more involved in Atlanta's offensive game plan over the last two weeks, catching 10 of 13 targets for 102 yards and three touchdowns after receiving just nine targets in his first four contests. However, Pitts could struggle against a solid 49ers defense that's given up just 8.4 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs through five games this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Right when it seemed like Pitts might never live up to the hype, the 2021 No. 4 pick put together the best season of his career. Pitts finished second among tight ends in routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy points, setting career highs in all but the yardage category. He scored five touchdowns and has increased his total in that category (by exactly one) each season in the league. Pitts did a big chunk of his damage with Kirk Cousins under center (some with WR Drake London sidelined), which is notable as Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. are set to battle for the Atlanta QB job. There's some obvious risk here considering Pitts finished 17th or lower in PPG three straight seasons before 2025, but he nonetheless enters his age-25 season as a priority target in the Atlanta offense. Consider him a midrange TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Wilson will look to break through against a tough Seattle secondary for Arizona in Week 2. Wilson performed well in a season-opening win over the Chargers, catching five of seven targets for 56 yards. He outproduced presumed No. 1 wideout Marvin Harrison, though newcomer Kendrick Bourne led the WR corps with an 8-75-0 line. All three figure to be challenged by a Seahawks defense that ranked 10th in passing yards allowed last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Wilson faces a tough challenge in Arizona's Week 3 matchup in San Francisco. Wilson was quiet against Seattle this past Sunday, catching just two of seven targets for 18 yards. However, he was still the Cardinals' second-leading receiver in a game during which QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards. The 49ers have surrendered only 15.6 fantasy points per game to wideouts, the ninth-best mark in the league threw two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Wilson appears to be Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett's favorite wideout target heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Giants. Wilson got a whopping 17 targets this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, recording 11 catches for 89 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Marvin Harrison posted a quiet 3-40-0 line on five targets. Of course, star TE Trey McBride will consistently draw plenty of Brissett's attention, but it looks like Wilson is in line for lots of looks in the team's offense. He could thrive against a Giants defense that is giving up 23.6 fantasy points per game to WRs, ninth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Wilson has settled in atop Arizona's WR depth chart heading into a Week 5 tilt against the Lions. Wilson caught seven passes on 13 targets for 95 yards against the Giants in Week 4, leading or co-leading the Cardinals in all three categories. He's drawn a whopping 30 targets over his past two contests, making it clear that QB Jacoby Brissett sees him as the top option among the team's wideouts. Wilson could be in store for a big game against a Detroit defense that has yielded 28.3 fantasy points per game to wide receivers, third-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Wilson is set to lead Arizona's wideout corps versus the Rams in Week 6. After Marvin Harrison was made inactive this past Sunday due to a pending trade, Wilson functioned as the no-doubt No. 1 WR for the Cardinals but managed just four catches for 30 yards against Detroit. He was outproduced by fellow wideout Kendrick Bourne, who posted a 5-70-0 line, but Wilson should have plenty of chances to thrive with Harrison officially off to Houston. The Rams have given up the fewest receiving yards per game to wideouts this season, but they've also surrendered seven receiving TDs to the position, tied for third-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Wilson has emerged as Arizona's leading wide receiver following Marvin Harrison Jr.'s departure, recording 33 receptions for 320 yards and a touchdown through six games. Wilson has averaged 9.7 yards per reception, and his established role as the team's new WR1 should keep him among Jacoby Brissett's preferred targets alongside star tight end Trey McBride. However, the Cardinals' passing attack has struggled to generate explosive plays, limiting Wilson's weekly ceiling. To make things even more complicated, the Week 7 matchup against the Broncos is far from easy, as Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts in 2026. That, coupled with Brissett's inconsistent play under center, limits Wilson's fantasy appeal considerably in most formats.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.3 targets and 7.6 fantasy points per game during his first 38 NFL games, Wilson broke out with Jacoby Brissett under center during the final eight games of 2025, averaging 11.0 targets and 21.2 fantasy PPG. The stretch also coincided with Marvin Harrison Jr. dealing with health issues, and it's worth noting that Wilson's receiving lines in the four games Harrison was active weren't quite as good (3-40-0, 3-61-0, 4-34-0, 3-36-0). A healthy Harrison (along with TE Trey McBride) figures to lead to a return to earth for Wilson, but the 26-year-old did enough late last season to warrant WR4/flex consideration in drafts.

The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for those matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: RJ Harvey returned from a one-game absence due to a hamstring strain in Week 2 to contribute to the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, gaining just six rushing yards on two carries but producing a 6-41-0 line on seven targets. The second-year back is secure in his role as Denver's top pass-catcher out of the backfield while J.K. Dobbins is the main option on early downs. Rookie Jonah Coleman could challenge both once he's back from IR. Harvey will look to make a bigger impact in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that's already given up 17 catches to RBs this season, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: RJ Harvey is coming off the best performance of his career as a pass catcher, posting a 10-68-0 line on 10 targets while adding 25 rushing yards on seven carries in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers. Denver trailed most of the game, which helped boost the second-year back's usage, but J.K. Dobbins' struggles in the early-down role are also opening the door for Harvey to log more touches in general, as his seven carries were also a season high. The eventual return of rookie Jonah Coleman from a high-ankle sprain could shake up the backfield further, but until then Harvey's arrow appears to be pointed up. He'll look to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs..
outlooksByWeek.6: RJ Harvey all but vanished from the Broncos' game plan in Week 5, gaining seven yards on three carries and failing to catch his only target as Sean Payton returned to play-calling duties. His usage as a pass-catcher was especially disappointing after the second-year back was fed 17 targets over the prior two weeks, turning that volume into a 16-109-0 line. J.K. Dobbins is the preferred early-down option in the backfield, and Harvey's value could become very dependent on game flow as a result. He might see more work in Week 6 if Denver falls behind early against a Seattle team that's in the bottom seven in the league in receptions per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: RJ Harvey found the end zone for the first time in 2026 during the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The second-year running back managed just 56 scrimmage yards on nine touches as he continues to work behind J.K. Dobbins in the backfield. Harvey's target volume has declined since Sean Payton took back play-calling duties, notching only five targets the last two weeks while producing a 3-31-0 line through the air. Harvey will try to reclaim a more consistent role in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dallas Goedert was the leading receiver for the Eagles in Week 1. Goedert snagged four passes for 77 yards and two touchdowns in the 24-22 win over Washington. Goedert was targeted five times. With A.J. Brown no longer in the fold, Goedert could see even more touches in the red zone. In Week 2, the Eagles will face the Tennessee Titans.  Tennessee was a tad frisky against the pass in Week 1, allowing just 215 yards passing to the Jets.  In addition, the Titans did not allow a passing touchdown for the game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dallas Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. Johnny Mundt caught two apsses in Goedert's place, and would be the next man up if Goedert cannot suit up. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dallas Goedert did not suit up last game for the Eagles due to a knee injury, and his status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. In his place, Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt combined for just two catches for 13 yards. Even if Goedert can suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.2 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dallas Goedert missed last game for the Eagles with a knee issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Goedert and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Goedert misses additional time, Zach Ertz would be the next man up.  An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dallas Goedert led the Eagles in targets and receptions last game. Returning from a two-game absence due to a knee injury, Goedert responded with six catches on nine targets. Unfortunately, Goedert gained just 38 yards, and the Eagles lost by a score of 19-17. If both DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley continue to be sidelined due to their respective hamstring injuries, though, Goedert should see plenty of looks, including in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dallas Goedert caught six passes for 61 yards last game for the Eagles. Goedert was second on the team in targets behind DeVonta Smith. Even with Tanner McKee at quarterback for the foreseeable future, Goedert should still have more than ample opportunities. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Goedert enters the 2026 season as the poster boy for inevitable touchdown regression to the mean. After scoring 24 touchdowns in his first seven seasons (3.4 per year), Goedert inexplicably leaped to 11 scores in 15 games in 2025. Goedert's expected TD total was 5.1, and he saw only five end zone targets (12 tight ends saw more). Goedert is a solid fantasy tight end -- he has finished 12th or better in PPG each of the past seven seasons -- but he often misses games (at least two in each of the past six years) and has never finished in the top eight at the position in targets or catches. The 31-year-old is likely to deliver fringe-TE1 numbers in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Coker (ankle) will look to continue shining in Carolina's Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Coker has shown out in the Panthers last two games (including their wild-card loss to end last season), having recorded a combined 17 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He's outproduced 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and looks to be a major part of Carolina's offense going forward. However, Coker is dealing with an ankle issue and could struggle against a tough Falcons defense that gave up just 5.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's favorite targets in Carolina's Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Coker has been incredibly productive, leading the Panthers in receptions (16) and yards (204) while being tied for first in targets (18) through two weeks. Across his last three games (including playoffs), the third-year pro has caught 25 of 30 targets for 338 yards and two touchdowns, emerging as one of the NFL's top young wideouts. He's in for a very favorable matchup in Week 3 as well, as the Browns' defense has surrendered 7.2 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to operate as one of the Panthers' top targets if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Coker has dealt with three separate injuries through three weeks this season (ankle, hamstring and quadriceps). Despite this, the third-year wideout has amassed 222 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 18 catches, leading the Panthers in yards and touchdowns. If Coker is able to suit up in Week 4, he's in for an incredibly favorable matchup, as Detroit's defense has allowed a whopping 31.7 points and 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to the WR position this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to return for the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Coker was on a tear to start the season, catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina's first two games. He's expected to continue benefitting from the new, aggressive Panthers offense, led by Bryce Young, who's averaging 40.5 passing attempts per game this year. Coker will likely find success if active in Week 6 against an Eagles defense that's given up seven touchdowns to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's top targets in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. In Coker's three full games this season, he's caught 22 of 31 targets for 301 yards and two touchdowns. With Young averaging 40.2 passing attempts per game, it appears as if Coker will continue to produce at a high level going forward. Additionally, he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Tampa Bay secondary that's allowed five touchdowns to wideouts through six games this season.

player.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain an important part of the Saints' offense in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Vele saw nine targets in the Week 1 overtime loss, tying his career high and trailing only Chris Olave in the Saints' receiving corps. Vele should continue to benefit from the absence of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) and is expected to see consistent volume until Tyson returns. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup for Vele, however, as the Ravens' defense has given up just 4.8 yards per pass attempt this season, which is tied for the second-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has given up just 15 receptions to WRs through two contests. Vele has clearly positioned himself as one of New Orleans' top receiving options early in the season, catching 12 of 16 targets for 133 yards and one touchdown thus far. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high volume of pass attempts, as Tyler Shough has already thrown the ball 90 times in two games, the second-most in the NFL. Despite this, Vele is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Devaughn Vele is likely to remain the Saints' second option at wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. While Jordan Tyson (hamstring) has been sidelined, Vele has been very fantasy-relevant, catching 15 of 22 targets for 172 yards and a touchdown (12.7 PPR points per game). Vele has almost no competition outside of Chris Olave in the Saints' WR room, which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. Additionally, New Orleans' offense is averaging 44 pass attempts per game, which suggests Vele will continue having scoring opportunities. He's in for a favorable Week 4 matchup, as Atlanta's defense has allowed 604 receiving yards to wideouts this season, the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain very involved in the Saints' offensive game plan in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Vele has been targeted 30 times (second-most on the team) through New Orleans' first four contests this season, logging 226 receiving yards and a pair of touchdowns. With Tyler Shough averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game this season, Vele will likely remain a solid fantasy option as the year progresses, at least until the return of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR). However, Vele is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 7.7 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Vele was quiet in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for just 26 yards. He still ranks second on the Saints in targets (36) and receiving yards (252) through five contests, which is a positive sign for his outlook moving forward. Vele could thrive in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's already allowed five touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain New Orleans' No. 2 wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Vele has been relatively quiet over the last two weeks, catching seven of 12 targets for 68 yards. Despite this, he's played over 90% of the Saints' offensive snaps in the last two contests, suggesting more fantasy production is coming soon, especially if New Orleans continues throwing the ball at such a high clip (39.2 pass attempts per game -- fourth-most in the NFL). Vele could struggle against a strong Steelers defense in Week 7 though, as they've allowed just 6.1 yards per pass attempt this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Vele is expected to open the season as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave until Jordyn Tyson returns from injury near midseason. Vele's first season with the Saints was marred with injuries. The 2024 seventh-round pick, who posted a 41-475-3 receiving line with Denver as a rookie, barely played throughout most of 2025 prior to taking on an every-down role during Weeks 10-15. In those five games (one of which he left hurt), he averaged 5.6 targets per game, but reached 12.0 fantasy points once (an 8-93-1 effort in Week 13 against Miami). The 28-year-old has yet to show he can be relied on for consistent targets and fantasy production, but he'll play an every-down role early on, which makes him a sleeper for flex value in deep leagues. He'll be worth a roster spot until Tyson returns.

outlooksByWeek.3: Emanuel Wilson will look to build upon a big performance when Seattle faces Washington in Week 3. With Jadarian Price suffering a shoulder injury against Arizona on Sunday, Wilson stepped up and led the Seahawks with 21 rushes for 92 yards. Price's injury isn't considered serious, but it's not certain that he'll be able to return to action in Week 3. Whoever leads Seattle's backfield will be looking to score the first rushing touchdown against the Commanders this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emanuel Wilson may be moving into a timeshare at running back for Seattle heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. An early fumble by rookie Jadarian Price was partly responsible for Wilson leading the Seahawks with nine carries in a Week 3 win over Washington, with Price logging just five totes and George Holani three. With that said, Wilson managed a paltry 14 yards on his carries, so he didn't exactly make a loud statement in a bid for more work. The Chargers just gave up 154 rushing yards to Buffalo's James Cook in Week 3, so they could be vulnerable on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.5: Emanuel Wilson will look to build upon a big Week 4 performance when Seattle faces San Francisco in Week 5. Wilson led his team's backfield this past Sunday against the Chargers, posting a 21-81-1 line on the ground. Equally promising was his 3-39-1 line as a pass catcher after he logged zero receptions over the first three weeks of the campaign. With Jadarian Price (chest) on IR, Wilson figures to continue to work as Seattle's No. 1 RB, though the eventual return of Zach Charbonnet (knee) could shake up the backfield. Charbonnet isn't expected to be ready for Week 5, however, so Wilson will likely get plenty of work against the 49ers, who are middle-of-the-pack so far in giving up 17.4 fantasy points per game to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emanuel Wilson will look to get into the end zone for a third straight game when the Seahawks travel to Denver in Week 6. Wilson has emerged as Seattle's clear top RB over the past two weeks, registering 41 carries for 142 yards and two touchdowns on the ground along with five catches for 50 yards and another score through the air in that span. He figures to continue working as the team's No. 1 RB at least until one or both of Zach Charbonnet (knee) or Jadarian Price (chest) is able to return, but that won't happen in Week 6. The Broncos have been vulnerable against the run this season, surrendering 4.51 yards per carry to running backs (eighth-worst in the league).
outlooksByWeek.7: Emanuel Wilson and the Seahawks play host to the Chiefs for a Week 7 clash on Sunday Night Football. He had 14 carries for 52 yards and failed to catch his only target during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. It was an underwhelming performance for Wilson, who had scored three touchdowns over his previous two outings. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) practicing and likely to make his 2026 season debut in Week 7, it's probably best to avoid the Seahawks backfield versus Kansas City's defense that's tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kirk Cousins had a bumpy Raiders debut in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, completing 21 of 30 passes for 160 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions. The veteran quarterback is just keeping the starting job warm for 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but the team is in no hurry to get the rookie in the lineup before he's ready, and wins will only give Cousins more job security. His passing numbers could improve once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to play, as his most productive connection was running back Ashton Jeanty, who was on the other end of two of Cousins' TD passes. Cousins will face a Chargers defense in Week 2 that had trouble slowing down Jacoby Brissett in its opener but finished fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kirk Cousins is having a late-season renaissance with the Raiders. The 38-year-old quarterback has thrown exactly three touchdown passes in each of the first three games of the season, leading his new team to a 3-0 record and keeping first overall pick Fernando Mendoza firmly on the bench. Cousins has also thrown three INTs, and those mistakes could catch up against tougher competition, as two of those victories have come against the NFL's five remaining winless squads. On the other hand, that production came despite Brock Bowers missing the first two weeks, and the star tight end erupted for a 10-116-1 line in his Week 3 debut. Cousins will get his first real test of the year in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kirk Cousins went down swinging in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, setting season highs with 52 pass attempts and 365 yards while throwing multiple TDs for a fourth straight game to begin the season. While rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza waits in the wings, Cousins' 11 touchdowns are tied for the league lead, and he sits just outside the top 10 in passing yards and completion rate, which should give him plenty of job security. The veteran quarterback will try to keep rolling in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that is tied for ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kirk Cousins' production is declining, potentially reducing his time as the Raiders' starting quarterback. After throwing for nine touchdowns during the team's 3-0 start to the season, the veteran has a 3:1 TD:INT over the last two contests, both losses. During a lopsided Week 5 loss to the Patriots, Cousins ceded the final drive to prized rookie Fernando Mendoza, which could be the first step toward Mendoza taking the reins. Cousins' job doesn't seem to be in immediate peril, and he could bounce back in a big way in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kirk Cousins is coming off a productive effort in the Raiders' near-upset of the Bills in Week 6, throwing for over 300 yards for the second time in six games and tossing multiple TDs for the fifth time. The veteran quarterback is on pace for his first 4,000-yard, 30-TD campaign since 2021 with the Vikings, but to reach those numbers he would need to keep first overall pick Fernando Mendoza on the bench, which looks increasingly unlikely after three straight losses for Las Vegas. Cousins will remain under center for now, but he faces another tough test in Week 7 against a Rams defense that is second in the league in passing yards per game allowed.

player.seasonOutlook: Cousins signed with the Raiders and will work as the team's starter to open the 2026 season ahead of No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza. Cousins made eight starts for Atlanta last season and was not much of a fantasy option, averaging 12.5 fantasy points per game while reaching 18 points only once. The 38-year-old will be a bridge starter at best until Mendoza is ready and is no longer a threat with his legs (7 yards on 14 carries last season). He won't be a fantasy option, even when on the field. He should only be drafted late in superflex leagues.

outlooksByWeek.7: Tanner McKee started last game at quarterback for the Eagles, and he could potentially find himself under center for the foreseeable future. Starter Jalen Hurts will be sidelined for the remainder of the season due to blood clots, leaving McKee as next in line under center. He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown last game versus the Panthers. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep it rolling in Detroit's Week 2 matchup at Buffalo. Gibbs was the bell cow managers hoped for in Week 1 against the Saints, logging 29 rushes for 156 yards, two touchdowns and catching all five of his targets for 30 yards. He'll also face a Bills defense that fared badly against the ground game in their season opener, allowing Gibbs' former teammate David Montgomery to total 79 yards and three touchdowns off 23 touches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to keep things rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Gibbs finished with huge numbers once again in Week 2, but most of his output came from six catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The superstar running back has seen high volume so far, with 56 touches for 299 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to his name this season. He'll face a Jets defense that's been tough against the run in its first two games, but New York hasn't faced anyone of Gibbs' caliber.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his touchdown tear alive as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Gibbs was a beast once again in Week 3 against the Jets, turning 20 carries into 99 yards and two touchdowns, as well as catching the ball six times for 65 yards and another touchdown. The fourth-year star has now found the end zone six times across three games, and he's totaled 463 yards from scrimmage. He'll face a Panthers defense that's allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to return to dominance as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Gibbs produced for fantasy managers in Week 4, but he still rushed 15 times for a season-low 46 yards with a touchdown, tacking on four catches for 31 yards. Either way, the superstar running back has found the end zone in every game this season, and he's surpassed 100 total yards in three of four games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top five against fantasy RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to come out of the bye week with a bang as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Gibbs was a monster in Week 5 against the Cardinals, rushing 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns, with five catches for 56 yards as well. The premier running back has now surpassed 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season, and he's found the end zone nine times across five games. He'll face a Green Bay front that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three campaigns. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with David Montgomery no longer in the mix. The 24-year-old Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey McBride marches into a Week 2 matchup versus Seattle fresh off a strong season-opening performance in Arizona's victory against the Chargers. McBride led Cardinals pass catchers across the board with nine catches, 13 targets and 95 yards in that win, and he scored the team's lone passing touchdown. The All-Pro is essentially matchup-proof as possibly the league's premier tight end, though he'll draw a tough Seahawks defense in Week 2. However, it's worth noting that Seattle gave up the sixth-most receiving yards to tight ends during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey McBride remains one of the most matchup-proof pass catchers in the league heading into the Cardinals' Week 3 tilt versus San Francisco. Though QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards in a loss to Seattle on Sunday, McBride accounted for 41 of those yards and got into the end zone. Through two weeks, McBride leads NFL tight ends with 17 receptions and ranks fourth with 136 receiving yards. The 49ers have been tough on the position so far, though, giving up just seven catches for 52 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trey McBride will look to continue a strong start to the campaign when the Cardinals face the Giants in Week 4. McBride posted a 9-75-0 receiving line in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. The All-Pro has now logged at least eight catches and at least 10 targets in every contest so far in 2026, giving him the highest floor of any TE in the NFL. The Giants rank in the bottom 10 leaguewide in catch rate and receiving yards allowed to tight ends, so they don't figure to be a threat to McBride's run of success.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trey McBride enters Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit coming off his quietest performance of the season. While the star tight end logged a healthy 12 targets and seven catches against the Giants in Week 4, he finished with just 31 receiving yards. It's a testament to McBride's excellence that such a stat line represents a downturn by his standards, and he'll have a good chance of bouncing back against the Lions. Detroit has allowed a whopping 19.2 fantasy points per game to tight ends so far this season, by far the most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trey McBride will look to remain productive for Arizona's offense in Week 6 against the Rams. McBride put up another big line against Detroit this past Sunday, catching nine of 10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end leads all NFL players with 42 receptions this season, and only Amon-Ra St. Brown (57) has more targets than McBride's 56. That should mean McBride gets plenty of opportunities against the Rams, but to find success he'll have to overcome a defense that is giving up the fewest fantasy points per game (3.2) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Trey McBride remains Arizona's most dependable receiving weapon, compiling 49 receptions for 361 yards and three touchdowns through six games. His 49 catches lead the Cardinals by a wide margin, and his consistent involvement provides a strong PPR foundation despite the team's struggles to generate explosive plays, as he has had at least seven catches in each of his six appearances to date. McBride also led Arizona's passing attack during its Week 6 victory over the Rams, reinforcing his importance to Jacoby Brissett. He faces a relatively neutral matchup against Denver in Week 7, with the Broncos allowing 8.2 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs in 2026, the 15th-best mark in the league. Given his involvement on offense, however, McBride should remain a reliable TE1 regardless of the opponent.

player.seasonOutlook: McBride has emerged as one of the league's top pass catchers -- not just tight ends -- as he trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons and is sixth in receiving yards (2,385). McBride led the tight end position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025, and his league-high 15 top-12 fantasy weeks were six more than any other player at the position. He finished third in the NFL with 17 end zone targets. McBride really thrived when Jacoby Brissett (21.1 PPG) replaced Kyler Murray (12.5) under center, which only adds to his 2026 appeal. The 26-year-old should be on your radar at the first-/second-round turn.

outlooksByWeek.2: Garrett Wilson should maintain steady volume for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. He garnered seven targets in a run-heavy situation to open the year, catching six for 79 yards. Green Bay's secondary is suspect and just allowed Vikings' top receiver Justin Jefferson to score twice, despite Carson Wentz being under center. The Jets will likely need to throw more in Week 2, potentially pushing Wilson into double-digit targets and setting him up for elevated numbers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Garrett Wilson's clear lead role in the Jets' passing game could pay dividends against a porous Lions secondary in Week 3. Wilson has registered seven targets in each of the Jets' first two outings, giving him ample opportunity to exploit a defense that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts through two weeks. The Lions' defense is vulnerable to all positions, but Wilson's spot as the top target is unchallenged.
outlooksByWeek.4: Garrett Wilson likely remains a heavily targeted option for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears. Wilson is coming off a terrific 10-catch, 107-yard Week 3 where he scored his first touchdown of the season and faces minimal competition for volume in the Jets' passing game. Chicago's secondary has rallied over the last two weeks, not allowing more than 153 yards through the air, but the pieces at corner leave plenty to be desired, setting Wilson up to take advantage of continued high looks in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Garrett Wilson seeks a rebound in Week 5 when the Jets face the Browns. After collecting seven or more targets in each of his first three games, Wilson bottomed out with only four looks in Week 4, finishing with a season-low 27 yards. Cleveland's secondary has allowed at least 291 passing yards in each of the last two weeks, and three opposing wideouts have topped 70 yards. With his usual volume, Wilson appears to be in a favorable Week 5 spot.
outlooksByWeek.6: Garrett Wilson commands a heavy volume of targets in the Jets' passing game heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Wilson collected 11 looks in Week 5, topping 100 yards for the second time this season, and has now garnered at least seven targets in four of five outings. New England's secondary is banged up, and the availability of star CB Christian Gonzalez remains uncertain. While the Jets don't want to pass heavily, when they do, targets should be funneled toward Wilson. He has a great chance to exploit a defense that has allowed two 100-yard receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Garrett Wilson plays a steady role in the Jets' middling passing game and enters a Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. Wilson managed just 44 yards in Week 6, his second-lowest output of the year, but still enters Week 7 with seven or more targets in four of his first six games. Miami has been stingy against wideouts, allowing just two touchdown catches and only two receivers to record more than 55 yards, but Wilson's volume should allow him to flirt with the upper end of that production.

player.seasonOutlook: Wilson is eyeing a bounce-back following an injury-shortened 2025 that limited him to seven games. It was the first time Wilson had missed time, having appeared in all 51 games during his first three seasons. The 2022 first-round pick ranked no lower than sixth among receivers in targets in each of those years, but he failed to produce a fantasy campaign better than 20th (PPG) due to New York's quarterback woes. Wilson was off to a hot start last season (four TDs, 14.2 fantasy PPG) thanks to a massive 33% target share (second highest). New York's signal-caller problems still aren't completely solved, but veteran Geno Smith should provide an upgrade over last year's Justin Fields/Tyrod Taylor duo. Wilson, 26, is one of the best raw talents at the position and should be valued as a good WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Skattebo showed no ill effects from last season's injury in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in he stunning 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys. With the Giants poised to possess the ball and feed the running game under new coach John Harbaugh, Skattebo should continue to be in line for a heavy workload. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Skattebo managed just 55 yards from scrimmage last game for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, teams will likely gameplan to stop the run, which starts with Skattebo. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Skattebo racked up 100 yards from scrimmage in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Skattebo took 20 carries for 60 yards while also catching three passes for 40 yards out of the backfield. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely on the running game led by Skattebo in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Skattebo has struggled to find room to roam for the Giants thus far this season. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 58 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals last game. He is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston. In Week 5, Skattebo will face a rather stingy Washington run defense as well. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Skattebo was mostly a non-factor last game against the Commanders, at least until the end of a wild contest which resulted in a tie. Skattebo managed 40 of his 71 scrimmage yards in overtime, though coughed up the ball as the Giants were in field goal range to potentially win the game. Skattebo would have truly been the goat for this contest had Washington not botched the final seconds of overtime. Skattebo has had 60 rushing yards or less in four-straight games, and has failed to score since the opener. However, in Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cam Skattebo had zero touches last game for the Giants. One week after losing a key fumble, Skattebo was removed from his starting job as the Giants backfield devolved into a four-man committee. Tyrone Tracy was the team's most productive back, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown, but managed just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches and Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries. Skattebo could return to a more significant role in Week 7 against the Texans, but it will be hard to trust any New York running back until one emerges from the pack. Houston is also allowing just 83 rushing yards per contest, which is third in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Skattebo is a Year 2 breakout candidate following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season. The fourth-round pick first played a significant offensive role in Week 2 and went on to average 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards while scoring six TDs during his six full games. His 19.1 fantasy points per game during the span would've ranked sixth over the full season. The 24-year-old enters 2026 with a new coach (John Harbaugh) and playcaller (Matt Nagy), but his competition for touches are Najee Harris and the same guys he beat out for work in 2025 (Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary). Assuming his ankle heals up as expected, Skattebo will be on the RB2 radar with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. He sat out Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, and it looks like he's in real jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Colts in a battle between 2-2 teams in Week 5. He missed his second consecutive game with a toe injury sustained in Week 2. Jaylen Warren accounted for 20 of 22 touches by running backs during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, a pattern that would surely continue if Dowdle remains sidelined against Indianapolis. Monitor his practice participation leading up to a favorable matchup versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (24.2) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to face off with the Buccaneers in Week 6. After sitting out the last three games with a toe injury, it appears Dowdle is ready to make his return against the 1-4 Bucs. He was brought to Pittsburgh to form a dynamic one-two punch alongside Jaylen Warren, but the incumbent starter has excelled as the featured player out of the backfield, particularly over the last three weeks. Assuming Dowdle takes the field in Week 6, he's likely to work as the clear backup to Warren, so it's best he remains on fantasy benches versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to Paris for a Week 7 meeting with the Saints. He returned from a three-game absence due to a toe injury and registered seven carries for 40 yards and three catches on four targets for nine yards during Pittsburgh's overtime win in Week 6. Dowdle played just 28% of snaps on offense as he works his way back into game shape, and he was pretty effective in limited action, so his workload should rise steadily in Week 7. Jaylen Warren started and earned 16 touches to Dowdle's 10, and there's a good chance they'll both be heavily involved versus a New Orleans defense that ranks dead-last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Addison will look to record his first reception of the year as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Addison ran the second-most routes for Minnesota in Week 1 against the Packers, but he was unable to convert on either of his two targets. Veteran quarterback Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion), relied more on tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver behind Justin Jefferson. This could make Addison's role remains small as long as Wentz remains under center. With that being said, the Bears' defense did allow the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Addison will seek to ramp things up as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Addison bounced back from a zero-catch performance in Week 1 this past Sunday, logging two catches for 21 yards against the Bears. Still, his output is nowhere near sufficient for fantasy owners, especially since he's put up WR2 numbers many times throughout the last three seasons. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers this season, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Addison will look to build off a big game as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Addison saw an uptick in looks after the departure of Justin Jefferson (ankle) in Week 3, finishing the win with five catches for 90 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. While Jefferson very well could return to the field in the coming week, Addison did prove to be a solid option for Kyler Murray. Addison has proven to be an asset for Minnesota alongside Jefferson when being thrown to by a competent quarterback, which could be showcased even against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Addison will aim to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Addison logged just four catches for 52 yards in Week 4 against the Dolphins, which was a bit of a disappointment given that Justin Jefferson (ankle) was inactive. Quarterback Kyler Murray also seemed to have built a connection with T.J. Hockenson against Miami, making it less likely that Addison will produce when Jefferson inevitably returns. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Addison will aim to make a return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Addison missed Week 5 against the Saints with a hamstring injury, but he luckily had a bye week of rest. The fourth-year wideout will now need to return to practice if he hopes to suit up in Minnesota's upcoming home game. He'll face an Indianapolis defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing with a 70-911-10 receiving line on 108 targets as a rookie in 2023, Addison has seen his target, reception, yardage and touchdown totals decrease each of the last two seasons. A few missed games were partially to blame for the dips, but Minnesota's quarterback woes were the main culprit in 2025, as Addison went from 10 TDs and a 65% catch rate in both 2023 and 2024 to three TDs and a 53% catch rate last season. Addison already has a pair of top-25 fantasy campaigns to his name, but it may be a stretch for him to get there in 2026 with Kyler Murray leading the Minnesota offense, not to mention Jauan Jennings' addition to the lineup. The 24-year-old is best valued as WR4/flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Khalil Shakir will look to remain Josh Allen's security blanket in Week 2 when the Bills host the Lions. Shakir managed four grabs on six targets to open the season, finishing with 50 yards. He operated underneath while newly acquired DJ Moore stretched the field. The Lions' vulnerable secondary gave up 410 yards passing in Week 1, but Shakir will likely be limited by shorter routes, creating a safe but uninspiring fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Khalil Shakir remains a steady, stable cog in Buffalo's passing game entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Shakir logged six targets in each of the Bills' first two games but hasn't topped 50 yards or scored. Shakir didn't take on an elevated role in Week 2 following DJ Moore's (shoulder) early exit, but he faces a secondary that allowed 75 yards to Kendrick Bourne and 119 yards to Tre Tucker, and both operate in a similar slot role to Shakir.
outlooksByWeek.4: Khalil Shakir seeks more opportunities in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Despite a season-high 71% snap share in Week 3, Shakir had his lowest output of 2026, catching just a six-yard pass on three targets in a game where Josh Allen struggled. Shakir could benefit from additional looks in Week 4 if DJ Moore is matched up consistently with CB Christian Gonzalez. Operating primarily out of the slot tempers high yardage totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Khalil Shakir maintains a steady role out of the slot for Buffalo as they prepare to face the Rams in Week 5. Shakir is coming off a season-high 82 yards in Week 4, his third game with at least six targets. His workload is independent of DJ Moore's shoulder status. Shakir will either garner more targets if Moore is out, or benefit from the attention Moore usually draws. However, the Rams defense hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, suggesting Shakir is a risky floor and limited ceiling option.
outlooksByWeek.6: Khalil Shakir continues to play a minimal role in the Bills' passing game as they enter a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Shakir had just three targets in Week 5, the second time he's experienced that limited volume in three weeks despite the continued absence of DJ Moore (shoulder). Shakir is averaging a career-best 14.2 yards per catch and with Las Vegas proving vulnerable over the middle (nine catches, 122 yards, two touchdowns last week to DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism), Shakir could exploit a favorable matchup despite a lack of heavy volume.

player.seasonOutlook: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a tough Week 2 matchup against the Ravens, whose defense gave up just 12.7 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1.
