Despite a poor first half, Shough threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns in last week's overtime loss, making him the league's leading passer. However, Shough was prone to turnovers, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble, which is something Baltimore could capitalize on. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup, as the Ravens allowed just 166 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Shough has been one of the NFL's most productive QBs through two weeks, leading the league in passing yards (662) while producing five total touchdowns. Despite throwing the ball 90 times in his first two contests, Shough remains one of the league leaders in completion percentage (68.9 percent). He's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, however, with the Raiders' allowing just one passing touchdowns this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Shough is expected lead the Saints' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14 points to the Packers in Week 3. Shough continued his stretch of impressive play in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, throwing for 255 yards, four touchdowns and an interception. Head coach Kellen Moore continues to put his faith in Shough, as the Saints' are throwing the ball 44 times per game through three weeks. Expect Shough to remain one of fantasy's best quarterbacks in Week 4 against a Falcons defense that's given up 21.6 fantasy points per game to the position this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Shough is expected to lead the Saints' offense into the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Despite a loss in Week 4, Shough remained productive, throwing for 286 yards and a touchdown with no turnovers. The second-year pro is now averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game, suggesting he'll remain productive for fantasy purposes as the season progresses. Despite this, he's in for a very tough Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 15.7 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Shough is expected to remain productive in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Shough had his worst performance of the season in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, completing just 16 of 25 pass attempts for 96 yards and two interceptions. Despite this, he currently ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards (1,299) through five games, attempting a league-leading 205 pass attempts. He could definitely bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's given up 22.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Shough will look to stay hot in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Shough was very productive in the Week 6 win over the Giants, accounting for just 176 total yards but scoring four touchdowns (three passing, one rushing). Despite attempting just 30 passes in last week's win, Shough is still averaging the third-most pass attempts per game in the NFL (39.2) through six weeks. Shough could struggle against a tough Steelers defense in Week 7, as they have allowed just 16.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this year.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the surprise second-half breakout players of 2025, Shough scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of his nine full games, including six straight to end the season. The 2025 second-round pick was a solid producer with his arm (250.1 passing yards per game) and his legs (19.3 rushing yards per game and three TDs). Shough didn't show a high ceiling (he never reached 22 fantasy points in a game), though that can be traced to a shaky supporting cast. That's an area that should be better in 2026 with Travis Etienne Jr. and No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) joining the team. He's still unproven, but Shough enters Year 2 (same as coach Kellen Moore) as an intriguing fantasy breakout candidate. He's worth a look in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Washington hopes for more efficiency when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Washington recorded a healthy eight targets in the team's opener, and while 17.7 yards per catch is encouraging, he caught only three balls. Washington has value as a returner in some leagues, and passing volume will likely remain high with Miami forced to throw from behind in the second half. Even so, Week 2's matchup against a defense that held more talented receivers to just 6.4 yards per target in their opener is a risky endeavor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Washington brings steady volume ahead of the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. With Malik Willis under center, Miami has completed just 29 passes through two games, but seven have gone to Washington, who's averaging 6.5 targets. Kansas City's rebuilt secondary has been terrific through two games, allowing just 204 yards to opposing wideouts. Washington seems unlikely to produce any massive numbers, but he also appears to be a steady cog in this limited offense, keeping him on WR3/Flex radars.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Washington remains heavily involved in the Dolphins' low-profile passing game heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. Washington is coming off of a season-high 10 targets in Week 3, and has collected three rushing attempts over the last two weeks while also being involved in kickoff returns, but he's yet to top 61 rushing/receiving yards per game or score. Washington's workload creates a viable floor, and Minnesota is allowing a healthy 8.2 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Washington's volume continues to be steady for the Dolphins as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. He hauled in five of QB Malik WIllis' nine completions in Week 4, his fourth-straight week with at least five targets while increasing his yardage in each of the last three outings. Cincinnati's secondary hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 63 yards, and while Washington's workload shouldn't be questioned, his potential remains capped by Miami's low-scoring offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Washington brings a steady workload but limited yardage potential into the Dolphins' Week 7 matchup with the Jets. Washington has commanded at least five targets in all five games, three times reaching eight or more, but has topped out at 67 yards, operating mainly on short, slot routes while Miami struggles to find a vertical passing game. The Jets are allowing just 7.3 yards per target; Washington too is averaging 7.3 yards per target, setting him up for a rather predictable Week 7 outing where he'll need a heavy target share to offer anything more than bye-week replacement scoring.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was a sixth-round flier back in 2024, but that didn't stop him from working his way into a substantial offensive role last season. Washington finished third on the Dolphins in targets, trailing only Jaylen Waddle and De'Von Achane. Of course, Miami's shaky group of offensive personnel was an obvious factor and Washington's efficiency wasn't very good (5.0 yards per target, 7.0 yards per reception, 0.9 yards per route run). The 25-year-old is fine as a short-range target and occasional rusher, but that's likely his ceiling with newcomers Jalen Tolbert, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr. expected to factor in at wide receiver.

The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Flournoy managed two catches for 22 yards on four targets in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Flournoy finished fourth on the team in targets for the game. The Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Flournoy tied for the second on the Cowboys in targets last game. Flournoy saw eight balls thrown his way, though managed just two catches in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Flournoy also gained just 22 yards for the game; in fact, he has yet to gain more than 25 yards in any contest in 2026. In Week 4, Dallas faces a Houston defense that has been surprisingly subpar against the pass.  The Texans are allowing 238.7 passing yards per clash, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ryan Flournoy has been targeted at least four times in every game this season for the Cowboys. However, he has yet to cross 40 yards receiving in any contest. Versus the Texans, he had four catches but only for a season-high 37 yards. With a lot of mouths to feed like CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and even tight end Jake Ferguson, Flournoy's output may continue to be depressed. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league. Flournoy is still looking for his first score of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ryan Flournoy set a season high in receiving yardage last game for the Cowboys. Flournoy brought in three passes for 90 yards in the 24-16 loss to the Bucs. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to Flournoy's success. However, Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Flournoy back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ryan Flournoy found the end zone last game for Dallas. Flournoy reeled in seven passes for 40 yards and the score in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Flournoy has at least four targets in every game this season, though has gone over 40 yards receiving just once. He remains firmly behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens heading into a Week 7 clash with Philly. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.7: Christian Kirk and the 49ers hope to improve to 7-0 when they visit Atlanta in Week 7. The veteran receiver has been on the reserve/PUP list to begin 2026 due to a calf injury and has yet to suit up for San Francisco. The 49ers opened Kirk's practice window on Oct. 15 and there were reports of him possibly being activated for Week 6, but that was indeed not the case. With Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to miss the road clash against the Falcons, San Francisco could really use Kirk's presence on the field.

player.seasonOutlook: Kirk signed with the 49ers after spending his first eight seasons with Arizona, Jacksonville and Houston. The 2018 second-round pick peaked with a 12th-place finish in fantasy points in 2022, but that marks his only career top-25 finish and he's been way off the fantasy radar the last two seasons, partially due to injury woes (13 missed games). Kirk doesn't have a clear path to consistent targets in San Francisco, with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling also in the mix (not to mention Christian McCaffrey and eventually George Kittle). The 29-year-old will begin the season on IR and is not on the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.6: Roschon Johnson could be in line for another solid workday in Week 6 as the Bears play the Falcons. Johnson got solid opportunities in Chicago's Week 5 blowout loss to Green Bay, with Kyle Monangai out with a toe injury, rushing the ball five times for six yards and reeling in five of seven targets for 34 yards. Johnson's receiving upside could keep him relevant again if Monangai remains sidelined. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 21st in receiving yards allowed to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Roschon Johnson could be in line for another solid workday again in Week 7 as the Bears play the Patriots. Johnson capitalized on his usage once again with Kyle Monangai (toe) sidelined in Week 6, rushing 13 times for 51 yards and a touchdown and catching two passes for 34 yards. He's now totaled 125 yards and a touchdown on 27 touches in the last two games with Monangai out. If this stays the case, Johnson will be playable against a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Baker Mayfield will look to rebound from a tough Week 1 performance in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Mayfield threw for 216 yards while adding a rushing touchdown last week, but he fumbled three times and struggled to finish drives. He should be in for a very favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 28.3 fantasy points to quarterbacks and four passing touchdowns in Week 1. If Mayfield isn't able to respond with a solid fantasy performance in a clear revenge game, there could be doubts about his reliability moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Baker Mayfield is set for a difficult Week 3 matchup when the Buccaneers take on the Vikings, whose defense has allowed 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Mayfield has really struggled during Tampa Bay's first two contests, accounting for just two touchdowns while turning the ball over four times. He's thrown for just 184.5 passing yards per game while completing 71 percent of his passes. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 3 matchup, with Minnesota's defense giving up just 12.5 points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Baker Mayfield (thumb) will operate as the Buccaneers' signal caller if active for the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Mayfield has been sidelined for Tampa Bay's last three contests, but head coach Todd Bowles told reporters he's "supposed to practice" Wednesday, suggesting he could return Sunday. Before the injury, Mayfield struggled in his first three games, throwing for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while also losing three fumbles. However, he could bounce back against a Panthers defense that's allowed 22.0 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayfield is back for Year 4 as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He has put together three consecutive top-12 fantasy campaigns, though his 2025 season (12th in total points, but 19th in points per game) was a big step back from 2024 (fourth overall and per game). Mayfield tossed 26 touchdowns (way down from 41 in 2024) and severely lacked upside, managing only four top-10 fantasy weeks. Granted, the 31-year-old was not fully healthy throughout the season and did still finish in the top 10 at the position in key categories, including passing yards, passing TDs and rushing yards. With a solid supporting cast and Zac Robinson as playcaller, Mayfield has some rebound potential and does just enough with his legs to make him an appealing QB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will likely have Drew Lock throwing balls to him when Seattle faces Arizona in Week 2. Lock took over for an injured Sam Darnold (glute) in the Seahawks' season-opening win, and Darnold is expected to miss Week 2. However, the QB change didn't impact Smith-Njigba's stat line in Week 1, as he finished with eight catches for 122 yards and a touchdown. He's as matchup-proof a WR as there is in the NFL, and he's set to take on a Cardinals defense that allowed Ladd McConkey (ribs) to put up a 5-82-1 line in less than a full game during a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba enters Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington riding the wave of a three-touchdown performance. That effort came Sunday versus Arizona, when the star wideout also caught nine passes for 155 yards. Smith-Njigba worked with backup QB Drew Lock in that victory due to Sam Darnold being sidelined with a glute injury, and it seems that the reigning AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year is more than capable up dominating regardless of who is throwing him the ball. Smith-Njigba could be in for another huge effort against a Commanders defense that has surrendered the 10th-most receiving yards (337) to wideouts through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off another huge game as Seattle prepares to host the Chargers in Week 4. Versus Washington in Week 3, Smith-Njigba recorded 10 catches on 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns. The star receiver has logged at least eight catches, 120 yards and one score in each of his first three games this season, making him among fantasy's most valuable assets once again. The Chargers don't figure to be able to contain Smith-Njigba given that they're allowing 9.76 yards per target to wideouts, fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaxon Smith-Njigba should once again be the centerpiece of Seattle's passing game in a big Week 5 clash against the 49ers. The star wideout posted a fine 5-76-0 receiving line against the Chargers this past Sunday, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. It's telling that despite his final stats being quite adequate, Smith-Njigba's targets, catches and yards were each a season-low mark in what has been a standout campaign thus far. San Francisco is allowing just 6.96 yards per target to wideouts though four weeks (fifth-best in the league), though Smith-Njigba has proven to be essentially matchup-proof since the beginning of last season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is arguably the most matchup-proof wideout in the NFL, but he could be challenged in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Smith-Njigba caught five of eight targets for 102 yards and a touchdown against San Francisco in a loss this past Sunday. He's now recorded at least 100 receiving yards and one touchdown in four of his five games this season, and Smith-Njigba leads the league with 583 receiving yards. He'll be matched up Week 6 against a Broncos defense that has allowed the third-lowest catch rate (54.5%) to wideouts, but Smith-Njigba figures to get a big boost by not having to face star cornerback Patrick Surtain, who is expected to miss the contest due to an ankle injury.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks return home for a Week 7 interconference clash against the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. He corralled 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6, setting season highs in receptions and targets. Smith-Njigba paced his team in all receiving categories despite a quiet first half, and he now owns a 49-717-7 line on 65 targets through six outings. Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs will try to make it tough on the 2025 Offensive Player of the Year.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, Smith-Njigba is fresh off a breakout season in which he paced all receivers in target share (36%), receiving yards (1,793), air yards (1,858) and yards per route run (3.8), while finishing no lower than fourth in targets, catches, touchdowns and fantasy points. JSN delivered top-10 fantasy weeks 10 times throughout 2025 and scored at least 13 points in 16 of 17 games. The 24-year-old is just now entering his prime and remains well positioned to handle one-third of the targets in Seattle's Sam Darnold-led offense. Smith-Njigba is an elite fantasy option who should be off the board in the early-to-middle part of Round 1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 showdown versus the Texans. He rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a TD and brought in five of six targets for another 22 yards during Cincinnati's Week 1 victory over Tampa Bay. Brown is the clear-cut lead back on a high-powered offense, and he should continue to see a hefty workload on the ground and in the passing game. However, Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, so consider this a less-than-favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to battle their division rivals in Week 3. He tallied 20 carries for 80 yards and corralled three of five targets for two yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win. Brown handled 23 of 26 touches out of the backfield, and he should continue to dominate those looks again in Week 3. The Steelers' defense ranks 26th in fantasy points allowed (27.5) to RBs after giving up 136 rushing yards and 4.9 yards per carry to the Patriots in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town for an AFC clash in Week 4. He rushed 13 times for 61 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. It was a quiet afternoon for Brown, with his 15 total touches well below his average of 22 accrued over his first two outings. He'll face another stout defensive unit, as Jacksonville ranks seventh in fantasy points (17.2) and fourth in rushing yards allowed (57.7) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase Brown and the Bengals visit the 0-4 Dolphins for a Week 5 showdown. He had nine carries for 10 yards but caught all 11 of his targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. Brown set a career high in receptions with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) leaving in the first half, and with Tee Higgins (adductor) picking up a questionable tag, the running back could again get high volume through the air while still handling the bulk of carries. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) and receiving TDs (4) allowed to the position, giving Brown a very favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase Brown and the Bengals are on the road for a divisional clash against the Ravens in Week 7. He registered 13 carries for 39 yards and caught three of four targets for 21 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Brown took a backseat to Samaje Perine, who had 14 carries for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a touchdown. Over his last two outings, he's rushed 22 times for 49 yards, a miserable 2.2 yards per carry. Next up is another difficult matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 18.6 fantasy points per game (7th) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown is entering his fourth NFL season and third as Cincinnati's lead back. His 2025 season got off to a rocky start (10.1 fantasy points per game and one touchdown during his first seven games), but it turned around drastically down the stretch (21.2 points per game and 10 TDs during his final 10 games). The improvement coincided with Cincinnati's improved QB play, which should continue into 2026 with a healthy Joe Burrow. Brown has yet to finish a season higher than 16th in carries or rushing yards, but he has scored exactly 11 TDs and has finished fifth in receptions in each of the past two years, both of which have resulted in top-10 fantasy campaigns. The 26-year-old once again has minimal competition for touches in a very good Bengals offense. He's best valued as a fringe RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jeremiyah Love's second NFL game for the Cardinals will be a tough Week 2 matchup against Seattle. Love was largely held in check by the Chargers in Week 1, rushing 11 times for 41 yards and catching two passes for nine yards, but he did get into the end zone on a five-yard run. He logged six fewer carries and 20 fewer rushing yards than Tyler Allgeier, which isn't ideal for fantasy managers who drafted the rookie with the expectation that he'd be the lead back right off the bat. Even if Love gets a larger share of the workload against Seattle, he could struggle against a defense that held Patriots No. 1 RB Rhamondre Stevenson to 2.8 YPC in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jeremiyah Love is still looking for his first big breakout game heading into Arizona's Week 3 clash in San Francisco. Love has notched 20 rushes for 70 yards and touchdown through two games while adding 25 yards on five catches. Meanwhile, Tyler Allgeier has posted a 22-71-0 line, as both RBs have struggled with efficiency in the early going. Love seems likely to eventually separate as the Cardinals' clear-cut top RB, though the veteran Allgeier could cut into his carries throughout the campaign. The 49ers have been impressive in getting off to a 2-0 start, though they're giving up 4.04 YPC to running backs, just 20th in the league so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jeremiyah Love appears to have ascended to the clear-cut No. 1 RB in Arizona heading into a Week 4 clash versus the Giants. Love handled a career-high 26 touches (21 carries and five catches) this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, compiling 90 yards on the ground and 19 (along with a TD) through the air. Tyler Allgeier was the only other Cardinals RB to log a carry in the contest, and he got just two totes. There could be room for Love to run against the Giants, who are giving up 5.05 yards per carry to running backs, the third-worst mark in the league through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and his status is uncertain for Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit. The rookie running back logged a full workload Week 4 against the Giants, finishing with 14 carries for 63 yards and one catch for minus-8 yards. Fantasy managers who roster Love will likely keep a close eye on the Cardinals' injury reports throughout the week to get a sense of his odds of playing in Week 5. If he does suit up, Love will face a Lions defense that allowed Carolina RB Chuba Hubbard to rumble for 122 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jeremiyah Love will look to rebound in Arizona's Week 6 matchup against the Rams. Love managed just 22 yards on 12 carries against Detroit this past Sunday, and he finished without a catch for the first time as a pro. The rookie continues to lead the Cardinals' ground attack but has managed a meager 3.7 yards per carry through five weeks. The Rams rank 12th in the NFL by giving up 15.5 fantasy points per game to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jeremiyah Love enters Week 7 with a questionable tag after missing Arizona's Week 6 game against the Rams with an ankle injury. The rookie has rushed 67 times for 245 yards and a touchdown while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and another score through five appearances. His 3.7 yards per carry shows room for improvement, though his involvement in the passing game adds fantasy value. Denver has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs in 2026, creating an attractive matchup if Love returns. However, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight could complicate his workload even if he's cleared to play.

player.seasonOutlook: Love was selected by the Cardinals with the No. 3 overall pick of April's draft. Love has good size and terrific speed (4.36 40-yard dash) to go along with a three-down skill set. He led this year's rookie class in both yards per carry (6.66) and yards after contact (4.16) while ranking second in forced missed tackle rate (3.5) during his collegiate career. He's a capable receiver at all levels, a competent pass blocker and protects the ball well (one fumble on 496 career touches). Love will immediately slot in as Arizona's feature back and, especially considering each of the past nine running backs drafted in the top 12 went on to finish top 12 in fantasy points as a rookie, he should be valued as a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rome Odunze will seek to do more as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Odunze was unable to capitalize on the highest-scoring Week 1 game ever, as he finished the game with two catches for 52 yards. The third-year receiver still figures to be a top target for Caleb Williams moving forward, especially in closer matchups where a consistent option is needed. Odunze will face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points to WRs (55.2) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rome Odunze will look to remain a top look in Chicago's passing offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Odunze caught three of four targets for 43 yards against the Vikings in Week 2, and he now sits at a 5-95-0 receiving line across two games. The third-year pass catcher's unimpressive output could continue, given that Tyson Bagent is slotted to start under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Odunze will face a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rome Odunze will look to improve on modest production as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Odunze reeled in three of six targets for 44 yards against the Eagles in Week 3, adding to his already disappointing start to the season. The third-year wide receiver has been consistent, recording three or fewer catches for 52 or fewer yards in each of Chicago's first three games. Odunze will face a Jets squad that has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving yards (337) to WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rome Odunze will look to build off a big performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Odunze was on fire in Week 4 against the Jets with Tyson Bagent under center, bringing in six of seven targets for 94 yards. The starting wide receiver has now posted a 14-233-0 receiving line on the year, which leaves plenty of room to grow. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 31.8 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rome Odunze remains a top option in Chicago's passing game ahead of Week 6 at Atlanta. Odunze brought in just three of his nine targets for 40 yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers, but he still ranked second in receiving yards. The volatility of the Bears' quarterback position has affected Odunze's production so far this season, so the return of Caleb Williams would likely be favorable. Either way, he'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rome Odunze will look to do more as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Odunze brought in just three of four targets for 39 yards in Week 6, which was a bit of a bummer, with Caleb Williams throwing for 305 yards. The third-year pass catcher has been held in check in more games than not this season, catching 20 of 33 targets for 312 yards with zero touchdowns. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Odunze opened the 2025 season with a bang, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and producing 15-plus fantasy points in each game. Things fell apart from there, as the 2024 first-round pick went on to deliver one touchdown and two double-digit fantasy outings over his next eight games prior to missing Weeks 14 through 18 due to injury. On the plus side, Odunze remained heavily targeted throughout the season, especially near the goal line, and he is ninth in the NFL with 24 end zone targets since he was drafted. On the other hand, his connection with Caleb Williams needs work, as his 48% catch rate ranked near the basement at the position. Odunze, 24, is still ascending and has a clearer path to targets with DJ Moore out of the mix. He's a candidate for a Year 3 leap and should be valued as a WR3 with upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Daniels overcame a slow start to nearly lead the Commanders to a comeback win against the Eagles in Week 1. Daniels finished the contest with 164 yards passing and two touchdowns, along with an additional 31 yards rushing for the game. Daniels will look to build some momentum in Week 2 versus an extremely suspect Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed the most yards in the NFL last season, and the supposedly revamped defense was trounced by the Giants in their 2026 opener. The Cowboys allowed 394 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns in an ugly 28-20 loss to Jaxson Dart and company.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow against the Cowboys in Week 2, the same elbow he injured last year for the Commanders. While the elbow is not fractured, Daniels is almost certain to miss Week 3 vs. the Seahawks. Veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4.  Daniels is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow, though, and especially since backup Marcus Mariota just led an improbable victory over the defending Super Bowl champions. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Whoever lines up under center in Week 4 will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jayden Daniels could return in Week 5 for the Commanders from a dislocated elbow. Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota left Washington's last game with a knee injury, which could hasten the need for Daniels to return versus the Giants. if neither quarterback can suit up, seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis would get the nod. The defense for the Giants looks totally revamped in 2026, allowing 205.3 yards per tilt through the air, which is 10th in the league. The Giants are tied for the league-lead with six interceptions.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jayden Daniels returned from injury and appeared to show no ill effects regarding his previously dislocated elbow. Daniels rushed for over 100 yards and two touchdowns, while also passing for 199 yards against the Giants. Unfortunately, poor game management at the end of overtime cost the Commanders the win, and overshadows what was otherwise a solid return to the lineup for Daniels. Unfortunately, a tall task lurks in Week 6 on the road versus the 49ers. San Francisco is undefeated and allowing just 297.2 scrimmage yards per tilt, which is sixth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Daniels is looking to bounce back after appearing in only seven games due to injury last season. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year began his career with a bang, tossing 25 touchdowns and adding 891 yards and six scores with his legs in his first season. He wasn't quite as dominant when healthy last season (16.3 points per game, compared to 20.9 in 2024), but he remained a major factor with his legs (58-278-2 in seven games, three of which were partial appearances). Daniels' supporting cast is underwhelming and he'll be working with a new playcaller (David Blough), but the dual-threat ability supplies the 25-year-old with elite upside. He's a strong QB1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs is hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league flex for the Colts' Week 2 trip to Kansas City. His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Downs is poised to work as the Colts' top wide receiver in Week 3 against the Texans, making him a solid WR3 or flex option in fantasy. Alec Pierce (heel) is expected to sit out, and the Colts lack viable alternatives, with over-the-hill veteran Keenan Allen and recent signing Darius Slayton representing the top options behind Downs in the wide receiver room. Downs caught seven of nine targets for 72 yards to lead the Colts in all three categories during the Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, which Pierce exited in the first half. Downs figures to see plenty of star Texans CB Derek Stingley, but the 25-year-old WR should get plenty of targets from Daniel Jones despite the tricky matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Downs has exceeded 70 receiving yards in each of the Colts' last two games while racking up 20 targets over that span. With fellow Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) on IR, Downs is a recommended Week 4 starting option since he is poised to see plenty of targets from Daniel Jones against a weak Washington secondary that has allowed the most catches (46) and touchdown receptions (six) to WRs, as well as the third-most receiving yards (573) to the position. Downs, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Keenan Allen accounted for 20 of Jones' 24 completed passes in Pierce's absence against the Texans in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Downs disappointed with 16 receiving yards against Washington's vulnerable secondary in Week 4 after notching at least 72 yards in each of the Colts' previous two games. Downs remains the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts, as Alec Pierce (knee) is still on IR heading into a Week 5 road game at Pittsburgh. The Steelers are allowing 149 receiving yards per game to wideouts and traded starting CB Joey Porter to Dallas prior to Week 4. Downs is well-positioned to shake off his Week 4 dud and deliver as a solid Week 5 flex play.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Downs is averaging 50 receiving yards per game and has exceeded 70 twice through five games. However, the 25-year-old wideout has yet to score in his fourth NFL season after compiling 11 TDs across his first three years. He's the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel) heading into a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Tennessee has allowed a couple of big individual performances to wideouts, surrendering at least 117 yards and a TD to both Zay Flowers and DeVonta Smith. However, those are established No. 1 wideouts, putting them a cut above Downs, whose career average is just 46 yards per game. With the Colts likely to rely primarily on their ground game in Week 6, Downs is a decent flex play but far from an elite fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Josh Downs has been outplayed by Keenan Allen since the Colts lost Alec Pierce to a heel injury. After exceeding 70 receiving yards twice through Week 3, Downs has compiled a meager 103 receiving yards over the the past three games combined, topping out at 47 yards in a game over that span. His role as a locked-in starter at WR for the Colts makes Downs a viable Week 7 flex play against the Vikings, though he has now gone nine consecutive games without a TD dating back to last season. Minnesota is allowing 133 yards per game to WRs but has limited the position to three TDs in five games, so Downs looks unlikely to end his scoring drought.

player.seasonOutlook: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to serve as one of the Saints' top running backs if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Kamara was sidelined for Week 1 but is expected to return for Week 2, likely operating as the Saints' top receiving back. He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alvin Kamara is expected to operate as the Saints' top pass-catching back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. In his return from a sprained MCL in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Kamara led the Saints' backfield in carries (nine), targets (six) and receptions (five). Despite this, Travis Etienne was more efficient with his opportunities, averaging 3.1 yards per carry compared to Kamara's 1.7. Even so, the Saints' backfield is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that's allowed just 3.8 yards per carry thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Alvin Kamara will likely be in for a larger offensive role with Travis Etienne (hamstring)  sidelined for New Orleans' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Kamara has received nine carries in each of the last two weeks after sitting out Week 1, but he's struggled with efficiency, averaging just 2.8 yards per carry. Additionally, he saw just one target in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, suggesting he may not have the same receiving volume as in past years. Regardless, this receiving volume should increase with Etienne out for Week 4. Kamara could still struggle against a Falcons defense that's given up 13.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top running back while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is sidelined during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. In his first game without Etienne this season, Kamara totaled 58 yards on 12 touches, but his workload was largely impacted by the game script. He led New Orleans' backfield in targets (seven), which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara is in for a tough Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 14.7 fantasy points per game to running backs this season, the fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Despite operating as New Orleans' No. 1 RB over the last two weeks, Kamara logged fewer snaps (12) and carries (three) than Kendre Miller (six carries on 13 snaps) in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings. Additionally, he got fewer targets than Miller (two to three), which is a very negative sign for his outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara could be productive against a Giants defense that's given up just 94 receiving yards but two receiving touchdowns to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Kamara had his best game of the 2026 campaign in a Week 6 win over the Giants, accounting for 69 yards and a touchdown on nine touches. Despite this, he logged just 18 offensive snaps, which is fewer both than Kendre Miller (31) and CJ Donaldson (22). Kamara dealt with an injury in the first half, but with Miller receiving 20 carries, it appears as if Kamara's upside is limited, operating primarily as a receiver out of the backfield. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up just 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

Tyson was selected by the Saints with the No. 8 overall pick of April's draft. He is a versatile receiver with decent size who led this rookie class with a 35% target share during the nine weeks he was active in 2025. Injuries cost him time during all four collegiate seasons, but he still managed a 158-2,282-22 receiving line in 33 games, posting a strong 2.73 YPRR along the way (third best in this class). Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August and will miss a month or two of the regular season prior to taking over as the Saints' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave. Once healthy, Tyson has a path to a substantial role in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough and could find himself on the WR3 radar. Of course, with the injury, he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers hope to improve to 2-0 when they visit the Patriots in Week 2. He secured all five targets for 46 yards and Aaron Rodgers' lone passing TD, and finished second on the team in receiving yards while tying for first in receptions. Freiermuth led Pittsburgh's TEs in offensive snaps (49), but Darnell Washington was a close second with 43. He and the Steelers will try to scheme up a way to beat a New England defense that is tied for second in receiving yards allowed to the position (13).
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers play host to the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 3. He paced the team's tight ends in snaps (46), receptions (4), yards (32) and targets (5) during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Freiermuth appears to have the upper hand over Darnell Washington (1-7-0) in the passing game, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are relatively low in an underwhelming Steelers offense. He'll have the added benefit of facing a Cincinnati defense that allows 18.5 fantasy points per game to TEs (27th) and just got torched for 12 receptions and 140 yards by Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 4 AFC North clash against the Browns. He caught two of four targets for 30 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Aaron Rodgers continues to spread the ball around, as six different Steelers receivers registered at least four targets, and four tied for the team lead in receptions with three. Freiermuth could be a sneaky play versus a Cleveland defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (14.9) to TEs and gave up eight receptions (on 12 targets) for 92 yards to the position in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town for a Week 5 home tilt. He played 75% of snaps on offense and caught three of five targets for 17 yards and his second touchdown of the season. Fellow tight end Darnell Washington (3-27-1) was slightly more productive while playing 70% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like it'll be a toss-up between the two on any given week as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 6. He played 38 snaps on offense (70%) and was highly productive, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two of Aaron Rodgers' three TD passes during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Freiermuth finished third on the team in receptions and yardage, while his seven looks were the second-most. Fellow starting tight end Darnell Washington was on the field for 34 offensive snaps (63%) and caught two of three targets for 12 yards. Freiermuth recorded a second consecutive outing with a score and now has four TDs on the season, and he'll aim to take advantage of a Tampa Bay defense allowing 15.7 fantasy points per game (22nd) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers travel to Paris to take on the Saints in Week 7. He caught two of three targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime in Week 6. Freiermuth and fellow tight end Darnell Washington each played 71% of snaps on offense, but it was the latter who made the bigger impact in this one, as Washington tallied a 4-25-1 line on six targets. Freiermuth will try to rebound versus a New Orleans defense that just surrendered six receptions for 99 yards and a TD to Isaiah Likely.

player.seasonOutlook: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Kelce showed he still has plenty left in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, leading the team with 71 receiving yards while catching three of five targets. The veteran tight end's production tailed off the last couple years, but he still topped 800 receiving yards in 12 straight seasons, and Week 1's performance moved him past Jason Witten into second place on the NFL's all-time list for TEs with 13,073 yards, trailing only Tony Gonzalez's 15,127. Kelce will take on a Colts defense in Week 2 that ranked 31st in receiving yards allowed to tight ends in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Kelce continued a strong start to his 14th NFL season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 9-101-1 line on 11 targets. The future Hall of Famer last delivered a 1,000-yard campaign in 2022, but he's jumped out to an early pace in 2026 that would see him top 1,400 receiving yards and set a new career high. With Patrick Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Kelce may need to rely on spike games rather than steady production for his fantasy value. He'll take on a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's allowed 10.2 yards per target to tight ends through two weeks, 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Kelce notched just two targets in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, but he caught both for 59 yards and a touchdown. The future Hall of Famer seems revitalized in his age-36 season, and he's already hauled in two catches of 40 or more yards, just one short of the career-high three he produced way back in 2016. Patrick Mahomes is spreading the ball around effectively, and Kelce, Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets through three games. The tight end has turned his volume into a strong 14-231-2 line. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs and has already coughed up five TDs to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Travis Kelce remains on pace for a bounce-back season coming out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye. Through four games, the veteran tight end is on pace for his first 1,000-yard season since 2022, although it's fair to wonder if he can keep that up given his reduced volume, as he's also on track to fall short of 100 targets for the first time since 2014. With Kenneth Walker having rejuvenated the team's rushing game and Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy both capable of handling underneath and intermediate routes, there isn't a clear niche for Kelce to thrive in. He remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, and that should keep his floor relatively high. Kelce will take on a Chargers defense in Week 6 that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Travis Kelce wasn't needed much in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, catching four of five targets for 53 yards. The veteran tight end has slowed down after a fast start to the season, and through five games he's produced a 20-299-2 line on 27 targets while the offense has leaned heavily on Kenneth Walker. Kelce remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, especially while Rashee Rice is sidelined. Kelce faces a tough matchup in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that's allowed the fewest receiving yards in the league to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Kelce re-signed with the Chiefs and is returning for what might be his final NFL season. The veteran tight end's days as an elite producer are behind him, and he saw a notable dip in usage last season (19.6% target share was his lowest since 2014). Kelce did hold up for 17 games and still finished in the top 10 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG. Kelce has reeled off 10 consecutive top-five fantasy campaigns despite not offering much in the scoring department (he hasn't cleared five TDs in a season since 2022). The 36-year-old's role could dip even further this season, so he's best valued as a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendrick Bourne had a promising performance for Arizona in Week 1 and will look to be productive again versus the Seahawks in Week 2. Bourne led Cardinals wideouts with eight catches and 75 yards in a season-opening victory versus the Chargers, with only stud tight end Trey McBride outpacing his eight targets. The veteran Bourne looked to have great rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett, so it will be interesting to see how the target distribution shakes out in Week 2 and beyond. He won't have an easy matchup against Seattle, who limited New England to 178 yards through the air in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kendrick Bourne appears to have earned a key role in Arizona's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup versus San Francisco. After joining the Cardinals in the offseason, Bourne has recorded 11 targets through two weeks, second-most among Arizona wide receivers. The veteran wideout has logged a 10-86-0 line on those opportunities, as he has established good chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. With that said, Week 3 could be another tough test for Arizona's air game: the 49ers have allowed just a 59.3 percent catch rate to WRs so far, ninth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kendrick Bourne is coming off two quiet weeks heading into Arizona's Week 4 tilt versus the Giants. After posting an 8-75-0 receiving line in the season opener against the Chargers, the veteran wideout has managed a modest four catches on six targets for 33 yards combined over his subsequent two games. Bourne appears to be well behind WR Michael Wilson and TE Trey McBride, and at least marginally behind WR Marvin Harrison, in the passing-game pecking order at the moment. There could be an opportunity to make some noise against a Giants defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards allowed to wideouts so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kendrick Bourne is looking to re-involve himself in Arizona's offense in Week 5 against the Lions. Bourne logged a healthy 42 of 66 offensive snaps against the Giants in Week 4, but he didn't draw a single target from QB Jacoby Brissett. In fact, Bourne has logged just six total targets across his past three games after posting an 8-75-0 line on eight targets in the Cardinals' season opener. Detroit could provide an opportunity for Bourne to get going, as the Lions have given up a league-high 61 total catches to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kendrick Bourne seems set for a major role in Arizona's offense ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Rams. With Marvin Harrison now officially traded to the Texans, Bourne figures to slot in behind Michael Wilson as the Cardinals' No. 2 wideout. That positioning led to a nice game for Bourne this past Sunday against Detroit, as he outproduced Wilson with a 5-70-0 line on eight targets. The Rams could present a challenge, however, as they've yielded the fewest catches per game (8.0) to wideouts through five weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kendrick Bourne has established himself as a regular contributor in Arizona's passing attack, catching 22 passes for 225 yards through six games, though he hasn't found the end zone. The veteran wideout is averaging a career-low 10.2 yards per catch in 2026, but that's also due to the struggles the Cardinals' passing attack has had with Jacoby Brissett under center. To make things even more complicated, he'll face the Broncos' secondary in Week 7, and Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026. That makes Bourne a difficult player to trust outside deeper PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omar Cooper is uncertain to play for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers due to an ankle sprain. In his NFL debut, he caught his only target for 30 yards. The Jets ran a heavy ground game to open the year, and while they will likely need to throw more in Week 2 to keep up, Cooper's role, even if healthy, is uncertain. The passing game should continue to flow heavily through Garrett Wilson, leaving Cooper's fantasy value volatile.
outlooksByWeek.7: Omar Cooper brings momentum into the Jets' Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. Returning from a four-week absence due to an ankle issue, Cooper flashed with 103 yards and a touchdown on seven targets. The Jets remain a low-volume passing attack, and Miami has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers, but Cooper provides a big-play option, averaging 19.0 yards per catch in limited action. He could offer a high-upside bye-week fill-in.

player.seasonOutlook: Cooper was selected by the Jets in the first round of April's draft. The Indiana product is fresh off a breakout 2025 season in which he posted a 69-937-13 receiving line after totaling 46 catches during his first three seasons with the Hoosiers. Primarily a perimeter target in limited action from 2022 to 2024, Cooper aligned in the slot on 80% of his routes last season. He is a short-area target (9.0 aDOT last season), but still posted strong efficiency numbers, including a 2.61 YPRR. He'll begin his career behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in New York's Geno Smith-led offense and is unlikely to produce consistent flex value as a rookie.

outlooksByWeek.2: C.J. Stroud has turned the ball over nine times in Houston's last three games, dating back to the start of last season's playoffs. He'll face a Bengals defense in Week 2 that just forced three turnovers from Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two TDs in Week 1 against the Bills but fumbled away Houston's chance to win the game in the final minute. The Texans' vaunted defense faces another tough test against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, so Stroud and the offense will be relied upon to keep pace. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in superflex or two-QB formats but ranks outside the starting range in single-QB leagues.
outlooksByWeek.3: C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards but led the Texans to just six points in the absence of top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) during Week 2's loss to the Bengals. If Houston remains without Collins in Week 3 against the Colts, Stroud will likely lean heavily on TE Dalton Schultz once more against a Colts defense that allowed 41 points to the Ravens and then 33 to the Chiefs. Considering the Colts have surrendered the most points and yards in the NFL, Stroud is worth a look in superflex or multi-QB lineups, but he will likely remain ranked outside the starting range in single-QB formats, at least until Collins returns.
outlooksByWeek.4: C.J. Stroud has missed top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) over Houston's past two games, failing to throw a touchdown pass in Week 2 and producing just 167 passing yards in Week 3. The Texans fell to 0-3 heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. On the bright side, the Texans rebounded from an 0-3 start last season to finish 12-5, and Collins has a realistic chance to return versus Dallas. If Stroud gets his top target back, the slumping QB would have a nice opportunity to get on track as a strong superflex or second fantasy QB against a weak Cowboys secondary that has allowed a 7:0 TD:INT through three games in 2026 after giving up the most QB production in the league last season. Should Collins sit again, Stroud would be a risky choice in all formats despite the favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.5: C.J. Stroud has some streaming appeal in single-QB formats for Week 5, when the Texans travel to Tennessee for a battle between 0-4 AFC South squads. He has thrown for at least 347 yards in two of Houston's four losses and has a 5:0 TD:INT. The Titans have been respectable against the pass, with only four touchdowns allowed through the air this season, but other teams were able to build leads and run effectively on Tennessee. The Texans are unlikely to find as much success on the ground, considering RBs David Montgomery and Woody Marks have combined to average 2.9 yards per carry this season. Stroud has been asked to throw the ball 38 times per game, and he's likely to remain busy in Week 5. The Texans got top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) back from a two-game absence in Week 4, and Collins contributed immediately in his return by catching both of Stroud's touchdown passes in a 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
outlooksByWeek.6: C.J. Stroud could have a key new target for Houston's pivotal Week 6 clash with the AFC South-leading Jaguars in London. The Texans are just 1-4 and have already fallen three games behind Jacksonville in the standings, but Stroud is quietly averaging a career-high 280 passing yards per game to go with a 6:0 TD:INT. Jacksonville gives up the fewest rushing yards and second-most passing yards per game, so Stroud will likely be asked to carry Houston's offense again in Week 6, making him a viable starting QB in fantasy. The Texans notched their first win of the season in Week 5 over the Titans and promptly traded for disgruntled Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison, who hasn't lived up to the hype as the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft but excelled at Ohio State while catching passes from Stroud in 2022. Harrison likely won't be fully up to speed, but he could still provide an upgrade over Houston's current wideouts behind Nico Collins.
outlooksByWeek.7: C.J. Stroud is averaging a career-high 286 passing yards per game and has posted a 9:1 TD:INT heading into Houston's Week 7 home game against the Giants. He threw a season-high three touchdown passes in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville while topping 300 yards for the third time in six starts. The Giants have surrendered 12 passing TDs, which is sixth-most in the NFL, and their three rushing scores allowed to QBs are tied for the most in the league, though they have also notched six interceptions. Stroud has consistently been asked to put the Texans' offense on his back due to the team's weak running game, and he has mostly been up to the challenge, so he remains a fringe fantasy starter for Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Stroud enters his fourth NFL season yet to emerge as a quality fantasy option and having seen his passing production dip during each season of his career. Stroud impressed as a rookie with 24 passing TDs, three rushing TDs and a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game (18.4). During the past two seasons, he failed to clear 20 passing touchdowns, has a total of one rushing TD and averaged 13.8 points, ranking outside the top 20 both years. Stroud's efficiency has been solid at best and thanks in part to Houston's elite defense, he hasn't needed to throw the ball (or scramble) very often. There's little reason to expect much change in 2026, so even with a good, deep group of pass catchers, the 24-year-old is best viewed as a low-upside, fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

outlooksByWeek.2: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. St. Brown kicked off the season with a bang against the Saints, catching 10 of 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns. The star wide receiver continues to hold the monopoly in Detroit's passing game, and his production doesn't look to be taking a dip any time soon. He'll take on a Bills defense that ceded a seventh-most PPR points to Houston wide receivers (40.0) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to stay hot as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. St. Brown finished with a monster performance in Week 2, bringing in nine of 13 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns. Not only has the star pass catcher recorded back-to-back two-TD performances, but he's also now amassed 19 catches for 209 yards in that stretch. He should continue to benefit from Detroit's shaky defense, even against a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to bounce back from a quieter game as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. St. Brown finished Week 3 against the Jets with a touchdown, but other than that, he has just four catches for 19 yards. The eight targets he finished with did still tie  Jahmyr Gibbs for a team lead, so the volume remains for the pair of stars to both produce highly. St. Brown will face a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to find the end zone again as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. St. Brown returned to a solid eight catches for 75 yards against the Panthers in Week 4, but he also broke his three-game touchdown streak. The star pass catcher has now totaled 31 receptions for 303 yards and five touchdowns this season. He'll take on a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to find the end zone again as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. St. Brown has remained hot as of late with 14 catches for 144 yards in his last two outings, but he's been unable to find the end zone since Week 3. The star wide receiver will take a 37-372-5 receiving line into a big matchup versus a Green Bay secondary that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: The only player in NFL history with 90-plus catches in each of his first five NFL seasons, St. Brown continues to assert himself as one of the league's best players. The 2021 fourth-round pick has finished exactly third among receivers in fantasy points three seasons in a row, ranking no lower than fourth in catches, yards and touchdowns each year. St. Brown actually enjoyed a career-high target share in 2025 (31.6%), which helped him to 13 top-20 fantasy outings. The 26-year-old has no added target competition and remains Jared Goff's clear No. 1 target. He should be off the board in the first round of your draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nico Collins is in danger of sitting out against the Bengals in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury. He paced Houston's passing attack with a 7-75-1 line on 10 targets in the season opener, so he would work as the team's WR1 again in Week 2 against the Bengals if given the green light to suit up. Cincinnati didn't allow a passing TD to the Buccaneers in Week 1 but had one of the league's worst all-around defenses last season, when the Bengals gave up the second-most yards and third-most points in the NFL. Collins remains a set-and-forget fantasy WR1 as he chases his fourth consecutive 1,000-yard receiving season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nico Collins (hamstring) didn't suit up for the Texans in Week 2 and may not be ready to return against the Colts in Week 3. If Collins recovers, he'll jump back in as the top option in Houston's passing game and a fantasy WR2 at worst. Should Collins sit again, TE Dalton Schultz could continue to work as the primary pass catcher for C.J. Stroud, while the Texans get by with Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne at WR.
outlooksByWeek.4: Nico Collins (hamstring) could return from a two-week absence in Week 4 against the Cowboys. Houston's No. 1 WR will immediately jump back into the fantasy WR1 range if he plays against a Dallas defense that's giving up 27.3 points per game. The Cowboys have allowed seven touchdowns through the air, though only three of those went to WRs. Houston hasn't garnered much production out of its wide receiver room in Collins' absence. If Collins remains unavailable, TE Dalton Schultz would likely remain the de facto top target for QB C.J. Stroud.
outlooksByWeek.5: Nico Collins returned from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury in Week 5 and reclaimed his customary spot as Houston's top receiver and a fantasy WR1. He scored twice against the Cowboys and has compiled 14 catches for 194 yards and three TDs in two appearances this season. Collins can be started with confidence in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 167 receiving yards per game to wideouts. DeVonta Smith and Zay Flowers each compiled at least 117 yards and a TD against Tennessee's secondary.
outlooksByWeek.6: Nico Collins is averaging 83 receiving yards and one touchdown per game as the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game. His role isn't expected to change in Week 6 against the Jaguars, even with the Texans having traded for 2024 fourth overall pick Marvin Harrison from the Cardinals. Jacksonville boasts the league's best run defense but has a vulnerable secondary, as the Jaguars are the only team to have allowed over 1,000 yards to wide receivers this season. Collins is a top-five fantasy WR for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Nico Collins has posted at least 79 scrimmage yards in three of his four appearances this season for the Texans ahead of a Week 7 home game against the Giants. The star wideout can be deployed in his usual spot as a fantasy WR1 for Week 7 while facing a Giants secondary that has done a decent job of suppressing yards from WRs but is tied for the fourth-most TDs allowed to the position with seven. Collins has 24 touchdown receptions in 46 games since the start of the 2023 campaign, including three scores in four games this season as the top target for resurgent QB C.J. Stroud.

player.seasonOutlook: Collins heads into his sixth NFL campaign yet to play a full 17-game season, but having been very productive when on the field. The 2021 third-round pick has cleared 1,000 yards and scored either seven or eight touchdowns each of the past three seasons, finishing in the top 10 in fantasy PPG and top 12 in yards per route run in all three. A force near the goal line, Collins ranked fourth among receivers with 13 end zone targets in 2025. The 27-year-old's target share doesn't stack up with other top receivers (he has never cleared 24.4%), but his high-end efficiency is just enough to keep him in the back-end WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Javonte Williams scored twice in the season opener for Dallas. Williams rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown, while catching five passes for 31 yards and a second score, though the Cowboys fell to the Giants by a score of 28-20. Nevertheless, Williams appears to have picked up right where he left off in 2025 during his career year. In Week 2, Williams will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL in that category currently.
outlooksByWeek.3: Javonte Williams was rather quiet last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 50 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone versus Washington, as the passing game took the spotlight in the 37-20 win. Williams may also have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL. However, Baltimore has allowed three rushing touchdowns already, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Javonte Williams rushed for a season-high 98 yards last game for the Cowboys. Williams also found the end zone for the third time this year. He has received at least 15 touches in every game this season. In Week 4, WIlliams should continue to remain heavily involved against the Houston Texans. The Texans have been extremely stingy against the run, though. Houston is surrendering just 86.7 rushing yards per clash, which is fifth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Javonte Williams scored three times in the second half of the last game for the Cowboys, leading a thrilling comeback victory over the Texans. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote this season, but has six combined touchdowns through four outings. He has also made his presence felt in the passing game with 15 receptions over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again last game for Dallas. Williams rushed 12 times for 45 yards and the score, notching his sixth rushing touchdown of the young season. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote, but has received double-digit carries in every contest in 2026. In Week 6, Williams looks primed for another jaunt to the end zone versus the Packers. Green Bay has given up eight rushing touchdowns already this season, which is 31st in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again for Dallas last game. Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Williams has scored in four-straight games for the Cowboys, though is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote overall. In fact, he has failed to cross the 50-yard rushing mark in two-straight games. In Week 7, Williams will face a sliding Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per contest, which is 19th in the league. The Eagles have also yielded eight rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 28th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys following a successful first year with the team. After failing to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign during his final three seasons in Denver, Williams finished 12th in 2025, setting career-best marks in carries, rushing yards, touches (287), scrimmage yards (1,338) and yards per carry (4.77). He also scored a career-high 13 touchdowns after totaling 16 during his first four campaigns, and his 16 carries inside the 5-yard line were fifth most among backs. That helped offset his receiving struggles, as his 2.7 yards per target was last among qualified RBs. With minimal competition for touches in a high-scoring Dallas offense, the 26-year-old is a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle did not contribute much in his Broncos' debut, catching just one of three targets for a meager two yards in the Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Steve Spagnuolo's rebuilt secondary prioritized taking Waddle out of the picture, and the former Dolphin wideout hasn't yet established enough chemistry with QB Bo Nix to overcome consistent double teams. Waddle will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Waddle broke out in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, erupting for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets as he began to get on the same page as quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle logged plenty of downfield targets but also had a red zone look, usage that promises plenty more big performances. The former Dolphin hasn't had a 1,000-yard season since 2023, but the early returns in Denver suggest he'll have little trouble returning to that level in 2026. He'll face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of those have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Waddle is struggling to adjust to his new offense with the Broncos. The former Dolphins wide receiver caught only two of his seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams for 10 yards, while adding a 14-yard run. Waddle leads Denver with 20 targets through three games, but he's turned them into just 11 catches for 150 yards, and he's still looking for his first TD of the season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Waddle scored his first touchdown with the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but it was overall another disappointing performance from the former Dolphin. Waddle has recorded double-digit targets only once in four games to begin the season, leading to a modest 16-185-1 line on 26 looks from Bo Nix. That's still better numbers than Courtland Sutton, and the issue seems to be the overall struggles of the offense under first-time play caller Davis Webb.
