Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Antonio Williams led the Commanders in receiving in Week 1 despite playing just 26 offensive snaps. Williams ended up with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL premiere. He had as many targets as Terry McLaurin. Williams should see the field with increasing frequency if he continues to perform this well. He has a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that was the worst in the NFL last season, and surrendered three passing scores in the season-opening loss to the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.3: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Antonio Williams finished third in targets for the Commanders last game. Williams caught just two balls on four looks, though, en route to only 15 yards receiving. Williams caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Antonio Williams had eight targets last game for Washington, which was second on the squad behind Stefon Diggs. Unfortunately, Williams could muster just three catches for 21 yards in the lackluster loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Williams, regardless of whether Terry McLaurin also suits up. McLaurin was sidelined with a hamstring issue. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Antonio Williams managed three catches last game for Washington. Even without the services of fellow wideout Stefon Diggs, Williams accumulated fewer than 35 yards receiving for the third-straight contest. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Allgeier heads into a Week 2 clash against Seattle with a big role in Arizona's backfield. Allgeier logged 17 carries for 61 yards in a season-opening win against the Chargers, getting more totes and producing more yards than rookie Jeremiyah Love. It remains to be seen if that will hold true throughout the campaign, but for the time being Allgeier seems set to be heavily involved in the Cardinals' ground game. With that said, both Allgeier and Love could find the sledding tough in Week 2 versus a Seahawks defense that yielded the third-fewest rushing yards per game during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Allgeier will seek to improve his efficiency on the ground during Arizona's Week 3 visit to San Francisco. Allgeier gained just 10 yards on five carries Sunday in a loss against Seattle, and he's averaging a meager 3.2 YPC through two contests. He paced the Cardinals with 17 carries in the team's season opener, but  Jeremiyah Love jumped ahead with him with nine carries Week 2 and could continue to settle in as the club's clear No. 1 RB moving forward. The 49ers have yielded 4.04 YPC to running backs so far, but that's led to just one rushing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Allgeier seems to have fallen well behind Jeremiyah Love for ball-carrying opportunities heading into Arizona's Week 4 matchup with the Giants. Love carried the ball 21 times against San Francisco this past Sunday, while Allgeier handled a season-low two totes. The latter did reel in a season-best four catches, but they amounted to just 10 receiving yards. Though the Giants are struggling against the run, ranking in the bottom half of the league in allowing 18.5 fantasy points per game to RBs, Allgeier will likely need to see more opportunities in order to make an impact.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Allgeier may be lined up for a big role for Arizona in Week 5 against the Lions. Rookie Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and if he can't suit up Sunday, Allgeier will likely lead the team's backfield. Even with Love healthy for nearly the entire game in Week 4, Allgeier posted good production, recording an 8-42-1 rushing line and two catches for seven yards. The Cardinals' RB group could find success against a Lions defense that is giving up 4.64 yards per carry to running backs, eighth-worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Allgeier's role in Arizona's backfield seems to be fading ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Rams. Allgeier logged just three carries for seven yards this past Sunday against Detroit while adding nine yards on two catches. The veteran running back has logged three or fewer totes two of the past three weeks and seems to be far behind rookie Jeremiyah Love, who got 12 carries versus the Lions, in the pecking order. With that said, he could get some opportunities as a pass catcher against the Rams, who have given up the fourth-most receiving yards per game (42.6) to running backs through five weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Allgeier could continue handling a significant share of Arizona's backfield workload in Week 7 against Denver, regardless of whether Jeremiyah Love remains sidelined with an ankle injury or returns after a one-game absence. Allgeier has rushed 53 times for 157 yards and a touchdown through six games, but he's averaging just 3.0 yards per carry, so he needs to be more efficient when he gets the ball. Bam Knight's emergence adds another obstacle to consistent fantasy production. However, Denver has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs in 2026, so Allgeier should have flex appeal if he has an expanded role for a second consecutive week.

player.seasonOutlook: Allgeier signed with the Cardinals during free agency. The 2022 fifth-round NFL draft pick impressed as a rookie in Atlanta, totaling 1,174 yards on 226 touches, but he hasn't come close to those marks while playing second fiddle to Bijan Robinson over the past three seasons, and he has yet to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign. Allgeier did score eight touchdowns last season, but he remains a nonfactor as a receiver, never clearing 18 catches in a season. The 26-year-old will step into a similar role in Arizona, as the primary backup and change-of-pace option behind No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love. Same as in Atlanta, Allgeier has no standalone value, but he's a very good insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Higbee remains in a crowded Rams tight-end corps heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Giants. Though Higbee led Los Angeles TEs with two catches in a Week 1 loss to San Francisco, he logged only 12 offensive snaps -- fourth-most among the group. The Rams frequently use three-TE sets, so Higbee figures to be involved in some capacity each week, but he could have a hard time carving out consistent production if he remains at the bottom of the pecking order in terms of playing time. The Giants held a trio of Cowboys tight ends to five catches for 32 yards in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Higbee may be in line for an upgraded role for the Rams in Week 4 versus Philadelphia. After falling below a 30% offensive snap share each of the first two weeks and producing just two catches for 12 yards, Higbee exploded for an 8-62-1 receiving line on 11 targets and a 71% percent offensive snap share in Week 3 against Denver. That was partly due to fellow tight ends Terrance Ferguson (ankle) and Colby Parkinson (shoulder) getting hurt, and at least Ferguson (and possibly Parkinson) is expected to be sidelined for Week 4. However, the Eagles have been stingy versus tight ends so far, yielding only 89 receiving yards and no touchdowns to the position through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Higbee may have worked his way back up to the Rams' No. 1 tight-end role with a Week 5 matchup against Buffalo on tap. After logging just two catches over the first two weeks of the season, Higbee has tallied a 13-129-1 line over the past two weeks. He's led Los Angeles tight ends in offensive snaps in each of those contests, with injuries to Colby Parkinson (shoulder) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) contributing to the uptick in playing time. Buffalo has given up just one touchdown to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Higbee has become a key target for Rams QB Matthew Stafford ahead of a Week 6 battle against Arizona. Higbee recorded a season-high 83 receiving yards on five catches while drawing six targets Monday versus Buffalo. After beginning the campaign with just two catches for 12 yards over his first two contests, Higbee has posted no less than five receptions and 62 yards each of the past three weeks. He could find more success against the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-worst 9.81 yards per target to tight ends on the season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Higbee has emerged as the Rams' most productive receiving tight end, catching 24 passes for 246 yards and a touchdown through six games. Even though he delivered a subpar showing in Week 6 against the Cardinals, finishing with four catches for 22 yards, he's clearly ahead of Colby Parkinson in the pecking order in the passing game. With Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for the time being, Higbee should be one of the players in line for an uptick in targets and touches. The Week 7 matchup against the Raiders is favorable on paper, as Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position on his own team and, thus, nowhere close to fantasy relevance.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bijan Robinson will continue to lead Atlanta's offense in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Panthers. Robinson received a whopping 29 touches in Week 1, tying Ashton Jeanty for the second-most in the NFL. The Texas product looked explosive despite the Falcons' offensive struggles, which is a good sign for his outlook going forward. Robinson is in for a great matchup as well, with the Panthers defense allowing 291 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bijan Robinson is expected to lead the Falcons' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has given up 22.9 PPR fantasy points per game to running backs this season. Despite Atlanta's offensive struggles through two weeks, Robinson has continued to produce, having recorded 254 total yards and a touchdown on 48 touches. With Michael Penix back at the helm for the Week 3 contest, Robinson should be in for even more production. Additionally, he's in for a favorable matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed three rushing touchdowns in its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue being the main playmaker on the Falcons' offense in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson has been stellar despite Atlanta's offensive struggles three weeks into the season, accounting for 467 total yards and three touchdowns. He's already recorded 79 touches (26.3 per game) this year, suggesting this massive fantasy output will continue as the season progresses. Additionally, Robinson is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 27.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue leading Atlanta's offense during the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Robinson has excelled through the Falcons' first four games, averaging 153.5 total yards per game and scoring five touchdowns on 99 touches. He ranks second in the NFL in total yards and will likely remain the focal point of a Falcons offense that's averaged 40 points per game over their last two contests. Despite this, Robinson is in for a difficult Wek 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 19.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bijan Robinson will lead Atlanta's offensive attack in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Robinson remained one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 5 despite the overtime loss, totaling 128 yards on 21 touches. He ranks as the No. 3 RB in all of fantasy through five contests, averaging a whopping 26.3 points per game. He could be in for a tough Week 6 matchup, however, as Chicago's defense has given up just 18.8 fantasy points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson logged a season-low nine carries in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, as Atlanta was trailing by 24 points in the second half. Despite this, he remained productive when given the opportunities, averaging 6.8 yards per carry. Expect Robinson to bounce back and remain one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has allowed 24.5 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through five contests.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson enters his fourth season having finished in the top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons. Also a big factor as a receiver, he has ranked no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in his three pro seasons. In 2025, PFF tracked him with 86 forced missed tackles, which was easily the most among backs. The 24-year-old is in his prime and, though he has a new coach in Kevin Stefanski, his path to a massive offensive role remains clear. He's on the short list of players who should be considered with the first pick of your fantasy draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ashton Jeanty looked like a franchise back in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, turning 29 touches into 147 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The ankle injury that limited him in training camp and the preseason was no longer an issue, and the second-year RB dominated the workload, as rookie backup Mike Washington notched only seven carries. Jeanty's pass-catching role could be cut back once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to return, but he will remain a focal point of the offense heading into a Week 2 clash with a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ashton Jeanty has looked the part of a bell-cow running back to begin his second NFL season, amassing 54 touches through two games and turning them into 210 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The 2025 first-round pick is still only averaging 3.4 yards per carry however, and the Raiders' offseason upgrades to the offensive line haven't yet led to better efficiency on the ground for Jeanty. He'll try to take advantage of a Week 3 clash with a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ashton Jeanty continues to garner a big workload for the Raiders, but he isn't yet consistently producing big numbers. Through three games, the second-year back is tied for third in the NFL in touches with 76, behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson, but Jeanty's averaging just 3.3 yards per carry and his 303 scrimmage yards are only 14th in the league. He also has yet to score a rushing touchdown in 2026, although he did haul in two TD catches in Week 1. Jeanty will try to improve his efficiency in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ashton Jeanty continues to bolster his lackluster rushing numbers with big production through the air. In the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, the second-year RB managed just 58 rushing yards on 15 carries, but he added six catches for 68 yards on a season-high eight targets. Jeanty's 3.4 yards per carry and zero TDs on the ground through four weeks are a concern, but his 19-165-2 line on 24 targets softens the blow. He'll take on a Patriots defense in Week 5 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ashton Jeanty continues to keep his production afloat via his skills as a pass-catcher. The second-year running back is averaging just 3.3 yards per carry after another poor showing on the ground in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, but he's supplied a 22-215-2 line on 30 targets through five games. The 30 targets are third in the league among RBs, behind the Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs and the Rams' Kyren Williams, while Jeanty's receiving yards are third behind Gibbs and the Steelers' Jaylen Warren. Jeanty will try to deliver a more well-rounded line in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and 31st in receiving TDs allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ashton Jeanty scored his first rushing touchdown of the season in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, but it was otherwise another lackluster performance for the second-year running back. Jeanty is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry, and the inefficiency is costing him volume, as he hasn't handled 20-plus touches in a game since Week 4. He remains involved as a pass catcher, however, hauling in at least three passes in every game this year while compiling a 26-251-2 line on 36 targets through six contests. Jeanty could contribute through the air in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but 29th in receiving yards per game allowed to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeanty is eyeing a leap forward in his second NFL season after an uneven rookie campaign in which the first-round pick enjoyed a ton of volume (seventh among backs in carries, targets and receptions) and played fairly well (eighth among RBs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF) but struggled to overcome the shaky Las Vegas offense. The good news is that the Raiders' offense should improve in 2026 with a better/healthier offensive line, a new coach in Super Bowl champion Klint Kubiak and a new quarterback in projected No. 1 NFL draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Jeanty has a clean path to a massive offensive role and is a strong bet for a leap forward. The 22-year-old is a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens was held to just 28 yards in the season opener for the Cowboys. Pickens did finish second on the team in targets with six, but was rather quiet still by his standards. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Pickens was second on the Cowboys in targets last game.  Pickens managed six catches for just 40 yards, though, as CeeDee Lamb went wild for Dallas. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Pickens has a disappointing nine catches for only 68 yards through two games for Dallas. The task may not get easier in Week 3, as Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Pickens is coming off his best game of the season for the Cowboys. Pickens led Dallas in targets with 11 opportunities, parlaying those looks into seven grabs for 82 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. However, Pickens has yet to find the end zone this season, and his overall numbers remain disappointing following a standout 2025 campaign. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL. Moreover, teammate CeeDee Lamb could be guarded by all-pro corner Derek Stingley Jr., which could free up Pickens for more targets.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Pickens has had back-to-back games with at least 75 yards receiving for the Cowboys. On the downside, Pickens was targeted just three times last game as compared to a staggering 21 targets for fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb. The targets are unlikely to be so lopsided in Week 5 versus the Bucs, but Pickens certainly appears to be playing second-fiddle to the aforementioned Lamb in 2026. Tampa Bay's defense has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Pickens stepped up last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards as he was dealing with a quadriceps issue. As a result, Pickens was the primary target in the passing game and corralled nine of 13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown.  Lamb is not expected to miss the Week 6 clash versus the Packers, though Pickens would benefit even if Lamb is limited. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Pickens led the Cowboys in receiving last game. With the Cowboys trailing for the entire contest, the passing game took center stage, though admittedly still struggled. Despite 11 looks, Pickens managed just 73 yards on six catches in the 23-13 loss to the Pack. Pickens has an impressive 24 targets over his last two contests alone. He will look to get back over the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: DJ Moore will look to build on an impressive debut when the Bills host the Lions in Week 2. Despite new quarterback Josh Allen continuing to spread the ball around, Moore popped with a 100-yard outing on eight targets. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to open the year, but just 7.3 yards per attempt as New Orleans was forced to throw from behind. That may not be the case Thursday, and Moore is unlikely to garner high volume. Even so, facing a secondary void of high-end talent, Moore can get deep and provide big yardage without a lot of opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: DJ Moore will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he is to help the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. After showing sound chemistry with Josh Allen in his first action for Buffalo, Moore failed to haul in a touchdown late in the second quarter in Week 2, suffering the injury that forced him to miss the second half. The Chargers have allowed three touchdowns to opposing receivers through two weeks and two 75-plus yardage performances, which should thrust Moore back into fantasy relevance if he's able to reprise his No. 1 WR role.
outlooksByWeek.4: DJ Moore aims to remain heavily involved in the Bills' Week 4 game against the Patriots. In two healthy games, Moore has 18 targets as Josh Allen's top option, creating a stable floor. New England's secondary is middling, allowing the 18th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, no one has topped 64 yards against them. Moore's potential could be further capped if he draws shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.5: DJ Moore continues to battle a shoulder issue as the Bills get set to travel in Week 5 to face the Rams. Moore exited Week 4's game against New England after aggravating the injury, his second early departure in four games. When playing an entire four quarters, Moore has dominated targets from Josh Allen, averaging nine looks. However, pairing injury concerns with the Rams' secondary not allowing an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, Moore could struggle in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: DJ Moore continues to battle through a shoulder issue that's cost him the better part of three games as the Bills head towards a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Moore has drawn 18 targets in his two healthy games, making his shoulder the only factor to worry about when considering him in lineups. The Raiders have allowed at least 91 yards to an opposing wideout in three straight weeks, adding confidence to Moore's viability if he proves healthy.

player.seasonOutlook: Moore was traded to Buffalo after spending his first eight NFL seasons with Carolina and Chicago. A featured target throughout most of his career, Moore was reduced to a 16% target share in 2025 -- his lowest since his rookie year in 2018. The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams will seek to convert on more of his looks as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Williams garnered nine targets against the Saints in Week 1, but he reeled in just four of them for 45 yards. The fifth-year wide receiver will need to keep his catch rate well above 50 percent if he hopes to record a third-straight 1,000-yard campaign, but he'll luckily face a Bills defense that allowed the seventh-most PPR points (40.0) to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameson Williams has yet to find the end zone heading into the Lions' Week 4 game at Carolina. Williams totaled a season-high 49 yards against the Jets in Week 3, but he's now recorded four or less catches for 50 or fewer yards in every game this year. The fifth-year wideout will seek to get more out of Detroit's offensive success against a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameson Williams will look to build off a big outing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. Williams had his best game of the year in Week 4 against the Panthers, bringing in six of eight targets for 102 yards. The speedster has still posted just a 16-229-0 receiving line to start the season, but he has seen eight or more targets in two games, which could bode well for his output. He'll also face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jameson Williams will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Williams found the end zone twice in a Week 5 win over the Cardinals before Detroit's bye week, which was done with two catches for 47 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now totaled 18 grabs for 276 yards and two scores on the season. He'll face a Green Bay secondary that's ranked in the middle versus fantasy WRs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Parker Washington can safely be started as a fantasy WR2 in Week 2, even with the Jaguars facing a stout Broncos secondary. Washington paced Jacksonville's pass catchers with five catches for 83 yards and a TD on six targets in the season opener. In his last five games, including the playoffs, Washington has racked up 31 catches, 537 yards, and four TDs. Fellow Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) tends to draw significant defensive attention, which should keep top Broncos CB Patrick Surtain from shadowing Washington as long as Thomas suits up.
outlooksByWeek.3: Parker Washington has established himself as the No. 1 WR for the Jaguars and is headed toward weekly fantasy WR1 territory ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Patriots. New England has one of the league's best secondaries, led by CB Christian Gonzalez, but Washington appears largely matchup-proof considering the 24-year-old WR just accounted for 98 of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards in a Week 2 loss to Denver that could wind up being Lawrence's worst performance of the season. Washington has at least five catches and 83 receiving yards in each of his last five games, as well as three touchdown catches over that span, so the breakout star can be started with confidence regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Parker Washington has entered set-and-forget fantasy WR1 territory. Jacksonville's top wideout is likely to thrive in Week 4 against a suspect Bengals secondary that just allowed touchdowns to Steelers WRs Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek. Despite facing the strong Cleveland, Denver, and New England secondaries, Washington is averaging 74 yards per game with two TDs through three weeks to start 2026 after averaging 116 receiving yards and scoring twice in the final three games of the 2025 regular season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Parker Washington has recorded just 47 receiving yards on eight targets over Jacksonville's last two games after turning 18 targets into 181 yards over the preceding two games. Washington could have an easier time getting back on track in Week 5 if the Eagles are without top cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee). Philadelphia's secondary still has plenty of talent but hasn't been nearly as effective this year, allowing four touchdown catches to WRs after holding the position to six TDs in the entire 2025 regular season. Washington leads the Jaguars in all receiving categories and remains a fantasy WR2 at worst despite the recent hiccup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Parker Washington bounced back from a seven-yard Week 4 dud with his best game of the season in Week 5, racking up 124 yards and two TDs against the Eagles. Jacksonville's No. 1 receiver is averaging 70 yards per game and has four TDs through five outings while leading the Jaguars in every receiving category. Washington can be penciled in as a fantasy WR1 for Week 6 against a Texans pass defense that has been surprisingly weak, allowing 193 receiving yards per game to wideouts and six TDs in five games to the position, making it one of the five most generous defenses against wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: A strong finish to the 2025 season has made Washington one of the fascinating breakout candidates of 2026. Though he's primarily worked as a situational/depth player since being drafted in the sixth round in 2023, Washington has flashed when asked to play a bigger role. In 21 games since the start of 2024 in which he had a route participation above 50%, Washington handled a 20% target share and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG. He surprisingly emerged as Jacksonville's top target late last season, which included a stretch of four straight games with at least nine targets and 19 fantasy points to end the season. The 24-year-old appears to have cemented a big role in Jacksonville, though Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and perhaps Travis Hunter will battle him for snaps and targets. Washington should be targeted for your flex spot.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel in Week 2 to face the Patriots, who have the ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to RBs. He rushed 10 times for 46 yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 20-13 win against Atlanta. Warren lost a fumble, but he still out-touched fellow RB Rico Dowdle 15-10 and had much better results from those opportunities. If the Steelers continue to favor the passing game against New England, or if they're forced into it via game flow, Warren would carry a bit more value in what looks to be a true timeshare.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Bengals to town for a Week 3 AFC North matchup. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and brought in two of four targets for 34 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Warren handled 11 of 20 carries from backs in this one, but the Steelers weren't able to get much going on offense. It looks like he's the 1A out of the backfield, and although it's not by a substantial amount, Rico Dowdle is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday with a toe injury. Warren faces a 14th-ranked Cincinnati defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He rushed 17 times for 127 yards and caught three of four targets for 49 yards during Pittsburgh's thrilling 30-27 victory in Week 3. Warren handled a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out, and it looks like that could again be the case with a short turnaround for Week 4's Thursday Night Football showcase in Cleveland. He'll face a tough matchup as the Browns rank sixth in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs and are one of seven teams yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town in Week 5. He tallied 17 carries for 93 yards while catching three of six targets for 33 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Warren handled a massive workload for the second straight week with Rico Dowdle (toe) on the sidelines. There's a chance Dowdle remains out against Indianapolis, leaving Warren as the unquestioned lead back versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense, which has allowed 24.2 fantasy points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and caught all six of his targets for 87 yards, including an 80-yard TD reception, during Pittsburgh's Week 5 win. Warren continued to handle a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out for the third straight contest. He compiled 490 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 61 touches over that stretch, and head coach Mike McCarthy stated Monday that Warren is viewed as "our featured player right now." Even if Dowdle can suit up versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) in Week 6, Warren is likely to keep working as the lead back for a Steelers offense averaging 29.3 points through their last three outings.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers face off against the Saints in Paris in Week 7. He had 14 carries for 50 yards and caught two of four targets for 28 yards during Pittsburgh's overtime victory in Week 6. With Rico Dowdle (toe) back on the field, Warren's opportunities dipped noticeably despite out-touching Dowdle 16-10. He should still handle a larger volume than Dowdle going forward, but managers should certainly temper expectations as long as both backs are healthy. Warren draws a very favorable matchup against a New Orleans defense that ranks dead last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trevor Lawrence is off to an inconsistent start this season, with seven touchdown passes in two home games but just one touchdown pass in two road games. The Jaguars are the nominal home team in Week 5 against the Eagles, but the game will be played in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium rather than in Jacksonville. Given Lawrence's struggles away from home coupled with a matchup against an Eagles defense that has allowed just four touchdown passes in as many games, this could be a week to look elsewhere at QB if a viable alternative is available on your bench or waiver wire. Jacksonville's passing game has enough upside for Lawrence to deliver a starter-level performance, but his floor is well below that.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trevor Lawrence threw for a season-high 331 yards against the Eagles as the Jaguars improved to 4-1 with a Week 5 win. He brings a 10:3 TD:INT into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans, which will be the Jaguars' second consecutive game in London. Houston has surprisingly been one of the league's most generous pass defenses, allowing QBs to throw for 256 yards per game, though the Texans have allowed only six TDs through the air. Lawrence produced just 380 passing yards with a 1:2 TD:INT in two meetings with the AFC South rival Texans in 2025, but since Houston's defense has taken a step back this season, Lawrence can continue to be deployed as a starting fantasy QB for Week 6.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Kincaid will look to match a career outing when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Kincaid had a personal-best 130 yards in his season debut but, more importantly, played 77% of the team's snaps after topping 50% just three times last year. If Kincaid remains on the field at this rate, he's likely to soar past his previous season's output. He'll face a defense on Thursday night that allowed 87 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends in Week 1, suggesting his statistical surge can continue.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Kincaid brings momentum into the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. After a 130-yard opener, Kincaid posted seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against Detroit, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps. Opportunity, not talent, has been an issue as he hasn't played over a 50% snap share since Week 5 in 2025. The Chargers were dominated by Tre McBride in Week 1 but rebounded against the Brock Bowers-less Raiders tight end room last week. Kincaid's big numbers are poised to continue in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Kincaid will seek to rebuild momentum when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. After gaining 225 yards in Weeks 1 and 2, Kincaid had just two catches for 38 yards in Week 3. Part of the decrease in volume could be DJ Moore's return to health, but Buffalo remains run-heavy, limiting Kincaid's looks. He recorded a 67% snap share, more than usual, so opportunity remains. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dalton Kincaid faces an uphill battle for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Rams in Week 5. He is coming off a season-low seven yards on two targets (one catch), and after a productive two-game start, has only five targets in Weeks 3 and 4. The Rams have defended tight ends at an elite level, allowing a mere 2.9 yards per target and only 85 total yards through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills' passing game is shrinking ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. After snagging 12 of 14 targets in his first two games, Kincaid has been limited to four catches on seven targets over the last three weeks, amassing just 52 yards. His snap share remains strong and elevated from 2025; Buffalo just seems more inclined to be a run-first offense. Las Vegas has allowed six touchdowns to opposing tight ends, resulting in the fifth-most fantasy points allowed to the position. Kincaid can be a viable starting option in a favorable bounce-back matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Kincaid is perhaps fantasy's biggest wild card among tight ends. The 2023 first-round pick has occasionally flashed a high ceiling (he actually led qualified tight ends in YPT and YPRR last season), but he also has missed substantial action (nine games the past two years) and has disappeared way too often (he failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in any game in 2024, and never cleared six targets in a game in 2025). Kincaid was limited to a 37% snap share when active last season, and he has yet to finish a season better than 14th in fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old has TE1 upside, but he's tough to trust and has added target competition (WR DJ Moore) in 2026. Consider Kincaid only in the mid-to-late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Johnson paced New Orleans' tight ends in yards (53) during the Week 1 overtime loss but trailed Noah Fant in receptions (three to four) and targets (seven to eight). Despite this, Johnson was on the field for 72 of the Saints' 90 offensive snaps, where Fant played just 37. Thus, Johnson is expected to remain New Orleans' top TE option against a Ravens defense that allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points to the position in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of New Orleans' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite a dip in snap rate and route share compared to Week 1, Johnson paced the Saints' tight end corps in receptions, targets and yards in Week 2. He ranks third on the team in targets and yards, which is a positive outlook for his value going forward. However, Johnson is in for an unfavorable matchup, as Las Vegas' defense has allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top weapons in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Johnson has been New Orleans' second-most productive receiver this season, catching 15 of 19 targets for 173 yards and three touchdowns. With head coach Kellen Moore's offense throwing the ball an average of 44 times per game through three weeks, Johnson is expected to remain one of fantasy's top tight ends going forward. Additionally, he's in for a terrific Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed 17.2 PPR fantasy points per game to the TE position this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Johnson had another productive outing in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons, catching six of eight targets for 59 yards. He's now tallied 232 receiving yards through four contests this season, the fourth-most amongst tight ends. Johnson will likely continue to benefit from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense that's averaged 45 pass attempts per game this year. Despite this, Johnson is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 7.7 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Johnson tallied just 16 yards on four receptions in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, struggling alongside the rest of New Orleans' offense. Despite this, he's tied for the second-most receptions (25) on the Saints through five weeks, accumulating 248 yards and three touchdowns. Expect Johnson to bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's allowed 14.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Juwan Johnson will look to bounce back from a lackluster performance in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Johnson has struggled over the last two weeks, catching just four of seven targets for 16 yards. Despite this, he remains third on the team in targets (35), receptions (25) and yards (248) through six games, suggesting more fantasy production in the near future. Johnson is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, however, as Pittsburgh's defense has allowed just 11.7 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson's impressive progression continued in 2025, as the converted wide receiver posted career-high marks in targets, catches, yardage and fantasy points (all four were eighth or better among tight ends). Johnson produced nine top-12 fantasy weeks, which tied for second at the position. He has finished in the top 12 in aDOT each of the past four seasons but hasn't been much of an option near the goal line (no more than four TDs or end zone targets in each of the past three seasons). The 29-year-old has added target competition, including eighth-overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy), but he very well could settle in as high as third in target priority in the Saints' Tyler Shough-led offense. Johnson is a fine TE2.

Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 2 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's now been placed on IR for the injury. The fifth-year running back (30 of 65 offensive snaps) and Aaron Jones (29 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps against the Packers, with Mason leading the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Unfortunately, Mason will now be out for at least the next four weeks, priming Jones for a bigger role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 3 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's been placed on IR for the injury. Mason will remain sidelined for at least the next three weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 4 as the Vikings take on the Dolphins. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next two weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 5 as the Vikings travel to New Orleans. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next week, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Mason could be set to return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Mason has been sidelined since Week 1 with a thumb injury that landed him on IR, but he's set to return to practice this week. The fifth-year running back's return should put him at least in a complementary role with veteran Aaron Jones. Indianapolis' defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Mason is back for his second season in Minnesota and will battle 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. for backfield opportunities. Mason's role was almost exactly as expected last season, as he was utilized often as a rusher (9.9 carries per game), but a nonfactor as a receiver (1.0 targets per game). Mason reached 13 fantasy points just once in his 16 games and it was a 23.6-point effort in Week 3, one of five games Jones missed. Mason, 27, is an effective rusher -- his 5.10 YPC ranks third and his 2.42 YAC second among 54 RBs with 350-plus carries since he entered the league -- but adding so little as a receiver (34 career targets) severely limits his fantasy output. Even if Jones were to miss time, Mason would max out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyler Murray's status is up in the air as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Murray went down early in Week 1 against the Packers after taking a hard hit to the head. Before his exit, Murray completed three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception, tacking on two rushes for nine yards on the ground. The veteran is now under evaluation for a concussion, which could very likely keep him sidelined for an extended period. Backup quarterback Carson Wentz delivered the win for Minnesota, and he's set to assume QB duties once again. The Bears gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in Week 1, so big output could definitely be in the cards for whoever lines up under center for the Vikings.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyler Murray will return to the field as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Murray has cleared concussion protocol after suffering a nasty hit early in Week 1. The veteran quarterback will finally get the chance to prove himself, especially given that he completed just three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception before his opening-game departure. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.4 fantasy points per game to QBs across its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyler Murray will aim to build on a serviceable performance as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Murray returned to the field in Week 3 versus the Buccaneers, completing 15 of 29 passes for 168 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, along with rushing the ball twice for 17 yards. The veteran quarterback also lost star wideout Justin Jefferson in the first half, so his final output and delivery of a win were more impressive. Miami has been much more favorable against quarterbacks than Tampa so far this season, allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game (23.7) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyler Murray will look to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. In his second full start of the year, Murray completed 27 of 37 passes for 247 yards, but he was unable to find the end zone. The veteran quarterback also now holds a 1:2 TD:INT through his three appearances this season, so he'll need to do more for Minnesota to lock him down as a long-term option. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyler Murray will look to keep the Vikings rolling in Week 7 against the Colts. Murray recorded his best game of the season against the Saints heading into Minnesota's bye, completing 80 percent of passes for 229 yards and a touchdown, with 10 rushes for 51 yards. The veteran quarterback could be a dangerous threat moving forward, especially if he can get it going on the ground once again. He'll face an Indy defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Murray signed with the Vikings after spending his first seven seasons with the Cardinals. The change comes after a disappointing and injury-shortened 2025 season in which he failed to clear 18.3 fantasy points in any of his five appearances. Murray has settled in as an accurate but conservative passer and continues to add value with his legs (78-572-5 in 17 games in 2024). Prior to the 2025 dud, Murray had finished each of his first six NFL seasons as a top-12 fantasy QB (points per game). Now that he beat out J.J. McCarthy for Minnesota's starting job, he'll have the luxury of working with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. Add that to his rushing ability, and the 29-year-old certainly could find his way into the weekly QB1 mix. Consider Murray in the middle to late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's top receiver in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns, whose defense struggled against wideouts in Week 1. Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top receiving option in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, whose defense has given up 38.9 PPR fantasy points to WRs this season. Egbuka had a rough Week 2 outing, finishing third on Tampa Bay in receptions (three) and targets (five) while slotting in at fifth in yards (16). However, he did score a touchdown and was on the field for 85 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting he'll remain the team's WR1. He's set for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that gave up just three points and 163 passing yards to the Bears in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emeka Egbuka will remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Despite another relatively underwhelming Week 3 performance (5-62-0), Egbuka clearly remains atop Tampa Bay's receiving corps, leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be sidelined in Week 4, which suggests Egbuka will likely see less opportunities. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka is in for a favorable matchup against a Green Bay defense that's allowed 34.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Emeka Egbuka will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Egbuka was targeted just four times during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, his lowest mark of the season. While Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains sidelined and Jalon Daniels acts as the Buccaneers' signal caller, Egbuka may continue receiving less opportunities. However, he's in for a great Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's given up 36.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Egbuka had a good bounce-back performance in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, catching six of nine targets for 38 yards while adding 14 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Despite a relatively underwhelming start to the season, Egbuka still leads Tampa Bay in yards (192), targets (33) and receptions (21) through five games. He could struggle in Week 6 against a Pittsburgh secondary that's allowed just 27.7 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Egbuka had his most promising game of the 2026 season in the overtime loss to the Steelers, turning a whopping 16 targets into seven receptions for 48 yards and a score. Tampa Bay's offense has struggled without Baker Mayfield (thumb), averaging just 167 passing yards per game since his injury. Despite this, Egbuka has remained productive and could benefit from the potential return of Mayfield in Week 7. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka could struggle against a Panthers defense that's allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Omarion Hampton scored a touchdown for the third time in four games during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but his role in the backfield continues to slip. The second-year back's nine carries and 11 touches were season lows for a spark for his unit. Hampton has still been the most productive of the trio this season with 267 scrimmage yards and three rushing TDs, but his 4.0 yards per carry trails Mitchell's, while Keaton Mitchell handled 15 touches and Kimani Vidal got seven, indicating that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is moving toward a full-blown committee as he searches 4.6 mark. Hampton will try to re-establish himself as the clear No. 1 on the depth chart in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Omarion Hampton continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme while working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line. Hampton does have three rushing touchdowns in five games, but his 3.7 yards per carry is a significant downturn from his 4.4 mark as a rookie, and he's averaging just 61.2 scrimmage yards per contest. He's also lost snaps and touches to Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as the backfield devolves into a committee. Hampton will try to find a spark in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Etienne is expected to remain New Orleans' top running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Alvin Kamara (knee) being sidelined for the Week 1 overtime loss, Etienne only received nine carries, tying Kendre Miller for the most on the team. However, Etienne was busy as a receiver, catching seven of nine targets for 46 yards, which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. He could be in for another productive week, as Baltimore's defense allowed 28.1 PPR fantasy points to running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Etienne is expected operate as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite signing a big contract with the Saints this past offseason, Etienne saw just 10 opportunities in the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He still leads the team in carries (17) but saw less work through the air, with Alvin Kamara (five catches on six targets) returning to the lineup. With Kamara back, Etienne may struggle to be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 17.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Etienne signed with the Saints after spending the first five seasons of his pro career with the Jaguars. The 2021 first-round pick has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. A capable rusher and receiver, Etienne has already reached 1,000-plus rushing yards three times and has 35-plus catches in each of the past four seasons. Even if the Saints retain Alvin Kamara as a situational player, Etienne will have a clear path to feature-back duties in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough. That will be enough to position the 27-year-old for his third top-15 fantasy campaign in four years. Consider Etienne a solid RB2 target with backend RB1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carnell Tate tied for the team lead in receiving yards during his NFL debut, but he had just 38 yards on six targets as Titans QB Cam Ward threw for a meager 140 yards. Tennessee's passing game is likely to struggle again in Week 2 against Philadelphia's excellent secondary, led by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Tate is likely to maintain a prominent role on the rebuilding Titans after being drafted fourth overall out of Ohio State, but the rookie WR is hard to trust as anything more than a fantasy WR3 or flex play until Tennessee's offense shows some life.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carnell Tate is off to an uninspiring start, with seven catches for 65 yards on 11 targets through two games with the Titans. A Week 3 road game against the injury-riddled Giants presents a nice opportunity for the rookie fourth overall pick out of Ohio State to break out, as the Giants just allowed 195 receiving yards and two TDs to Rams WR Davante Adams. Tate leads his team in targets through two games, but the Titans have struggled to move the ball through the air. Given Tate's draft pedigree and matchup, he's a high-ceiling fantasy WR3 for Week 3, though it's fair for fantasy managers to be hesitant given the highly touted rookie's lackluster production so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Carnell Tate has 20 targets through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 road game against the Ravens, turning that decent volume into a pedestrian 13 catches for 123 yards, averaging 41 yards per game. Tennessee's entire passing game is tough to trust given the struggles of QB Cam Ward, but Tate has the most upside among the team's pass catchers. A Week 4 breakout is possible against a Ravens defense that has given up the second-most catches to WRs, especially if the Titans fall behind and are forced to air it out, but Tate can't be trusted as anything more than a flex option until Ward shows signs of progress.
outlooksByWeek.5: Carnell Tate broke out in Week 4 against the Ravens, recording 145 receiving yards after totaling just 123 yards over his first three games for the Titans. The rookie fourth-overall pick has been limited by the struggles of second-year QB Cam Ward, who is averaging just 182 passing yards per game. Tate is likely to match up frequently with top Texans CB Derek Stingley in Week 5, but Stingley and company have allowed the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and touchdown receptions (six) to wide receivers. With Tate trending in the right direction, he's a high-upside flex option for Week 5 as the promising rookie continues to search for his first NFL touchdown.
outlooksByWeek.6: Carnell Tate crashed back down to earth in Week 5, producing just one catch for six yards against the Texans while playing through a back injury after breaking out for a career-high 145 receiving yards against the Eagles in Week 4. Tennessee's fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will likely remain a boom-or-bust fantasy option throughout his rookie campaign while occupying a starting role in what has been the worst offense in the league. A Week 6 road game against the Colts appears more likely to deliver a peak than a valley, assuming Tate is close to full health, as Indianapolis is giving up 160 receiving yards per game and 15 yards per catch to wideouts. Tate is a high-ceiling Week 6 flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Carnell Tate had 70 receiving yards and his first NFL touchdown in Tennessee's Week 6 win over the Colts and broke out for 145 receiving yards against the Ravens in Week 4, but he was held to just six yards by the Texans in between. The rookie, fourth overall pick is still searching for consistency in a Titans passing game that ranks among the league's worst, but Tate has shown enough upside to warrant a lineup spot as a flex option in most formats heading into a Week 7 home game against the Browns. Cleveland has been weaker than league average at defending wide receivers, allowing 157 yards per game and seven TDs in six games to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Tate was selected by the Titans with the fourth overall pick of April's draft. He didn't see a ton of volume at Ohio State, but he was efficient, averaging 13.1 yards per target (first in this rookie WR class) and 3.06 yards per route run (third) in 2025. He also paced the class in YPT for his career (11.6) and caught an impressive 75% of his targets during the 39-game span. Tate underwhelmed in the 40-yard dash at the combine (4.53 at 192 pounds), but he measured in with big hands and a large wingspan. Wide receivers selected in the top 10 handle, on average, one-quarter of their team's targets and generally deliver WR2/3 fantasy production. Cam Ward's development will be key here, but Tate's combination of talent and projected target volume is enough to make him an appealing WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harold Fannin and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2, facing the 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (25.1) to TEs. The second-year pro managed two catches on three targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 loss in the season opener. Fannin has the perfect chance at a rebound performance against Tampa Bay, as Cincinnati's Mike Gesicki cooked their defense with five receptions for 78 yards and a TD in Week 1. Even with poor quarterback play, Fannin has the talent and opportunity as the focal point of an offense that might not be good but will be forced to throw the ball plenty while playing from behind.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harold Fannin and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3 for their 2026 home opener. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with five catches on six targets for 54 yards. Fannin is still searching for his first TD of the season after collecting six as a rookie, as fellow tight end Blake Whiteheart was on the receiving end of a 17-yard score from Deshaun Watson. Fannin looks to find the end zone against Carolina's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns host their division rival Steelers in Week 4 for an AFC North clash between two 2-1 teams. He caught seven of nine targets for 51 yards and two TDs during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3, including the game-winning score. Fannin led the team in receptions and yardage while tying KC Concepcion for first in targets. He now has a 12-126-2 line on 18 targets across three contests as one of Deshaun Watson's favorite receivers. Fannin will have a tough matchup against Pittsburgh's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.3) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns look to stay hot and earn a fourth consecutive victory against the Jets in a Week 5 road clash. He caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. The second-year tight end now has three combined TDs over his last two outings. Fannin should once again be a featured target for Deshaun Watson versus the Jets' ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (10.2) to TEs. They have yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are back home to host the Ravens for an AFC North divisional tilt in Week 6. It was a quiet day for the sophomore tight end, as he caught just one of four targets for four yards during Cleveland's 17-12 defeat in Week 5. Fannin notched at least 50 receiving yards or caught a touchdown in three straight outings prior to this dud, so fantasy managers can blame the poor showing on weather. He'll look to get back into the end zone versus a Baltimore defense that surrendered five receptions for 42 yards and a TD to Kyle Pitts Sr. in their last outing.
outlooksByWeek.7: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are in Tennessee for an interconference clash in Week 7. He caught one of three targets for nine yards during Cleveland's 13-10 Week 6 win. Following a three-game stretch in which he recorded a 15-132-3 receiving line on 20 targets, Fannin has now gone two straight outings with one reception and fewer than 10 yards. The second-year TE will try to bounce back versus a Titans defense allowing 10.5 fantasy points per game (T-7th) to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Fannin is a rising star at the tight end position after overcoming the presence of David Njoku and a quarterback merry-go-round to produce a 72-731-6 receiving line (plus 7-13-1 rushing) as a 21-year-old rookie last season. The third-round pick's 108 targets rank eighth all time by a rookie tight end, and he finished no lower than eighth at the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points last season. Fannin figures to see some touchdown regression (seven TDs, 3.8 expected, three end zone targets) and Cleveland still has quarterback question marks, but with Njoku gone, Fannin has a path to improve a bit on what was already a healthy 22% target share. He's a solid TE1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dak Prescott was held to just 175 passing yards in the season opener for the Cowboys.  Dak did toss two touchdowns, but he also threw a costly interception before the end of the first half, which led to a Giants touchdown. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Dak with an uninspiring output. Prescott will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dak Prescott tossed four touchdowns last game in a virtuoso performance for the Cowboys. Prescott completed 26-of-31 throws for 279 yards and the four scores in the dominant 37-20 win over the Commanders. Prescott has six touchdowns and just one pick through the first two games of the young season. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dak Prescott threw for 276 yards and a touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens last game. Dak has passed for at least 275 yards through the air in each of the last two contests for the Cowboys, while also failing to toss a single interception over that span. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
