outlooksByWeek.5: Dak Prescott crossed the 300-yard passing mark last game for the Cowboys for the first time in 2026. Prescott actually threw for 335 yards in the thrilling comeback win over the Texans. More than half of the yards came via CeeDee Lamb, as the duo combined for a staggering 17 of Dak's 32 completions. Dak has eight passing scores and just one interception through four games. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dak Prescott went over the 300-yard passing mark for the second-straight game for Dallas. Unfortunately, Dak threw just one touchdown pass for the second-consecutive contest, while also tossing two picks in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Nevertheless, Dak is currently fourth in the NFL in passing yards, and tied for eighth in the league in passing touchdowns. However, in Week 6, Dallas will face a Green Bay defense allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered just six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dak Prescott has thrown four interceptions in his last two games for the Cowboys. While Dak has also thrown for over 250 yards in five-straight outings, he has passed for one touchdown apiece in four consecutive contests. Dallas has lost three of those four games. He will look to right the ship in Week 7 versus division foe Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Prescott is entering his 11th NFL season following a successful 2025 campaign in which he led the NFL in completions and ranked no lower than fourth in dropbacks, pass attempts, passing yards and passing TDs. Prescott appeared in all 17 games and has now finished no worse than 11th in fantasy points during all seven seasons in which he has played at least 16 games. Last season, his nine top-10 fantasy weeks were tied for third most at the position. Prescott is no longer much of a threat with his legs, but he should continue to put up big passing numbers with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at his disposal. The 33-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in targets last game. Likely saw a staggering 12 balls thrown his way en route to seven catches for 66 yards in the win over Arizona. However, fellow tight end Theo Johnson stole a touchdown from him. Still, Likely's renewed usage with quarterback Jameis Winston under center was a pleasant surprise, as Likely only had five targets in the prior game versus Tennessee. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 5 versus Washington. The Commanders defense has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Likely exploded for 11 receptions and two touchdowns last game for the Giants. The 11 receptions set a career high, and Likely scored twice for the second time in five contests. Likely has a staggering 25 targets over the last two outings alone. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaiah Likely has remained extremely busy for the Giants, regardless of who lines up at quarterback. Likely has received double-digit targets in four of the last five games for the G-Men. Likely has scored three times in the last two contests, and five times on the season overall. Likely leads all NFL tight ends in receiving yards and touchdowns, and is second in receptions to Trey McBride. Likely should be primed for another big outing in Week 7 versus the Texans. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Makai Lemon was listed as the No. 3 wideout for the Eagles heading into their Week 1 clash with Washington. Unfortunately, Lemon lost five yards on three catches in his NFL debut.  On the bright side, he was targeted four times and was one of only three Eagles receivers to record a catch. Better outputs lie ahead, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans surrendered 215 yards passing to Geno Smith of the Jets in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Makai Lemon had just one catch in Philadelphia's win over Tennessee. Lemon is battling with Darius Cooper for the No. 3 wideout spot, as Dontayvion Wicks has all but claimed No. 2 for his own. Lemon had just one target last game, while Cooper had three and Wicks managed six. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Makai Lemon is coming off his best game as a member of the Eagles.  Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Lemon managed three catches and 29 yards on four targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Lemon has yet to find the end zone as a rookie. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Makai Lemon saw a career-high six targets last game for the Eagles. With DeVonta Smith shelved due to a hamstring ailment, Lemon finished with the second-most targets on the team behind Darius Cooper.  However, the Philadelphia passing game struggled mightily overall, with no wideout gaining more than 33 yards through the air. While Smith should remain sidelined for Week 5, it remains to be seen how the targets will be divided between Lemon, Cooper and Dontayvion Wicks. Nevertheless, an intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. Lemon was targeted seven times en route to five catches for 43 yards in the 19-17 loss to the Jags. Lemon has 13 targets in his last two outings. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has boosted the opportunities for Lemon, a trend that could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. In addition, the Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Makai Lemon caught three passes for 19 yards last game for the Eagles. Lemon was third on the team in targets with six, though the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap Lemon's upside as well.  In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Lemon was selected by the Eagles with the 20th overall pick of April's draft. Lemon is on the small side (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), but he posted a 3.04 YPRR (best in this rookie class) during his collegiate career, dropping only three of 190 career targets (his 1.6% drop rate also paced this class). Lemon, who aligned in the slot on 74% of his collegiate routes, posted a dominant 79-1,156-11 receiving line in 2025, while also contributing as a rusher (two TDs) and returner. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon will battle Dontayvion Wicks for No. 2 work opposite DeVonta Smith. Lemon's skill set provides him with upside, but with plenty of mouths to feed in Philly's low-volume pass offense, he's best valued as a flex option in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeMario Douglas will seek more production in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. He logged a reasonable seven targets to open the season but turned that into just 20 yards on five grabs. Douglas has a rapport with QB Drake Maye as a safety valve, and while snaps seem safe with A.J. Brown (ankle) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Douglas topped 40 yards just four times last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeMario Douglas' role in New England's struggling passing offense is questionable ahead of a Week 3 game at Jacksonville. In Week 2, Douglas logged just two targets in his first full game without A.J. Brown after a seven-target opener, and he's averaging just 4.8 yards per reception to start the season. Jacksonville is allowing a hefty 10.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but Douglas' inability to stretch the field would require uncharacteristic heavy volume to provide a modest fantasy return.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeMario Douglas hasn't been consistently targeted in the Patriots struggling passing attack ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Douglas has just one catch in each of his last two games, and while last week's popped for 38 yards, he's averaging just 9.4 yards on his seven snags to date. Buffalo's defense has been friendly to opposing wideouts, allowing 9.3 ypt with six receivers going for 40+ yards, but with limited volume, Douglas doesn't seem destined to exploit that.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeMario Douglas hasn't emerged in the Patriots' receiving corps ahead of a Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. Despite A.J. Brown's continued absence, Douglas has just four total catches over the last three weeks, tallying 62 yards. An uptick in volume appears unlikely against an exploitable secondary that allows 8.2 yards per target, leaving Douglas as a dart throw as opposed to a reliable lineup option.
outlooksByWeek.6: DeMario Douglas faces an uphill battle to match Week 5's success when the Patriots face the Jets in Week 6. Douglas shined with two touchdowns and a season-high 65 yards against the Raiders, but he's still hauled in no more than two balls in three of five outings while being held to 38 yards or fewer in his first four games. New England is spreading the ball around in its surging passing attack, so Douglas seems unlikely to retain heavy volume. The Jets have allowed four opposing receivers to register 63 yards or more in the last two weeks, giving Douglas a shot at some upside.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeMario Douglas is emerging as a viable option for the Patriots ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Bears. Over the past two weeks, Douglas has garnered 13 targets, turning them into 11 catches and three touchdowns. Though A.J. Brown is back from an ankle injury, New England could be without Romeo Doubs due to a shoulder ailment, suggesting Douglas' place in the receiving pecking order may be unchanged, giving him a chance to post solid numbers against a secondary that's allowed nine opposing receivers to gain at least 55 yards.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
outlooksByWeek.4: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tony Pollard is averaging 61 scrimmage yards per game and scored his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Ravens, though that wasn't enough to keep the Titans from dropping to 0-4. In Week 5, Tennessee hosts the AFC South rival Texans, who are also 0-4. The Titans should manage to stay within striking distance and give Pollard his full workload on the ground, though Houston has held RBs to just 91 scrimmage yards per game. Pollard is a high-floor, low-ceiling flex play as usual for Week 5 given his role as the lead back in a struggling Titans offense that's averaging the fewest yards and second-fewest points per game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tony Pollard remains a viable flex option in Week 6 against the Colts thanks to his high touch floor as the starting RB in a putrid Titans offense. Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season but has been limited to one TD on a Titans offense that has found the end zone just six times through five games. Indianapolis is giving up 100 rushing yards per game to RBs as well as a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to the position, so Pollard has a higher ceiling than usual in this Week 6 matchup to go with his steady floor.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tony Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in each of the Titans' last five games. He's locked into a high touch floor in any game the 1-5 Titans can keep within striking distance, and Tennessee is unlikely to fall too far behind in Week 7 at home against the Browns, who are scoring just 17.7 points per game, tied for fourth-fewest in the NFL. Cleveland has started 4-2 thanks to a stout defense that's allowing 20.3 points per game and has allowed just one TD to a running back all season, but Pollard's hefty usage keeps him locked in as a viable flex play for Week 7, even though he looks unlikely to add to his season total of one TD in a Titans offense that's tied for the worst in the league at 14.0 points per game.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals take on the Texans, who ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs in Week 2. After a two-catch, 12-yard dud in the season opener, he'll be aiming for a big bounce-back performance against a vulnerable secondary. Chase logged just four targets in Week 1 despite 35 pass attempts from Joe Burrow. The QB-WR duo should be primed for a rebound against a Houston defense that gave up 409 total yards at home last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to square off against the Steelers' second-ranked pass defense in Week 3. Pittsburgh is allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs and is one of six teams that have yet to give up a receiving TD to the position. Chase will surely put that to the test, as he's coming off a 7-75-2 receiving line on nine targets in Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. Across two outings versus the division-rival Steelers in 2025, Chase registered a 19-191-1 line on 33 targets, so Joe Burrow will continue to feed his star wideout regardless of the matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and his third receiving touchdown of the season during Cincinnati's Week 3 defeat. Chase led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets, and it's clear that his two-catch, 12-yard outing in the season opener was a fluke. He should continue garnering a massive target share from star QB Joe Burrow against Jacksonville's 17th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (31.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to face the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Week 4 before leaving Cincinnati's 22-17 loss with a concussion in the second quarter. Chase was evaluated for the injury after his facemask was pulled following a catch, and he'll have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before he can return to practice and play in the upcoming contest versus Miami. If he is indeed active, Chase will be going up against the Dolphins, who rank third in fewest fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are on the road for an AFC North showdown against the Ravens in Week 7. He corralled six of 10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Chase cleared concussion protocol in time to pace his team in all receiving categories, as no other Bengal had more than 25 yards or four targets. He'll once again be the primary offensive threat for Joe Burrow versus the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Chase is fresh off yet another elite fantasy season and he's now finished four of his five NFL campaigns no lower than fifth in fantasy PPG (the exception was 11th in 2023). Chase actually saw a big dip in yardage (1,740 to 1,426), TDs (17 to 8) and fantasy PPG (23.7 to 19.6) from 2024 to 2025 (which was no surprise with Joe Burrow missing nine games), but still put up big numbers thanks to pacing the league in pass routes and targets for the second season in a row. In fact, Chase's 125 receptions make him the third receiver in NFL history with 125-plus catches in multiple seasons. The 26-year-old remains the top target in a high-scoring Bengals offense, and is one of the top players in all of fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyrone Tracy was the third-string running back in the season opener for the Giants while Najee Harris was a healthy scratch in Week 1, though that could change quickly. While Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary look like the 1-2 duo out front, Tracy lost a fumble in the red zone that could have proven costly. Tracy had a rough camp even before the gaffe, so his time on the Giants could be coming to an end. If Tracy does suit up in Week 2, he will act mostly as depth against a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season. The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyrone Tracy was the most productive back last game for the Giants, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown. However, he managed just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches overall. Meanwhile, Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches, Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries and Cam Skattebo did not even register a touch following last week's costly fumble. It will be hard to trust any New York running back until one emerges from the pack. In Week 7, the Giants will also face a stingy Texans run defense. Houston is allowing only 83 rushing yards per contest, which is third in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Tracy is set to compete with Devin Singletary for opportunities in a Giants backfield led by second-year back Cam Skattebo. Tracy has produced 200-plus touches and 1,000-plus yards in each of his first two NFL seasons, but that doesn't tell the full story. Tracy got there as a fifth-round rookie in 2024 by impressing and taking New York's starting gig by Week 5. Last season, he quickly lost lead-back duties to Skattebo, but played a much larger role once Skattebo went down for the season with an injury (9.0 touches per game during Weeks 1-9, but 18.6 per game from Weeks 10-18). Tracy has no standalone fantasy value, but he's effective as a rusher and receiver. That makes the 26-year-old a solid backup who would be worth adding if Skattebo misses additional time.

The Titans finished 25th in fantasy scoring from the D/ST last season, and other than draftees Dl Keldrick Faulk and LB Anthony Hill, didn't do much to substantially upgrade during the offseason. This looks like a one-and-done streamer, as the Titans face the Jets at home, a plus matchup, but are then a no-go in fantasy for the month that follows (PHI, @NYG, @BAL, HOU, @IND).

outlooksByWeek.2: Blake Corum was one of few Rams players to have a good game on offense in their season-opening loss, and he'll look for more success in Week 2 against the Giants. Corum led Los Angeles with 54 rushing yards on just 10 carries versus San Francisco last Thursday, averaging 5.4 YPC after putting up an average of 5.1 YPC during the regular season last year. Kyren Williams remains the Rams' lead back, but there's little doubt that Corum has forced his way into a substantial role as well. The Giants held Dallas' No. 1 RB Javonte Williams to 3.4 YPC on 12 totes in Week 1, though Williams did score a rushing TD and put up a 5-31-1 line through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Blake Corum should continue to be a big part of the Rams' backfield versus the Broncos in Week 3. Against the Giants on Monday Night Football, Corum racked up 79 yards on 12 carries while adding a 13-yard reception. Through two weeks, Corum has 22 carries to Kyren Williams'  23, so the pair appear to be headed for a pretty even workload in 2026. Denver could be vulnerable to both ball carriers, as the Broncos have given up a whopping 5.40 YPC to RBs this season -- third worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Blake Corum will look to bounce back following a quiet Week 3 performance when the Rams visit Philadelphia in Week 4. Corum was held to season-low marks of six carries and 15 yards this past Sunday versus Denver while Kyren Williams put up 158 total yards. Though some expected Corum to challenge Williams for touches even more this season, the latter has emphatically cemented his No. 1 RB role with his strong early-season performance. Both Corum and Williams may need to rely on their work on the ground against the Eagles, who have given up the fewest receiving yards to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Blake Corum will aim to rebound from a pair of quiet games when the Rams host the Bills in Week 5. After after averaging 66.5 rushing yards in Los Angeles' first two games, Corum has totaled just 29 yards on the ground over his past two contests. He's been quite inefficient with his carries, logging just 2.6 yards per carry on his 11 totes while Kyren Williams has dominated backfield touches. Buffalo has given up six TDs to running backs this season, but three have come through the air. That's not Corum's forte -- he has just four catches for 20 yards with no scores as a receiver through four weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Blake Corum's role as a ball carrier seems to fading ahead of the Rams' Week 6 game versus Arizona. Corum rushed just five times for 19 yards Monday against Buffalo, marking his third straight contest with six or fewer carries after averaging 11 totes across the first two weeks. However, Corum did score his first TD of 2026 and had easily his best game this season as a receiver against the Bills, catching three passes for 53 yards. Given his recent downturn in carries, Corum may need to get into the end zone to come away with serviceable fantasy production, but the Cardinals have given up only four total TDs to running backs through five weeks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Blake Corum has developed into a legitimate complementary option in the Rams' backfield to star tailback Kyren Williams, rushing 47 times for 223 yards and a touchdown while adding nine receptions for 91 yards and another score through six games. His 4.7 yards per carry almost equals Williams' 4.9 mark, but the main difference is the touches, as Corum is averaging just 7.8 carries per game compared to Williams' 13.3. Still, Corum faces an encouraging Week 7 matchup against the Raiders, who have surrendered 19.6 fantasy points per game to RBs in 2026, the ninth-worst mark in the NFL.His limited receiving involvement and secondary role make him a touchdown-dependent flex option rather than a dependable weekly starter.

player.seasonOutlook: Corum has spent his first two NFL seasons as Kyren Williams' backup, and that's expected to be the case again in 2026. The 2024 third-round NFL draft pick played well in the role last season, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry (seventh among RBs) and scoring six touchdowns on 145 carries. However, Corum played only 29% of the Rams' snaps and remained a nonfactor as a receiver (36 yards on 14 targets). The 25-year-old has no standalone fantasy value, but he's an elite insurance stash, as he'd launch into the fringe-RB1 mix in the Rams' high-powered offense should Williams miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wan'Dale Robinson stepped up against his former team in Week 3 with seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against the Giants, but he had just 47 yards on seven targets in his first two games with the Titans. The 5-foot-8 wide receiver gets almost all of his production on short passes, but Robinson is a viable Week 4 flex option on the road against the heavily favored Ravens. The winless Titans may find themselves in another deep hole, which could allow Tennessee's low-octane passing game to make up for a lack of quality with quantity. Baltimore has allowed the second-most catches to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Wan'Dale Robinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans, but he's averaging just 31 receiving yards per game as a Titan after coming over from the Giants in free agency. Houston has been surprisingly poor at defending wide receivers, allowing the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and TDs (six) to the position. Robinson's inconsistent usage in a low-octane passing game makes him hard to trust, but he's a viable flex option for Week 5 given the Texans' struggles against his position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Wan'Dale Robinson is averaging just 35 receiving yards per game for the Titans heading into a Week 6 road affair against the Colts, who are allowing 160 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Robinson has drawn at least five targets from Cam Ward in all but one game this season, and his steady involvement makes him a viable flex play for Week 6 against the Colts' beatable pass defense. However, Robinson's ceiling is capped due to the poor play of Tennessee's entire offense, which ranks last leaguewide with 11.6 points per game. Two of Ward's three touchdown passes through five games have gone to Robinson.
outlooksByWeek.7: Wan'Dale Robinson drew 30 targets from Titans QB Cam Ward over the past four games. Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll loved peppering Robinson with short targets when they were together on the Giants, and Daboll has maintained that philosophy in their new surroundings. Robinson has caught 19 of those 30 targets for 151 yards and two TDs, and his consistent involvement in Tennessee's offense gives him a respectable floor as a solid Week 7 flex option against the Browns, who are giving up 157 yards per game to WRs and have allowed seven TDs to the position through six games. Robinson and QB Cam Ward are the only Titans with multiple TDs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson signed with the Titans after catching 90-plus passes each of the past two seasons. The 2022 second-round pick has progressively improved his production each season in the pros, peaking with a 30% target share (ninth among WRs), 1,014 yards (13th) and 13.6 fantasy PPG (16th) in 2025. An undersized, short-range slot target, Robinson isn't positioned for many big plays and is very rarely used near the goal line (he's yet to clear four TDs in a season and has 13 career end zone targets). In Tennessee, Robinson will battle rookie Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley for the team lead in targets, but his potential for flex production will depend on whether Cam Ward is able to make a Year 2 leap. Robinson, 25, is a low-ceiling, middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Nix was held in check by the Kansas City defense in the Broncos' season opener, completing 17 of 28 passes for just 131 yards and a touchdown. He also threw an interception and committed three fumbles, losing one of them, while getting sacked four times. Nix also wasn't able to take advantage of his newest asset, as Jaylen Waddle logged only three targets and caught one of them for two yards. It was a hugely disappointing effort from Nix and the reigning AFC West champions, but they'll look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked 18th last season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Nix rebounded from a sluggish opener to lead the Broncos to a comeback win over the Jaguars in Week 2. The third-year QB has a meager 2:2 TD:INT through two games and has yet to add any production on the ground, but his 288 passing yards In Week 2 were more than double the Week 1 total, and his completion rate jumped from 60.7% to 71.0%. Nix also began establishing some chemistry with new top wideout Jaylen Waddle, who erupted for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets. Nix will face a Rams defense in Week 3 that has held opposition QBs under a 60% completion rate to begin the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bo Nix engineered an impressive second-half comeback in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, producing two passing TDs and one rushing score despite completing just 50.0% of his passes. The third-year quarterback hasn't had a statistically impressive start to the season, posting a 4:3 TD:INT ratio and passing for barely over 200 yards a game, but Nix has led his team to a 2-1 record. He'll take on a 49ers defense in Week 4 that's been stingy to begin the year, ranking eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bo Nix wasn't able to pull off another comeback win for the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers. The third-year QB failed to complete 60% of his passes for a second straight game, and through four weeks, he's produced just six touchdowns (five passing, one rushing) while committing four turnovers. Denver's lack of a consistent running game isn't helping the offense find a rhythm, but Nix shoulders plenty of responsibility for the team's 2-2 start to the season. He'll try to bounce back in a Week 5 road game against a Chargers defense that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bo Nix didn't show any improvement in Week 5 as the Broncos switched back to Sean Payton as their play-caller, throwing for a season-low 123 yards and producing just one touchdown in a win over the Chargers. The third-year QB has a meager 6:3 TD:INT through five games and is completing fewer than 60.0% of his passes, averaging fewer than 200 passing yards per game. There's still reason to believe Nix's numbers will improve once Payton gets back in a rhythm, but the Denver offense's ceiling seems limited even if it's operating at peak efficiency. Nix isn't likely to break out in Week 6 against a Seahawks defense that ranks sixth this season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bo Nix continues to struggle, failing to throw a touchdown in Week 6 for the first time this season while compiling a season-low 107 passing yards. The third-year quarterback has produced fewer than 6.0 yards per attempt in four straight games, and the Broncos' switch back to Sean Payton as the play-caller hasn't yet sparked the offense. Nix has just seven total touchdowns (six passing and one rushing) against five turnovers through seven games, but he'll get a chance to build some momentum in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Nix enters his third NFL season after finishing exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points during each of his first two campaigns. Nix's passing efficiency has a ways to go (career 6.5 yards per attempt), but his dual-threat ability has kept him in the weekly QB1 mix. Nix has finished both seasons no lower than 11th in pass attempts, completions, passing TDs, carries, rushing yards and rushing TDs. Last season, he provided a solid floor (11 games with 15-plus fantasy points), but his ceiling was low (four top-10 weeks). In 2026, he'll have a new playcaller in Davis Webb and an upgraded group of pass catchers with Jaylen Waddle added to the mix. The 26-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake London looks poised to bounce back from a tough Week 1 in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Carolina's defense just allowed a whopping 59 points to the Bears in Week 1, giving up 42.2 PPR fantasy points to wide receivers. London's rebound could depend on the quarterback play, as Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) are both questionable for Sunday's contest. However, with Carolina's defensive struggles during Week 1, London should be in for a fantastic matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake London will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. London has caught just six of nine targets for 80 yards in Atlanta's first two games, as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand struggled to get the offense going. However, Michael Penix is set to return as the Falcons' QB1 during the Week 3 contest, giving London a far more optimistic projection. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with Green Bay's defense allowing three receiving touchdowns and 34.5 PPR fantasy points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake London will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. With Michael Penix returning from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London had one of the best performances of his career, catching nine of 10 targets for 194 yards. With Penix on the field, London has averaged 6.7 receptions, 98.7 receiving yards and 0.6 touchdowns per game, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as long as Penix remains healthy. Despite this, London is in for a tough Week 4 matchup against a Saints secondary that's given up 29.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. London has excelled since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, catching 14 of 16 targets for 290 yards across his last two contests. With Penix at the helm, London has averaged a whopping 6.6 receptions and 98.5 yards per game, suggesting that he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as the season progresses. Additionally, London is in for a terrific matchup against a Ravens secondary that's allowed 37.9 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake London will likely remain the Falcons' top pass catcher in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. London impressed in the Week 5 loss despite not finding the end zone, totaling 118 yards on seven receptions. He's been one of fantasy's top wideouts since Michael Penix (ribs) returned in Week 3, averaging seven receptions and 136 yards per game across three contests. As long as Penix is healthy for the Week 6 contest, London should have another fantastic opportunity to put up big numbers against a Bears defense that's given up 32.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Despite logging double-digit targets for the third time in his last four games, London recorded just four receptions and 62 yards in the Week 6 loss to the Bears. Since Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged 9.3 targets, 6.3 receptions and 117.5 yards per game, making him one of fantasy's most productive receivers. Even so, London could struggle against a tough 49ers defense in Week 7 that's given up just 28.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through five games this season.

player.seasonOutlook: London enters his fifth NFL season with eyes on finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game for the third season in a row. The 2022 first-round pick broke out with a 100-1,271-9 receiving line and a fifth-place finish in fantasy points (14th PPG) in 2024. Last season, he missed five games and fell to 19th in fantasy points, but he was actually better on a per-game basis (seventh) and was the top scorer among receivers three times between Weeks 6 and 10. London remains heavily targeted (career 28% share) and sees plenty of work near the goal line (25 end zone targets over the past two seasons). As long as one of Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. can play somewhat competent ball, the 25-year-old London shouldn't have trouble providing fringe-WR1 fantasy production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Allen will look for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. Allen failed to throw a touchdown pass in Week 3 for the first time this season, while also tossing his first two interceptions. He rushed for two scores for the third straight week and has at least six carries in three straight games, but he's completed 20 passes or fewer in every outing. He'll oppose a familiar opponent in a Patriots defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite yielding three touchdown passes by Trevor Lawrence in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Allen brings a multi-touchdown streak into the Bills' Week 5 matchup at the Rams. Allen has provided multiple scores in each of Buffalo's first four games, throwing six scores while rushing for seven, though his yardage has topped 253 just once. The Rams, however, have allowed only one rushing touchdown and a mere 4.84 yards per pass attempt in what looks to be a battle of elite versus elite.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Allen looks to continue to provide elite returns when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Allen is coming off his best rushing effort of the year in Week 5, finishing with 121 yards while scoring on the ground for the eighth time in five games, adding further upside to his reliable passing efforts. Facing a Raiders defense in Week 6 that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks likely won't hinder Allen's appeal, as he's set for top-tier dual-threat production Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to get going when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Adams was held to a 3-26-0 receiving line versus San Francisco in Week 1, though the Rams' offense as a whole was held in check. Adams did draw the second-most targets (six) among Los Angeles pass catchers, as he continued to draw QB Matthew Stafford's attention more than any other player besides star Puka Nacua (nine targets). The Giants largely held Dallas' passing game in check during a Week 1 win, with no Cowboys pass catcher logging more than five receptions or 44 yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Davante Adams is coming off an explosive Monday Night Football performance heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. With Puka Nacua sidelined by a hip injury, Adams starred Monday against the Giants, posting a massive 10-195-2 line. Nacua's status for Week 3 is up in the air, and Adams would logically stand to be Matthew Stafford's top target again if Nacua can't suit up. However, Denver is a tough matchup, as the Broncos have yielded just 6.55 yards per target to wideouts this season (fifth-best in the NFL).
outlooksByWeek.4: Davante Adams has looked resurgent of late ahead of the Rams' Week 4 tilt against the Eagles. With Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined the past two weeks, Adams has gone off for 15 catches, 332 yards and two touchdowns. However, Nacua has a chance to return to action against Philadelphia, which would potentially result in Adams seeing less attention from QB Matthew Stafford. With that said, both wideouts could feast against an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league by giving up an average of 157.7 receiving yards per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Davante Adams is coming off a quiet performance as the Rams prepare to host the Bills in Week 5. Against Philadelphia in Week 4, Adams was held to four catches for 32 yards. That was a substantial downturn after Adams averaged 7.5 catches and 166 yards over the previous two contests, though he still got a healthy nine targets against the Eagles. It has to be mentioned that star wideout Puka Nacua returned to action in Week 4 and posted a 9-125-0 line, while Adams' big performances the previous two weeks took place in games Nacua missed due to injury. Both WRs could find success against the Bills, who have allowed the fourth-most receiving yards to wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Davante Adams is coming off his second two-TD game of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 6 battle versus Arizona. Against Buffalo on Monday Night Football in Week 5, Adams recorded a 5-51-2 line on seven targets. While he lagged far behind Puka Nacua's 24 targets and massive 17-138-1 line, Adams continued to work as a top option for QB Matthew Stafford in the red zone. That could come in handy again versus the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-high 10 receiving touchdowns to wide receivers so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Davante Adams was placed on Injured Reserve due to a ruptured left hamstring in the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals and is expected to be sidelined until after the Rams' Week 11 bye in a best-case scenario. With Adams out, names such as Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell should be in line for more targets, while established threats in the passing game like Puka Nacua, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams will also be in line for an uptick in numbers. Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdonwns this season, and he will be sidelined for the time being, so he'll miss out on the chance of being productive in a favorable Week 7 matchup against a below-average Raiders defense.

player.seasonOutlook: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle had a quiet season opener but will look to increase his production when San Francisco faces the Dolphins in Week 2. Kittle tallied a modest two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards in last Thursday's win over the Rams. That was his first game back after tearing his Achilles in January, which may have been a factor in his receiving line following below his usual standards. Miami allowed Raiders tight end Michael Mayer to record six catches in Week 1, suggesting that Kittle could find room to operate against the Dolphins defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Kittle will look to build upon Sunday's strong performance when San Francisco hosts the Cardinals in Week 3. In just his second regular-season game since tearing his Achilles in January, Kittle led the 49ers with 80 receiving yards on four catches with one touchdown Sunday in a win over Miami. The veteran tight end remains a key target for QB Brock Purdy, and Kittle's importance in the passing game could be even more elevated with WRs Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both managing injuries. Through two weeks, Arizona has allowed tight ends to catch all 10 of their targets for 105 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver as one of the hottest tight ends in the league. Following a quiet season opener in Australia, Kittle has put up 10 catches for 162 yards and three touchdowns over the subsequent two weeks. He's caught all but one of his 11 targets during that span, as he has been clicking very well with QB Brock Purdy. Kittle could continue rolling against a Broncos defense that has given up the eighth-most receiving yards (199) to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Kittle could again be a key component of San Francisco's offense in Week 5 against Seattle. Kittle has scored a touchdown in three straight games, and he got into the end zone on a game-sealing 56-yard reception in Week 4 versus the Broncos. The veteran tight end enters the clash against Seattle with 244 receiving yards on the season, third-most among NFL tight ends. With that said, the Seahawks' defense has given up the fourth-fewest receiving yards to tight ends, so Kittle has his work cut out for him in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Kittle should be past an illness by the time the 49ers face Washington on Monday Night Football in Week 6. Kittle suited up this past Sunday against Seattle despite falling under the weather near game day. He ended up with a modest five catches on six targets for 24 yards but logged his usual big workload with a season-high 93 percent offensive snap share. Kittle could be primed for a big game against the Commanders, who have surrendered 15.8 fantasy points per game -- second-most in the league -- to tight ends.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Kittle and the 49ers are in Atlanta as they look to stay undefeated in Week 7. He caught five of eight targets for 69 yards and a touchdown during San Francisco's 23-17 win in Week 6. Kittle finished second on the team in receptions, yardage and targets on a night where Brock Purdy attempted just 29 passes. The talented tight end boasts a 26-337-5 line on 36 targets through six outings, and he'll aim to keep rolling versus a Falcons defense tied for 23rd in fantasy points allowed per game (16.0) to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle may be ready for Week 1 and isn't expected to miss more than a game or two, though he's now 32 years old and might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so his upside makes him worth a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jakobi Meyers maintains a high floor, though he's a low-ceiling fantasy WR3 or flex play for Jacksonville's Week 2 home game against Denver's elite defense. Meyers has posted at least 39 receiving yards in all 10 of his games with the Jaguars since coming over in a midseason trade last year, including 40 receiving yards and a TD in the Week 1 win over Cleveland. Parker Washington and Brian Thomas have more downfield playmaking capability, but Meyers should see his share of short targets with Trevor Lawrence likely looking to get the ball out quickly to counter a Broncos pass rush that led the league with 68 sacks last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jakobi Meyers has been targeted just three times through Jacksonville's first two games. That lack of volume makes him hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league dart throw in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that held the Seahawks and Steelers to a combined 16 points. Parker Washington (18 targets), Brian Thomas (11 targets), and even TE Brenton Strange (five targets) have all been higher on Trevor Lawrence's priority list than Meyers. To the veteran wide receiver's credit, Meyers's 28-yard effort on one target in the Week 2 loss to Denver marked the first time in 11 games as a member of the Jaguars that he failed to record at least 39 receiving yards. Therefore, he could rebuild a solid fantasy floor if Lawrence starts looking Meyers's way more frequently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jakobi Meyers led the Jaguars with seven catches for 64 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in Week 3 against the Patriots after catching all three of his targets for 68 yards and a TD across Jacksonville's first two games. The veteran wideout has been playing alongside Parker Washington in two-WR sets and working ahead of Brian Thomas, as Meyers' 79% snap share this season is nearly double Thomas' mark. Washington is the clear No. 1 receiving option for the Jaguars, but Meyers is shaping up as the team's next-most reliable pass catcher, which is enough to be deployed as a WR3 or flex option in Week 4 against the Bengals, who didn't allow a touchdown pass through Week 2 before giving up TDs to three separate Steelers wideouts in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jakobi Meyers has been efficient with his opportunities for the Jaguars, catching 13 of 15 targets for 165 yards and two touchdowns heading into a Week 5 trip to London to face the Eagles. His usage has fluctuated in a Jacksonville passing game with many mouths to feed, but Meyers is a viable flex option for Week 5, especially in deeper leagues. The Eagles are giving up 164 yards and one receiving touchdown per game to WRs, and they could be without top CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) in Week 5, which would make things easier for some combination of Meyers, Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Josh Cameron.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jakobi Meyers is averaging 40 yards per game and has scored twice through five outings heading into Jacksonville's Week 6 matchup with the Texans in London. Houston has struggled to cover wide receivers, having allowed 193 yards per game and six TDs to the position through five games. Meyers is a distant second on the WR depth chart behind Parker Washington, but the plus matchup makes Meyers a viable flex option.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the league's most underrated players, Meyers is entering his first full season with Jacksonville after being acquired via trade in November. The 2019 UDFA has produced 800-plus receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while operating primarily as a short-to-intermediate target. More of a solid producer than a high-ceiling contributor, Meyers has finished no lower than 32nd in fantasy points over the last five seasons, but has yet to do better than 19th. The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
outlooksByWeek.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.
outlooksByWeek.5: Romeo Doubs has an ascending role in the Patriots' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. He collected a season-high nine targets in Week 4, and while it resulted in just six catches and 58 yards, he found the end zone twice. Las Vegas will rush the passer, which has troubled Drake Maye. The secondary is allowing 8.2 yards per target to wideouts, so Doubs can capitalize on whatever volume he receives.
outlooksByWeek.6: Romeo Doubs' opportunities have been limited through five games, with the Patriots hosting the Jets in Week 6. After recording nine targets in Week 4, Doubs hauled in just one of three looks in Week 5, giving him three or four targets in four of the first five games with his new team. Though the Jets have been statistically stout against the pass, allowing just 195.4 yards per game, they've allowed five opposing wide receivers to post at least 58 yards in as many games. With Drake Maye spreading targets around, Doubs' ceiling is low, making him a fringe flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Romeo Doubs was placed on the injured list after injuring his shoulder while making a diving touchdown catch in Week 6. The Patriots expect him to return following their Week 11 bye. While Doubs is out, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams should log more targets.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre Tucker was fairly quiet in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, catching two of four targets for 27 yards. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, project to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Tucker isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre Tucker produced his first ceiling game of 2026 in the Raiders' Week 2 win over the Chargers. churning out a 5-119-1 line on seven targets. The volatile wideout is showing some early chemistry with new quarterback Kirk Cousins, and no one else has yet shown any indication that they'll be able to challenge him for the top spot on the depth chart, even if Tucker's skill set would be better suited for a WR2 or even WR3 role. Tucker will try to build on last week's effort in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre Tucker remains in the top spot on the Raiders' wide receiver depth chart, but he's a boom-or-bust option. After popping for a big game in Week 2, Tucker fell back to a 4-43-0 line on just four targets in a Week 3 win over the Saints. With Las Vegas off to a 3-0 start, changes in the offensive mix aren't likely, but Tucker simply doesn't have the physical tools to consistently get open and win 1-on-1 matchups in the NFL. Another rare ceiling game is unlikely in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tre Tucker handled a season-high eight targets in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, but he turned them into just four catches for 44 yards. The fourth-year wideout has reached 50 receiving yards only once in four games to begin the season, producing a 15-233-1 line on 23 targets. With a healthy Brock Bowers back as Kirk Cousins' No. 1 option, Tucker's chances of another ceiling game have shrunk. He'll face a Patriots secondary in Week 5 that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tre Tucker has hauled in at least four passes in four straight games as the Raiders' top wide receiver, although he plays a clear second fiddle to tight end Brock Bowers in the passing game. Tucker has failed to reach 50 receiving yards in three of those games, and his only touchdown came during his Week 2 eruption against the Chargers. The fourth-year wideout will have a ceiling game once in a blue moon, but his weekly floor is low, at least while Kirk Cousins remains under center instead of rookie Fernando Mendoza. Tucker will try to get enough volume to take advantage of a Week 6 matchup against a Bills secondary that ranks last in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tre Tucker continues to build chemistry with Kirk Cousins. The Raiders' No. 1 wide receiver hauled in two touchdowns in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, and through six games Tucker has produced a 24-371-3 line on 35 targets, putting him on pace for his first 1,000-yard effort. Tight end Brock Bowers remains the top option in the passing game, and Tucker has yet to record more than eight targets in a game in 2026. The prospect of Fernando Mendoza replacing Cousins under center at some point offers additional uncertainty for Tucker. He'll have a hard time delivering another ceiling game in Week 7 against a Rams secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: A team's No. 1 wide receiver is often a household name, but that's certainly not the case for the underrated Tucker, Las Vegas' top wideout for most of the 2025 season. Tucker has finished in the top 10 among wide receivers in both snaps and routes each of the last two seasons and ranked just outside of the top 30 in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns in 2025. Tucker, who also contributes as rusher, has yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign while working in the Raiders' struggling offenses and would need a terrific rookie season from Fernando Mendoza to get there in 2026. That's a long shot for the undersized receiver, so he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.3: Ollie Gordon's workload could increase if Jaylen Wright misses the Dolphins' Week 3 game against the Chiefs. Despite being No. 3 on the depth chart, Gordon has outsnapped Wright behind Miami's workhorse, De'Von Achane. Kansas City allowed stud Jonathan Taylor to rush for two scores in Week 2 but kept Denver's backs under control in Week 1. Barring an injury to Achane, it's difficult to envision a path to meaningful production for Gordon.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out in Week 3. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins often falling behind in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the preferred pass-catching option. Confidence isn't inspired facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 yards per carry and 11 catches to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ollie Gordon could be emerging in the Dolphins' backfield heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. With De'Von Achane (knee) out, Gordon ran for 100 yards on just nine carries in Week 4, vastly outperforming Jaylen Wright, while also scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. Touches figure to remain low if the Dolphins are forced to play from behind early, but facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry could lead to steady yardage without high volume, and Gordon will remain an option near the goal line.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ollie Gordon will likely continue to serve as the lead back for the Dolphins in Week 7 against the Jets. Prior to Miami's Week 6 bye, Gordon had 17 or 18 carries in two of three games. The lone outing with a decrease in carries was also his only 100-yard game, and he scored in each contest. Though he hasn't factored into the passing game, volume remains king for running backs, and Gordon appears to have that in a matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, resulting in the 11th-most fantasy points allowed.

player.seasonOutlook: Gordon is battling Jaylen Wright for backup work behind lead back De'Von Achane in Miami. Gordon was used sparingly as a rookie and didn't exactly move the needle. The 2025 sixth-round pick averaged an ugly 2.84 yards per carry on 70 attempts and 3.6 yards per target on the nine balls thrown his way. Gordon is still very young (22 years old), and his size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) adds to his long-term intrigue. He'll have some insurance appeal if he beats out Wright for primary backup duties.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to take on the Buccaneers and their 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (26.8) to RBs in Week 2. The second-year back rushed 12 times for 33 yards and caught both targets for 17 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 Week 1 loss. Running lanes and beneficial game flow are two things to be concerned with for Judkins, as the Browns again appear to be one of the worst offenses in the league. If the QB play improves even slightly, he could see an uptick in opportunities in both the running and passing games, but he should be started with caution until that situation improves.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for an interconference showdown in Week 3. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with 12 carries for 21 yards and caught all five targets for 27 yards. No other running back tallied more than two carries, so it's clear Judkins is still the No. 1 option out of the backfield, but that hasn't come with much success through two weeks of action. Next up is a Carolina defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points allowed (36.3) and last in TDs surrendered to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Steelers to town for an AFC North clash on Thursday night in Week 4. He rushed 18 times for 70 yards and caught both targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset win over the Panthers in Week 3. Judkins surpassed 35 yards on the ground for the first time this season, and there's a chance he could build upon that against their division rivals. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (22.1) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Jets in Week 5, looking for their fourth consecutive win. He had his best performance of 2026 in Week 4, rushing 17 times for 53 yards and his first TD of the season while catching six of seven targets for 43 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory. No other back recorded more than two carries, and Judkins led the team in receptions and tied for third in targets. Up next is a Jets defense that allows 28.3 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 30th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the division rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He tallied 14 carries for 44 yards and caught three of four targets for six yards during Cleveland's Week 5 loss. Judkins played just 52.9% of snaps, likely due to a right ankle injury suffered in-game, and he was reportedly spotted wearing a walking boot afterward. Head coach Todd Monken called it a "tweak" on Monday and considers his starting running back day-to-day. Judkins' practice participation this week will be worth monitoring, as he'll be facing a Baltimore defense that allows 18.8 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.
outlooksByWeek.7: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Titans for an interconference clash in Week 7. He was inactive for Cleveland's 13-10 victory in Week 6 due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 5. Jaleel McLaughlin (9), Audric Estime (9), and Michael Burton (1) handled the backfield responsibilities, with Estime notching his first TD as a Brown. Judkins is averaging 3.0 yards per carry on 73 attempts, and if he's active for Week 7, he'll face a Tennessee defense allowing 20.3 fantasy points per game (13th) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Judkins is entering his second NFL season after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which a solid 14-game stretch of action was bookended by missed time early because of an off-field issue and late because of a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. When on the field, Judkins handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts (16.4 per game). Though he was held to 3.6 yards per carry, he was dealing with a league-high 7.4 box defenders per attempt. He wasn't involved much as a receiver (2.6 targets per game), however, and was limited to 12.1 fantasy points per game (26th among RBs). The Cleveland offense has a new coach (Todd Monken) and quarterback questions remain, so while Judkins has a clear path to a big carry total, the 22-year-old might cap out as a midrange RB2 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendre Miller could operate as the Saints' No. 2 running back if Alvin Kamara (knee) remains sidelined for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Miller was surprisingly involved in New Orleans' Week 1 gameplan, tying Travis Etienne for the most carries on the team while finding the end zone. Despite averaging only 3.3 yards per carry, Miller could have a similar role if Kamara remains out for Week 2. It's also a favorable matchup for running backs, as the Ravens defense allowed 5.2 yards per carry and two rushing touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kendre Miller is expected to split carries with Alvin Kamara in the Saints' Week 4 matchup  against the Falcons, with Travis Etienne (hamstring) out. Miller tallied 19 yards on six touches during the Week 3 loss, playing behind both Alvin Kamara and Etienne. As Etienne deals with an ongoing hamstring injury, Miller is likely to split work on the ground with Kamara in the Week 4 contest, operating as one of the Saints' leading rushers. Despite this, Miller is in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed just 3.1 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kendre Miller is likely to remain one of the Saints' top rushers while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is out during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Miller received the second-most carries (six) on New Orleans in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons but was largely ineffective, averaging just 1.5 yards per carry. Even if Miller continues splitting work with Alvin Kamara, he likely won't have much fantasy value, as the Saints' offense is averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game. Additionally, Miller is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 307 rushing yards all season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kendre Miller is expected to remain a large part of the Saints' rushing attack in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Miller operated as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, receiving more carries (six) and targets (three) while playing more snaps (13) than Alvin Kamara (three carries and two targets on 12 snaps). While Travis Etienne (hamstring) remains sidelined, Miller appears to have assumed the role as the Saints' top rusher. He could thrive in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's given up 21.3 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kendre Miller appears to have emerged as the Saints' top running back ahead of the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. While Travis Etienne (hamstring) remains sidelined, Miller has taken over as New Orleans' primary rusher, logging 22 touches and 70 total yards in the Week 6 win over the Giants. Additionally, Miller played a season-high 46% of the Saints' offensive snaps, which is partially due to Alvin Kamara's injury in the first half, but still remains a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Miller could struggle in Week 7, however, as Pittsburgh's defense has allowed just 4.0 yards per carry this year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylin Noel finished second on the Texans with 53 receiving yards in the season opener despite being targeted just twice. Noel will need to earn a larger role to gain fantasy relevance, but he has a chance to do so given Houston's lack of a clear No. 2 WR behind Nico Collins. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte combined for eight targets in Week 1 but recorded only 53 receiving yards between the two of them, matching Noel's yardage total. Noel can't be trusted as a starter heading into a Week 2 home game against the Bengals, but the 2025 third-round draft pick could be worth stashing, especially in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylin Noel could see extra opportunities in Week 3 if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a second consecutive game against the Colts. Noel has just three catches this season, but two of them have exceeded 30 yards. The 2025 third-round pick's big-play ability makes him a viable deep-league option in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL through two games. Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jared Wayne are the other healthy options in Houston's WR room.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylin Noel is a deep-league dart throw for Week 4 against the Cowboys, especially if top Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) is sidelined for a third consecutive game. Noel is tied for fifth on the team with nine targets through three games, but he leads all of Houston's WRs with 11.2 yards per target. Given the Texans' lack of production from the position in Collins' absence, it would be sensible to give Noel more opportunities. Whether they materialize is another matter, and Noel's limited usage so far this season suggests he'll be tough to trust in Week 4, even against a Cowboys defense that's giving up 387 scrimmage yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylin Noel turned three targets into 85 yards for the Texans in their Week 4 loss to Dallas, and the 2025 third-round pick continues to make the most of his opportunities. Heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans, Noel has caught eight of 12 targets for 186 yards while leading the league with 23.3 yards per reception. Noel's big-play potential makes him worth a flier in deeper formats against a Titans secondary that has been prone to breakdowns, but he hasn't garnered consistent enough volume from C.J. Stroud to be started comfortably in any matchup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylin Noel continues to make the most of his opportunities for the Texans. The 2025 third-round pick has caught every pass thrown his way in four of five games this season, leads the team with 17.5 yards per catch and just scored his first TD of the campaign while tying his season high with five targets in the Week 5 win over Tennessee.
