Noel's arrow is pointing up ahead of a Week 6 matchup against a Jacksonville defense that's allowing a league-high 204 receiving yards per game to WRs, though his floor remains low due to modest volume, as he has earned just 17 targets through five games. He's a boom-or-bust Week 6 flex option for managers in deeper leagues or in search of a bye-week plug-in.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylin Noel has made the most of his opportunities all season, and Houston's 2025 third-round pick has started to earn a larger role in recent weeks. He takes a two-game touchdown streak into Week 7 against the Giants. Noel has caught all 12 of his targets for 233 yards over the past three games after posting five catches for 101 yards on nine targets through Week 3. Nico Collins remains the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game, and the role of trade acquisition Marvin Harrison should grow moving forward, but Noel's recent success makes him a viable Week 7 flex play against a Giants secondary that has allowed seven receiving TDs to WRs in six games.

player.seasonOutlook: Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the Patriots for a Week 2 road clash. He completed 24 of 40 pass attempts for 221 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for minus-3 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory over the Falcons. The Steelers attempted 41 passes compared to just 21 rushing attempts, as Rodgers connected with seven different receivers on the day. They'll face a tougher test on the road against New England's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.3) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the division-rival Bengals in Week 3. He threw for 187 yards (23-for-39) with no touchdowns and one INT and lost one of his two fumbles during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots. Cincinnati has been somewhat stingy against opposing QBs, allowing 20.2 fantasy points through two outings (15th) despite giving up 353 passing yards versus Houston in Week 2. The Bengals are the only defense without an interception to this point, but they're also the only team that has yet to surrender a passing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He's coming off easily his best outing of the young campaign, throwing for 292 yards (19-for-34) with three TDs and one INT while rushing three times for 10 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Rodgers spread the ball around to nine different receivers, finding Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek for his three scores. He'll face Cleveland's 16th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.9) per game to QBs as the Steelers look to improve to 3-1 in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the Colts for a Week 5 showdown. He threw for 299 yards (22-for-40) with three TDs and two INTs during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. That's two straight outings with three passing TDs and nearly 300 yards through the air, but the 42-year-old was sacked five times in addition to his two turnovers. Rodgers will look to clean up the mistakes against a Colts defense allowing 24.3 fantasy points per game to QBs (27th) and 261.3 passing yards (29th).
outlooksByWeek.6: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Tampa Bay for an interconference clash in Week 6. He threw for 235 yards (22-for-31) with three TDs and no INTs while rushing once for six yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. That's three straight weeks that the 42-year-old has tossed three scores, and he now has a 10:4 TD:INT through five games this season. Rodgers looks to stay hot versus a stingy Buccaneers defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points allowed to QBs (18.4 per game).
outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 matchup against the Saints. He threw for 253 yards (33-for-49) with two TDs and one INT while rushing once for minus-one yard during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime. Rodgers led four straight scoring drives to send the game to OT after the Steelers trailed 16-3 to start the fourth quarter. He now owns an 11:4 TD:INT over his last four outings, and he'll face a New Orleans defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed per game (21.4) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers and will return for his second season with the team. The 42-year-old is reuniting with his longtime head coach from Green Bay, Mike McCarthy. The duo will look to improve on a 2025 campaign in which Rodgers finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns while ranking 23rd among 28 qualified QBs in QBR. Even if Rodgers' efficiency improves, he remains a nonfactor as a rusher (he last cleared 107 yards in 2020) and hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2021 (25th, 18th and 25th in points per game in his past three full seasons). Even with a more pass-friendly playcaller and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added to the wide receiver room, Rodgers is no more than a low-ceiling QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: T.J. Hockenson will look to build off a solid Week 1 performance as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Hockenson was second in targets against the Packers behind Justin Jefferson, reeling in four of five targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. The veteran tight end was a go-to outlet for veteran Carson Wentz, and he could continue to be one no matter who lines up under center moving forward. He'll take on a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Carolina tight ends in a high-scoring season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: T.J. Hockenson will look to stay involved as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Hockenson saw his volume go down a bit in Week 2 against the Bears, reeling in just three catches for 29 yards. The starting tight end looks like he'll be a touchdown-dependent fantasy option. With that being said, Kyler Murray is slated to start Sunday, and he's been known to rely on his tight ends in the past. The Bucs have allowed 22.1 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season, 31st in the lerague.
outlooksByWeek.4: T.J. Hockenson remains a secondary option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 4 against the Dolphins. Other than a 4-36-1 receiving line in Week 1, Hockenson has looked otherwise like a disappointment this season. The veteran tight end has stayed consistent with four targets in back-to-back games, but he's converted them into a combined five catches for 40 yards in the stretch. Miami has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends (16), but even then, Hock will likely need to find the end zone to have relevance beyond a depth option.
outlooksByWeek.5: T.J. Hockenson will look to build on a huge performance as the Vikings play New Orleans in Week 5. Hockenson finished Week 4 with a bang after starting the season quietly, catching all 13 of his targets for a whopping 119 yards. The veteran tight end could continue to be an outlet for quarterback Kyler Murray, especially with some struggles from the quarterback so far. The Saints have ranked bottom five against fantasy TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: T.J. Hockenson holds a questionable tag heading into Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Hockenson sustained a concussion in the Vikings' Week 5 win over the Saints heading into the bye, so his status is up in the air just two weeks later. The veteran tight end will need to clear protocol if he hopes to get back on the field, and that'll be evident through his practice availability. Indianapolis has ranked in the middle against fantasy TEs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: It's been a rough go for Hockenson since he peaked with a 95-960-5 receiving line in 2023. He tore an ACL in Week 16 that season and was limited to a 41-455-0 receiving line upon his return in 10 games in 2024. A bounce-back was expected in 2025, but Hockenson handled a weak 16% target share (his lowest since he was a rookie in 2019) and couldn't overcome the team's QB woes en route to a 51-438-3 showing. Hockenson has now followed four straight top-seven fantasy PPG seasons with finishes of 17th and 26th. The 29-year-old could very well get back on track in 2026, but he'll need solid play from Kyler Murray. Hockenson is a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.3: Konata Mumpfield's role in the Rams' Week 3 matchup against Denver could depend on the status of Puka Nacua (hip). With Nacua sidelined Monday versus Denver, Mumpfield drew the start, but he finished with just one catch on two targets for 12 yards. Meanwhile, Davante Adams posted a massive 10-195-2 line, with no other Los Angeles wideout reeling in more than one catch. The Broncos won't be an easy matchup in Week 3, as they've held opposing WRs to an average of just 13.2 fantasy points per game this season, fourth-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Konata Mumpfield is coming off the biggest performance of his young career ahead of the Rams' Week 4 matchup in Philadelphia. Mumpfield established new professional high marks with four catches for 93 yards against Denver in Week 3, with one of his receptions going for a 48-yard touchdown. The second-year wideout logged a healthy eight targets in the loss, but important context is that Puka Nacua sat out due to a hip injury. Should Nacua be able to return in Week 4, it's reasonable to expect Mumpfield to see considerably less opportunities. Still, the Eagles have been vulnerable against wideouts and just allowed Chicago's WR duo of Luther Burden and Kalif Raymond to combine for 13 catches, 151 yards and two TDs on Monday Night Football.
outlooksByWeek.5: Konata Mumpfield is dealing with a shoulder injury heading into the Rams' Week 5 battle versus Buffalo. Mumpfield suffered a bruised rotator cuff in in Week 4 against Philadelphia, though he was able to return to action after getting hurt. That bodes well for his chances of playing in Week 5, though even if he does suit up he's unlikely to be a big part of the offense with both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams healthy. His path to production may be touchdown-dependent, and the Bills have given up six receiving TDs to wideouts -- tied for second-most in the NFL -- through four weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Konata Mumpfield enters Week 7 with an opportunity to expand his role in the Rams' passing attack after Davante Adams suffered a significant hamstring injury that will sideline him for multiple weeks. Mumpfield has caught eight passes for 127 yards and a touchdown through six games, averaging an impressive 15.9 yards per reception despite limited opportunities. His ability to generate explosive plays could make him a useful complement to Puka Nacua, but his fantasy upside will be boom-or-bust, as he's likely to operate as a touchdown-dependent option with other names ahead of him in the pecking order. At least the Week 7 matchup against the Raiders is favorable, as Las Vegas has allowed the 10th-most receiving yards and fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Derrick Henry and the Ravens play host to the Saints for their 2026 home opener in Week 2. Henry rambled for 144 yards and three TDs on 24 carries and caught his only target for 19 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 victory. Next up is a Saints defense that surrendered 165 yards and two TDs on the ground to Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions. Henry has tallied 16 rushing TDs in consecutive years, and he's nearly a quarter of the way there already after just one game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Texas to battle the Cowboys in Week 3. In Baltimore's Week 2 loss, Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and one score, and he caught all three targets for another 19 yards. He accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, and he'll continue earning a massive workload on the ground in order to take pressure off Lamar Jackson. Henry faces a Dallas defense that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) and 27th in rushing yards allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Derrick Henry and the Ravens return from Brazil to host the winless Titans in Week 4. He tallied 26 carries for 89 yards and two TDs and caught his only target for no gain during Baltimore's 34-31 last-second victory in Week 3 over Dallas. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs after giving up 138 rushing yards to the Giants. Henry will handle his usual workhorse role and could benefit from a positive game script versus a Titans team that ranks third in fewest points allowed per contest, at 12.3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Derrick Henry and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 5 clash against the Falcons. He tallied 23 carries for 73 yards and one touchdown while catching both of his targets for six yards during Baltimore's Week 4 victory. Henry notched his seventh rushing TD of the season and now has at least one score in all four outings. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status up in the air, Henry should continue to be the focal point of the Ravens' offense versus Atlanta's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.9) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Cleveland for a divisional clash in Week 6. He rushed 24 times for 102 yards and caught one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5. The game marked Henry's first scoreless outing on the ground in 2026, and he draws a difficult Week 6 matchup against a Browns' defense that has surrendered just one combined TD to the position. Cleveland ranks seventh by allowing 17.6 fantasy points per game to RBs, but the Jets' Braelon Allen racked up 116 rushing yards and one score on 24 attempts in Week 5. The Browns could again be without two starters on the defensive line, and with Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question, Henry has another opportunity to be the primary engine of the offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Derrick Henry and the Ravens welcome the Bengals to town for a divisional clash in Week 7. He rushed 17 times for 58 yards and caught his lone target for two yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6, also losing a costly fumble in the fourth quarter. The outing marked Henry's first this season without a touchdown, and his 60 scrimmage yards were his lowest output through six games. He will aim to bounce back at home in Week 7 versus a Cincinnati defense that allows 19.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry continues to defy the odds, playing at a high level despite now entering his age-32 season. In 2025, he finished exactly second in the NFL in rushing yards for the fourth season in a row, and his 24 carries inside the 5-yard line were easily the most in the league. Henry leads the NFL in carries inside the 5-yard line (42) and is second in touchdowns (34) since joining Baltimore prior to the 2024 season, and he hasn't finished lower than eighth among RBs in touchdowns since 2017. Henry continues to run at a high level (his 5.20 yards per carry last season ranked fifth among qualified backs), but he's still a nonfactor as a receiver (outside the top 45 backs in targets, catches and yards last season). He remains a featured rusher in a terrific offense and is well positioned for his fifth consecutive top-eight fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Walker earned his big salary in his Kansas City debut, rumbling for a career-high 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries while catching three of six targets for 18 yards and another score in a season-opening win over the Broncos. It was the kind of volume Walker rarely garnered in Seattle, but the fifth-year RB is being counted on to handle bell-cow duties with his new team, as rookie Emmett Johnson figures to be his primary backup for most or all of the season. Walker will aim to keep rolling in Week 2 against a Colts defense that just got steamrolled by Derrick Henry, but which ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Walker has had a dazzling start to his Kansas City tenure, topping 100 rushing yards in each of his first two games and piling up 369 scrimmage yards in total with two touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. The former Seahawk is thriving in a bell cow role, and his 6.2 yards per carry would be a career high if he can keep it up. Walker will take aim in Week 3 at a Dolphins defense that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Walker didn't need a ceiling game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. While he failed to reach 100 rushing yards for the first time this season, he did score his second rushing and second receiving touchdown of the year. Walker's addition has supercharged the entire offense, and he's thriving in a bell-cow role, amassing 360 rushing yards in three games while averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He's also on pace for a career-best campaign as a pass catcher. Walker could face a test in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenneth Walker was dominant for Kansas City in the team's first four games prior to a Week 5 bye, rumbling for 537 rushing yards on 6.2 yards per carry while scoring six times-four on the ground and two through the air. Last season's Super Bowl MVP with the Seahawks is earning every penny of his big free-agent contract, and his presence in the backfield is also opening things up for Patrick Mahomes, putting KC in the top five in the NFL in points per game at 29.5 and second in yards per game at 412.0, behind only the Rams. Walker should be able to continue rolling in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenneth Walker continues to shine as the new focal point of Kansas City's offense. Through his first five games with the team, Walker has piled up eight total touchdowns-six rushing and two receiving-while topping 100 rushing yards in four of those contests. He leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, despite already having had his bye and having played one fewer game than Bijan Robinson and James Cook, the only other two backs with more than 600 yards. Walker will try to deliver a revenge game in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Walker signed with the Chiefs after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seahawks. The reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded running back from 2025, Walker is poised for feature-back duties in a good, Andy Reid-led offense. Having worked in a committee most of last season, Walker was limited to only five touchdowns and 11.3 fantasy points per game (both career lows), but he still generated 252 touches and a career-high 1,309 yards. He has yet to finish a season better than 18th in fantasy points (12th on a per-game basis) and has missed at least two games in three of four seasons in the league, but the 25-year-old's ability to contribute at a high level as a rusher and receiver is enough to position him as, at least, a fringe RB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.
outlooksByWeek.4: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Bears in the Jets' Week 4 matchup due to a thigh injury. Hall has struggled over the last two weeks, gaining just 61 yards on 29 carries, but his workload in the passing game has been steady. Should he play, Hall has an inviting matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry. Braelon Allen would likely lead the backfield in the event of Hall's absence, with Isaiah Davis playing second fiddle.
outlooksByWeek.5: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Browns in the Jets' Week 5 matchup due to a quad injury. He missed Week 4 with the issue, and when healthy, he was limited to 32 or fewer yards in his last two outings. Should he suit up, it's possible he'd be eased into his return and share snaps with Braelon Allen, but it's a favorable spot if a normal workload can be anticipated. While Cleveland has yet to allow a running back to score, they're allowing 4.8 yards per carry, with the last three lead backs all reaching at least 82 yards.
outlooksByWeek.6: Breece Hall needs to overcome a quad injury to suit up for the first time in three weeks when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Braelon Allen has shouldered the load in Hall's absence, and a split workload can be anticipated once Hall returns. Hall would require an unlikely heavy volume to be a top option facing a New England defense that's allowed just 399 rushing yards through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Breece Hall has missed three straight games due to a quad injury as the Jets get set to face the Dolphins in Week 7. Braelon Allen has shined during Hall's absence, and should Hall be deemed healthy, it would appear safe to assume he'd be eased back into action. Miami's defense ranks in the middle of the pack against opposing rushers, allowing 4.0 yards per carry and three rushing scores, but five touchdowns through the air to opposing backs. With questionable volume if he returns to action, it's probably wise to wait one more week before deploying Hall.

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Saints to town for a Week 2 matchup. Flowers left Baltimore's 41-23 Week 1 win in the second quarter and did not return. He is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury, per head coach Jesse Minter. Soft tissue injuries can be tricky, especially for someone as shifty as Flowers, but it sounds like the issue is not considered serious. He's fresh off posting a career-high 150 receiving yards on five catches (six targets) and a TD, so if the speedster is active against New Orleans, he should see plenty of looks from Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 matchup between 1-1 teams. He was ruled out of Baltimore's Week 2 loss with a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, so his status in practice this week will be something to monitor. If he's able to suit up in Week 3, Flowers will face a Cowboys defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) and 13th in receiving yards allowed to WRs. In his absence, Rashod Bateman put up a 7-88-1 receiving line on nine targets as Lamar Jackson's No. 1 receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Titans to town in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and handled a full workload, catching five of six targets for 84 yards while taking his lone carry for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 3 victory. Flowers led the team in receptions, targets, and yardage, and that should remain the same against Tennessee, which has the 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs. The hamstring issue appears to be behind him for now, but managers will want to keep an eye on his practice reps leading up to Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Zay Flowers looks to continue his hot start in 2026 when the Ravens visit the Falcons in Week 5. He grabbed eight of 10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. The fourth-year wideout owns an 18-352-2 receiving line on 22 targets across three contests. However, if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to suit up, Flowers will be catching passes from Tyler Huntley, who completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards in relief of Jackson. He'll have the added benefit of facing an Atlanta defense that allows 38.4 fantasy points per game (T-27th) to WRs and gave up eight receptions for 116 yards to Chris Olave.
outlooksByWeek.6: Zay Flowers and the Ravens travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He hauled in eight of nine targets for 53 yards during Baltimore's overtime victory in Week 5. Flowers paced the team in receptions and targets and was second in yardage, showing a strong rapport with Tyler Huntley, who started in place of the injured Lamar Jackson (ankle). No matter who's under center, Flowers remains the top receiving threat against Cleveland's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (36.4) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zay Flowers and the Ravens return home for a divisional showdown against the Bengals in Week 7. He caught six of 11 targets for 66 yards and had one carry for one yard during Baltimore's Week 6 loss. Flowers led Baltimore in receptions, yardage, and targets, with no other player earning more than five looks from Tyler Huntley. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question for a third consecutive week, Huntley is in line for his second start under center. Regardless of who is at QB, Flowers will continue operating as the clear-cut No. 1 option in the passing game versus Cincinnati's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (29.3) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Flowers' emergence into a star continued in 2025, as the 2023 first-round pick posted career-best marks in target share (29%), targets (118), catches (86) and yardage (1,211). Despite still lacking a role near the goal line (he has never cleared seven end zone targets or six touchdowns in a single season), Flowers finished seventh among receivers in fantasy points (13th PPG), which marks his first finish better than 25th (31st PPG). A highly targeted, short-range RAC specialist, Flowers' ceiling is lower than other top receivers, but the 25-year-old remains positioned as Lamar Jackson's top target in Baltimore's new-look offense. Flowers makes for a solid fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Marvin Harrison will look to get going in Arizona's Week 2 tilt against Seattle. Harrison notched just one catch on three targets in a season-opening win over the Chargers, though that reception did go for a robust 33 yards. With that said, the fact that he drew such a small amount of QB Jacoby Brissett's 37 targets provides some cause for concern, especially with newcomer Kendrick Bourne getting a healthy eight targets and No. 2 wideout Michael Wilson drawing seven. The Cardinals' wideout corps as a whole faces a tough challenge in the Seahawks, who didn't allow any Patriots pass catcher to exceed 51 yards in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Marvin Harrison will look to bounce back from his Week 2 goose egg when the Cardinals face San Francisco in Week 3. Harrison was targeted by QB Jacoby Brissett just once Sunday in a loss to the Seahawks and finished without a catch. The third-year receiver concerningly has just one catch for 33 yards through two weeks, and perhaps even more distressingly for his fantasy managers, he's drawn only four targets to Michael Wilson's 14 so far. The 49ers rank in the top 10 through two weeks by giving up only 247 receiving yards to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Marvin Harrison heads into the Cardinals' Week 4 matchup against the Giants having yet to get going this season. Harrison did record a campaign-best three catches and 40 yards this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, but he was far outshined by fellow wideout Michael Wilson, who posted an 11-89-1 line on a massive 17 targets. Star tight end Trey McBride also continued to shine with a 9-75-0 receiving line, so Harrison appears to be QB Jacoby Brissett's third option in the passing game at the moment. The Giants could present an opportunity for Harrison to get into the end zone, as they've given up four receiving TDs to wideouts so far this year, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Marvin Harrison heads into Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit struggling to build chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. Though Harrison recorded a 12-yard touchdown reception in Week 4 against the Giants, that was his only catch on four targets. The third-year wideout has exceeded one reception just once through four games this season and has totaled only 12 targets, remarkably far behind the 44 targets fellow wideout Michael Wilson has logged. With that said, the Lions could provide a prime opportunity for Harrison to get back on track, as Detroit has surrendered 207.3 receiving yards per game to wideouts, third-worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Marvin Harrison could make his Texans debut in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Harrison will likely be brought along slowly after being acquired in a trade from Arizona, so expectations should be tempered for Week 6, though the 2024 fourth overall pick is at least worth a flier in deeper leagues against a Jacksonville secondary that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers. Harrison had just 85 receiving yards in four games for the Cardinals this season, but a reunion with former Ohio State QB C.J. Stroud could be what Harrison needs to get his career back on track. While catching passes from Stroud in 2022, Harrison posted his best college season, with 77 catches for 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Marvin Harrison was on the field for only 12 snaps in his Texans debut against the Jaguars in Week 6 but came away with three catches for 34 yards from former college teammate C.J. Stroud. Harrison's role figures to grow as he gets acclimated to his new surroundings and learns the playbook. The trade acquisition from Arizona had only 85 receiving yards through four games with the Cardinals this season, but Harrison was considered an elite wide receiver prospect when he was drafted fourth overall in 2024. He's certainly worth a speculative add if available, but Harrison will remain a risky flex option in Week 7 against the Giants since his usage is likely to be limited again.

player.seasonOutlook: Harrison's pro career is off to a slow start after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick back in 2024. The Ohio State product was serviceable as a rookie (885 yards and eight TDs), but he missed five full games and was limited in others en route to a 41-608-4 receiving line in 2025. Harrison has finished 41st and 39th, respectively, in fantasy PPG despite a massive role near the goal line (he's third in the NFL in end zone targets since he was drafted and finished both seasons in the top five). Harrison is only entering his prime at age 24 and perhaps he'll make a Year 3 leap with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and with Kyler Murray no longer under center. Harrison performed better with Jacoby Brissett under center last season and has the raw talent to make him well worth post-hype consideration in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans had a strong 49ers debut last Thursday versus the Rams and will next face Miami in Week 2. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the season opener, with his score coming on a two-yard connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout tied with Deebo Samuel for the most targets among SF wideouts, so he looks to have already established a good rapport with Purdy. Evans could be in for another strong performance Sunday against a Titans defense that allowed three passing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Evans picked up a hip injury in San Francisco's win over Miami on Sunday, but early indications suggest he'll be fine for a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Evans has established a nice rapport with QB Brock Purdy so far this season, as the veteran wideout has caught nine of 10 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. San Francisco's WR corps has been thinned by the season-ending injury to rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson's more recent ankle injury, which will likely sideline him for Week 3, so Evans' availability as a reliable target for Purdy has taken on increased importance. Arizona was crushed by star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) in Week 2 and has given up four total receiving TDs to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Evans' status for San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver is cloudy due to injuries to his ribs and oblique. Evans was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's win over Arizona and wasn't able to return to the contest. He had gotten off to a strong start prior to the injury, catching three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown. If he's able to suit up against Denver, he'll face a tough challenge against star cornerback Patrick Surtain and a defense that has allowed the NFL's second-lowest catch rate (50.9%) to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Evans seems likely to continue playing through an injury to his ribs for San Francisco's Week 5 matchup against the Seahawks. The veteran wideout toughed out the injury in Week 4 and posted a 5-76-0 receiving line against a tough Broncos secondary. That receiving yardage was a season-high mark for Evans, as were his eight targets. Seattle could pose a significant challenge to the 49ers' receiving corps, however, as the Seahawks have yielded just 12.8 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season -- third-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mike Evans is coming off his best game as a member of the 49ers heading into a Week 6 tilt against Washington. Evans posted a 7-113-1 receiving line and added a two-point conversion in a tight win over the division-rival Seahawks this past Sunday. Fellow wideout Deebo Samuel injured his hamstring in the victory, and if he's unable to return for Week 6, Evans' importance in the passing game could be elevated even higher. The Commanders may be ripe for the picking, as they've given up the seventh-most fantasy points per game (25.0) to wideouts on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Evans and the 49ers are in Atlanta for a Week 7 road tilt. Unfortunately for him, he'll likely be spending it, and possibly more, on the sidelines after aggravating his Achilles injury in San Francisco's Week 6 win. Evans is expected to sit out the contest against the Falcons with a Week 8 bye on the horizon, giving him extra time and recovery for a chance to suit up in Week 9.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Monangai will look to be a big contributor once again for the Bears in Week 2 against the Vikings. While Monangai still took a back-seat role to D'Andre Swift in Week 1 against the Panthers, he still finished the game with 10 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown, along with 24 yards off two catches. The second-year ball carrier should still have plenty of a share in Chicago's rushing game to be fantasy relevant, especially given how much potential their offense showed for the season. Monangai will face a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but the Bears have a much superior RB room as of now.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Monangai should remain a high-volume RB2 as the Bears take on the Eagles in Week 3. Monangai saw double-digit carries once again in Week 2, but he totaled just 47 yards on the ground and tacked on 11 yards off two catches. The second-year running back has now seen 12 touches in each of Chicago's two outings this year, and he could see even more with Tyson Bagent slated to start under center. Philly has also ceded 216 rushing yards to RBs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Monangai should remain the complementary option in Chicago's backfield in Week 4 against the Jets. Monangai logged his third straight showing with 10 carries in Week 3 versus the Eagles, but he converted them for a season-low 31 rushing yards. The second-year running back also garnered no targets in the passing game, which came as a letdown after he posted a 4-35-0 receiving line leading up to the Monday Night win. He'll look to improve on his consistent volume against a New York defense that's allowed an eighth-most 24.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Monangai will look to shed a questionable tag after a huge performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Monangai dominated the Jets on the ground in Week 4 with 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns, but he also injured his thumb and is currently day-to-day. The second-year ball carrier's practice availability should dictate whether he's able to play in Chicago's rivalry debut of the 2026 season. If he's active, he'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyle Monangai will aim to return to the field as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Monangai sat out in Week 5 with a toe injury, but he's week-to-week and not a candidate for IR. The second-year ball carrier put together a career-best 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets in Week 4, so he could be inching towards a featured role if he can get back to the field. If he plays, Monangai will face an Atlanta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Monangai has missed back-to-back games with turf toe, and he'll need to get back to practice if he hopes to see the field in a TNF matchup. If he is active, he'll return to a favorable backfield role versus a Falcons defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

outlooksByWeek.6: Zach Charbonnet continues to rehab from a torn ACL and isn't expected to play in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Charbonnet did have his 21-day practice window opened last week, and he got in a couple limited practice sessions, but the fact that the Seahawks are playing on Thursday night this week complicates his outlook for a return to action. As such, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani are slated to lead Seattle's RB corps again. Charbonnet does have a chance to make his 2026 debut in Week 7 against Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zach Charbonnet (knee) and the Seahawks welcome the Chiefs to town for Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He's been on the physically unable to perform (PUP)/reserve list to begin 2026, but Seattle opened his three-week practice window back on Oct. 1. With that being said, Charbonnet will need to be activated by Thursday in order to avoid him being out for the rest of the season. He's expected to join the official roster after practicing in a limited fashion the last couple weeks. However, Charbonnet will likely be eased into the backfield rotation if he is indeed able to make his debut, so it would be wise to wait until after the meeting with Kansas City's defense that's tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Charbonnet would've been entering his fourth NFL season as the clear lead back in Seattle, but a torn ACL during the team's playoff game against the 49ers has put his 2026 campaign in jeopardy. It's a tough break for the 2020 second-round NFL draft pick, who set career-high marks in touches (204) while ranking fifth among backs in rushing touchdowns (12) and carries inside the 5-yard line (16) last season. Charbonnet's minimal receiving role (career-low 24 targets) limited him to 11.3 fantasy points per game, however, and he has yet to deliver a top-20 fantasy campaign. Kenneth Walker III is gone, but first-round rookie Jadarian Price could very well cement himself a big offensive role by the time Charbonnet is healthy. The 25-year-old is worth only a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Robinson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson could have material fantasy value this week, as Carolina's defense allowed 291 rushing yards and six touchdowns in Week 1. Additionally, Robinson received nine carries in the Week 1 loss to the Steelers, which is solid volume for a complementary role. He could find value with the Panthers giving up 52.8 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Robinson (ankle) will operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Robinson logged 13 touches in Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Panthers, but eight of those came in the fourth quarter -- suggesting he's still firmly the second option at RB. The Alabama product has been efficient, however, averaging 4.1 yards per carry through two weeks. He's also in for a favorable matchup, with the Packers defense allowing 22.9 PPR fantasy per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brian Robinson is expected to continue operating as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson had his best performance of the season in the Week 3 win over the Packers, rushing 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson has managed to be extremely efficient when given opportunities, averaging 4.6 yards per touch. He's also in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a New Orleans defense that's given up 4.8 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brian Robinson is expected to remain involved in Atlanta's offensive game plan in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Robinson had his best game of the season in the Week 4 win over the Saints, accumulating 67 yards on 15 touches while scoring three touchdowns. The Alabama product has now logged double-digit carries in three straight games, suggesting that he's established himself as a valuable portion of this Falcons offense. Expect Robinson to remain Atlanta's No. 2 running back behind Bijan Robinson in a tougher Week 5 matchup against a Baltimore defense that's given up just 3.8 yards per carry to RBs this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brian Robinson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Robinson was ineffective in the Week 5 overtime loss, accumulating just 16 yards on seven carries (2.3 yards per carry). Through five contests this season, Robinson has averaged 42 rushing yards per game, with most of his value coming from touchdowns (four on the season). He could struggle in Week 6 against a Bears defense that's given up just 409 rushing yards to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brian Robinson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson was held to just three touches during the Week 6 loss to the Bears, mostly because of the Falcons large deficit early in the game. On the season, Robinson has rushed 53 times for 211 yards and four touchdowns while catching five of six targets for an additional 30 yards. He could struggle finding the end zone in Week 7, however, as San Francisco's defense has given up just three total touchdowns to RBs through five games.

player.seasonOutlook: After a one-year stint as Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco, Robinson signed with Atlanta where he'll now operate as a change-of-pace back behind Bijan Robinson. The 2022 third-round pick soaked up 200-plus touches in each of his first three NFL seasons (all with Washington) prior to dipping to 100 touches in 2025. Robinson is a big back who can handle early-down and short-yardage work, but he's not much of a factor as a receiver (92 career targets). He's yet to post a top-20 fantasy campaign and he won't come close to that in 2026 unless Bijan Robinson suffers a major injury. The 27-year-old back is no more than a solid insurance stash.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Williams is set to miss another game as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is set to get the start again versus a Packers defense that gave up 148 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Caleb Williams' status is up in the air ahead of Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Williams has been sidelined since he injured his hamstring against Minnesota in Week 2, but he could be ready to return if he has a favorable practice week. If he plays, the starting quarterback will face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Williams will aim to build on a stellar return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Williams had no struggles in Week 6 against the Falcons in his first game since Week 2, completing 83 percent of passes for 305 yards and one touchdown. The third-year quarterback has now surpassed 250 passing yards in both games that he's played through this season, and the sky's the limit now. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Mayer led the Raiders in targets with seven in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, although he turned that volume into just six catches for 32 yards. That opportunity came as Brock Bowers was sidelined following minor knee surgery, and while the third-year star isn't expected to be out long, he has yet to be cleared for Week 2. If Mayer does get the start at tight end, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in points allowed to TEs last year, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Mayer hasn't made much of an impact as the Raiders' top tight end through the first two weeks of the season, catching nine of 11 targets for 55 yards without scoring a touchdown. That role has come while Brock Bowers was recovering from minor knee surgery at the end of training camp, but with Bowers expected to return in Week 3, Mayer will see even his modest volume collapse. If Bowers' 2026 debut does get delayed further, Mayer will still be facing a Saints defense that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Mayer's stint as the Raiders' starting TE ended in Week 3 with the return of Brock Bowers, but he stayed involved in a win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 32 yards and his first touchdown of the season. A lack of options at wide receiver could mean Klint Kubiak will continue to lean on both his tight ends for offense, keeping Mayer relevant even with Bowers as the clear No. 1 target for Kirk Cousins. Mayer could make a splash again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs so far, but which ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Mayer was busy in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, turning a season-high 10 targets into eight catches for 82 yards. The additional volume came after wide receiver Jalen Nailor left the game with a concussion, forcing Kirk Cousins to lean even more heavily on his tight end duo of Mayer and Brock Bowers to move the chains. Even with a healthy Bowers back in action the last two weeks, Mayer has delivered an 11-114-1 line on 13 targets. However, he'll struggle to maintain that pace in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Mayer's volume took a significant step backward in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots. After turning 10 targets into an 8-82-0 line in Week 4, Mayer got only one look from Kirk Cousins in New England, turning it into a two-yard gain. Brock Bowers is the unquestioned top option in the team's passing game, but a lack of established wide receivers has created an opening for Mayer to be more than just injury insurance. Through five games, he's delivered a 21-171-1 line on 25 targets, putting him on pace for career-best numbers in 2026. Mayer will face a Bills defense in Week 6 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Mayer took advantage of the extra defensive attention the Bills paid to Brock Bowers in Week 6, catching seven of nine targets for a season-high 95 yards. While Bowers remains the top option in the Raiders' passing attack, Mayer is on pace for a career-best year of his own, producing a 28-266-1 line on 34 targets through six games. He is eight receptions and 63 yards away from establishing new personal bests. Mayer will likely struggle to reach those marks in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 showdown against the Patriots. He caught both of his targets for 18 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 win over the Falcons. Washington and Pat Freiermuth were co-starters at TE, but the latter tallied five catches for 46 yards and a TD. New England's defense is very stingy against the position, as they rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (3.3) to tight ends.
outlooksByWeek.5: Darnell Washington and the Steelers host the Colts in a matchup between 2-2 teams in Week 5. In Week 4, he played 70% of offensive snaps and caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown. Fellow tight end Pat Freiermuth (3-17-1) was also productive, playing 75% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like they'll have a nearly even snap split as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel to square off against the 1-4 Buccaneers in Week 6. He played 34 snaps on offense (63%) en route to catching two of three targets for 12 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Fellow starting tight end Pat Freiermuth was on the field for 38 offensive snaps (70%) and was the more productive of the two, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two TDs. The playing time will continue to be relatively similar, making Washington a boom-or-bust fantasy option against Tampa Bay's 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.7) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darnell Washington and the Steelers are in Paris for an interconference tilt against the Saints in Week 7. He brought in four of six targets for 25 yards and a touchdown during Pittsburgh's thrilling comeback victory in overtime in Week 6. Washington and fellow tight end Pat Freiermuth each played 71% of the offensive snaps, lending more credibility to the "your turn, my turn" trend that's developing in 2026. He'll look to exploit New Orleans' 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.6) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Though he never quite made it onto the fantasy radar, Washington was one of the most fun, surprising "breakout" players of 2025. Essentially an extension of the offensive line at 6-foot-6, 264 pounds, Washington is known mainly for his blocking. Still, the 2023 third-round pick played well enough that he was stealing snaps and targets from both Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth. Washington never cleared six targets or 10.7 fantasy points in any game, but he was effective with the ball in his hands and averaged 8.5 yards per target. Though Smith has been released, Pittsburgh's offense is no longer being led by TE superfan Arthur Smith, which is likely to lead to a lesser role for Washington. Expect him to operate as a rarely targeted blocking complement to Freiermuth.

outlooksByWeek.2: KC Concepcion and the Browns are on the road in Week 2 to face the Buccaneers and their eighth-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed to WRs (101). The rookie looked hungry and fought for more on every play, catching four of five targets for 43 yards and rushing three times for 15 yards while losing a fumble. Concepcion's blunder came on a play from behind as he tried to gain extra yardage, but it was still a promising debut for the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, as he led the team in receptions and targets. Still, it's difficult to trust anyone on the Browns' offense, especially against a Tampa Bay defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 71 combined yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: KC Concepcion and the Browns return home in Week 3 to host the Panthers and their 18th-ranked passing defense. He finished Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with six catches on six targets for 28 yards and had one rush for minus-6 yards. Concepcion led the team in receptions but was last in average yards per touch at just 4.7. His general involvement on offense is a great sign, but it appears fellow rookie Denzel Boston is the Browns receiver to roster thanks to his big-play ability.
outlooksByWeek.4: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome Pittsburgh to town for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He caught just two of nine targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset victory in Week 3. Concepcion wasn't able to contribute much despite tying for the team lead in targets with Harold Fannin Jr., but it's still a positive sign that the Browns are looking to get the ball in his hands. He'll get his first chance to face the division-rival Steelers and their 14th-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed (403) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Jets for a Week 5 showdown. The rookie receiver finished second on the team in receptions (5) and yardage (64), while his eight targets led the way in Cleveland's Week 4 victory. Concepcion also returned two punts for 10 yards, as it remains clear the Browns want the ball in his hands in a variety of ways for him to shine as a playmaker. However, he'll face a talented Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome the division-rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He caught his lone target for five yards before leaving Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5 with a head injury after a hard hit. Concepcion has entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will have to be cleared by an independent neurologist before returning to the field. The promising rookie's status should be monitored leading up to a Week 6 showdown against Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Titans in Week 7. He hauled in four of six targets for 37 yards and rushed twice for two yards during Cleveland's 13-10 comeback win in Week 6. The rookie first-round pick led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and was second in yardage behind veteran Jerry Jeudy (69). Concepcion will look to deliver more, along with the entire Browns' offense, versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.
